structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development offers accessibility-related improvements to homes of seniors aged 55 and older. Improvements may include installation of grab bars and railings, widening of doorways, installation of ramps, accessible showers, and other modifications to help seniors remain in their homes and maintain independence.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Zero percent to 6% interest loans (based on income) with terms up to 30 years, or grants up to $25,000 to finance accessibility improvements. Loan amounts up to 110 percent of property value. Loans must be repaid upon sale, transfer, or refinance of property. All closing costs are included in the loan. Loans in excess of $5,000 or with deferred payments are secured by a mortgage. For families with incomes at or below 50 percent of the statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income, deferred payments may be available if necessary for project feasibility. Maximum total funding generally does not exceed $50,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Senior homeowners aged 55 and older who are Maryland residents
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Actual costs of making the house accessible or functional for residents, including widening doorways, installation of accessible showers, ramps, grab bars, lever handles, first-floor bathroom and laundry room additions (considered on case-by-case basis), chair lifts, handicap ramps, bars, railings, and doors.
requirements_list: Be Maryland residents with at least one resident age 55 or older
Must own and occupy the home as their principal residence (seniors living with relatives considered on case-by-case basis)
Home must be structurally sound and free of health and safety hazards
No outstanding federal or state tax liens, open bankruptcy, or foreclosure
Household income cannot exceed 80% of Statewide or Washington DC MSA median (see income limits document for specific thresholds based on household size)
Provide a work proposal for accessibility repairs from a licensed and insured Maryland contractor
Submit supporting documentation including proof of home ownership, photo ID, property tax bill, homeowners insurance declaration page, and bids from licensed contractors with required documentation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are available at local County Housing Offices or Maryland Access Point Agencies. Applicants should provide a work proposal for the accessibility repairs from a licensed and insured Maryland contractor, along with photos documenting the issues. Applicants must submit supporting documentation including proof of home ownership (deed and current mortgage statement or property tax bill), photo ID, homeowners insurance declaration page, and contractor bids with required documentation (MHIC or trade license, Certificate of Liability Insurance, Letter of Good Standing, and W-9). Completed applications can be submitted via email to DHCD.SLP_documentation@maryland.gov or mailed to: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA, Special Loan Programs, 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. Assistance with completing applications is available at agencies or through in-home appointments. Once submitted, the application is processed by the department and the applicant is contacted.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore Regional Neighborhood Initiative (BRNI) program demonstrates how strategic investment in local housing and businesses leads to healthy, sustainable communities with a growing tax base and enhanced quality of life. The program focuses on areas where modest investment and coordinated strategy will have appreciable neighborhood revitalization impact.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding for housing and business development projects in eligible neighborhoods, including down payment assistance, property acquisition and rehabilitation, energy efficiency improvements, mixed-use development, community infrastructure, workforce development, and strategic demolition.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community Development Organizations with an approved strategic neighborhood revitalization plan
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment assistance to attract home buyers; acquisition or rehabilitation of vacant or blighted properties; improvement of existing residential and business properties; energy efficiency through weatherization and energy retrofits; development of mixed-use projects combining housing, retail and office space; development or enhancement of community open space or public infrastructure; workforce and employment development programs; strategic demolition; operating costs for community enhancement projects

Must have an approved strategic neighborhood revitalization plan (can submit plan at time of application if not already approved)

Projects should capitalize on community strengths and be targeted in specific neighborhoods
Projects must be part of approved strategic neighborhood revitalization plan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Community Development Organizations should contact their Regional Project Manager for eligibility verification and application details. Organizations without an approved strategic neighborhood revitalization plan must submit one at the time of application; the plan must be approved by the Department prior to funding awards.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore Vacants Reinvestment Initiative provides capital to Baltimore City, Maryland Stadium Authority, and Baltimore City's community-based development organizations to successfully redevelop vacant properties. The program focuses on eliminating vacant properties and strengthening neighborhoods through renovation of vacant buildings on clusters of contiguous blocks, redevelopment of vacant lots for housing, mixed-use projects, and green space. The FY27 BVRI round seeks to expedite abatement of vacant properties—particularly vacant buildings with city-issued vacant building notices—increase occupied housing with emphasis on homeownership, stabilize and grow population and households, strengthen neighborhood housing values and homeownership wealth without displacement, leverage private sector capital for housing development finance, and achieve whole block outcomes where every property on a block has a productive use.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: FY27 BVRI funds are provided as partially forgivable subordinate loans from Maryland Community Investment Corporation (MCIC), with forgiveness based on Net Sale/Refinance Proceeds and project appraisal gap. Forms of financial assistance include: (1) Renovation and new construction loans or lines of credit to be repaid through home sales or refinance into permanent financing for rental projects; (2) Grant funds to fill the gap between total development costs and sale prices; and (3) Credit enhancement to leverage private capital. Funds may be used for: acquisition, stabilization, and renovation of vacant buildings (prioritizing those with city-issued vacant building notices); acquisition and aggregation of vacant lots for new infill housing construction, mixed-use projects, and community-managed open space; urgent demolition of properties that pose community health risks or further near-term redevelopment projects; and predevelopment activities including architectural, engineering, site infrastructure, and site development for renovation and new construction projects.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 1, 2026 at 11:59 PM
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community development organizations (CDOs) and nonprofit organizations with a track record of completing the rehabilitation of vacant property and/or infill new construction projects that operate for the purpose of improving the physical, economic, or social environment of their geographic areas of operation in Baltimore City. Also includes public and nonprofit partners in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition, stabilization, and renovation of vacant buildings (prioritizing those with city-issued vacant building notices); acquisition and aggregation of vacant lots for new infill housing construction, mixed-use projects, and community-managed open space; urgent demolition of vacant buildings for community health or near-term redevelopment purposes; architectural and engineering work; site infrastructure and site development; and predevelopment activities for renovation and new construction projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Sustainable Community Areas in Baltimore City, with special consideration for projects in the Baltimore City Vacancy Reduction Priority Geographies, which includes Impact Investment Areas. Target areas should include contiguous clusters of whole blocks where the applicant can directly abate or facilitate the abatement of all vacant property, particularly buildings with Vacant Building Notices.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a community development organization (CDO) or nonprofit organization with a track record of completing rehabilitation of vacant property and/or infill new construction projects
Projects must be located in Sustainable Community Areas in Baltimore City
All projects should be located in a cluster of contiguous blocks where the applicant can demonstrate capacity and a plan to address all vacant property over time
Awarded funds will primarily support activities that accelerate remediation of vacant buildings with city-issued Vacant Building Notices
Target area should be part of applicant's existing service area
Target area should include approximately 5 blocks by 5 blocks that is walkable
Applicants must submit complete applications with all required documents including property pipeline spreadsheet and partner letters
If funded, may be required to provide government resolution, corporate board resolution, and charitable registration

Required organization documents: By-Laws, Articles of Incorporation, Current Board Roster, Annual Report, IRS Letter of Determination, Financial Audit, Operating Budget, Profit & Loss Statement, Balance Sheet, and Public Disclosure Authorization
Applications without completed property spreadsheets and missing partner letters and other required information will not be considered for funding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted exclusively through Survey123 platform (no paper applications accepted). The application includes branching logic and requires submission of: (1) Organization information and documents (By-Laws, Articles of Incorporation, Board Roster, Annual Report, IRS Letter of Determination, Financial Audit, Operating Budget, Profit & Loss Statement, Balance Sheet, Public Disclosure Authorization); (2) Target area identification and map; (3) Vacancy reduction strategy narrative addressing community strengths, assets, and whole block outcomes; (4) Completed vacant property pipeline spreadsheet listing all properties expected to be redeveloped with FY27 BVRI funding; (5) Project-specific information for residential rehabilitation, infill construction, modular infill, green space/placemaking, and/or mixed-use projects as applicable; (6) Sources & Uses budgets; (7) Letters of support from development partners; (8) Evidence of site control where applicable; and (9) Sales/leasing strategies. Applications are scored on: Organization Experience and Development Capacity (30 points), Whole-Block Redevelopment Strategy and Program Alignment (30 points), Vacant Property Pipeline and Production Readiness (25 points), and Budget and Financing (15 points). Projects in ENOUGH and Just Communities areas receive up to 10 bonus points each. Applicants may be contacted for follow-up discussions and site visits during review. All projects receiving funding are subject to Maryland Historical Trust Act requirements. Register as a new user in the Project Portal, upload required organizational documents to profile, and submit application through the portal.

structured_extraction.program_name: BeSMART Energy Efficiency Loan for Homeowners
structured_extraction.program_description: The BeSMART Home Loan Program provides financing to improve the energy efficiency and comfort of your home by replacing and upgrading appliances, heating, ventilation and cooling systems, and whole house envelope improvements so homeowners can save on utility bills.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $30,000 in unsecured financing for energy efficiency measures at 6.99% APR. Loan term is flexible and can be chosen by borrower (up to 10 years maximum). Minimum loan amount is $5,000. There are no pre-payment penalties, and borrowers can avoid interest by paying off the loan early. For solar photovoltaic projects, borrowers can finance up to 50% of their total loan amount for solar panels and storage systems. For health and safety costs related to energy improvements (such as mold remediation or radon mitigation), up to 25% of the total loan can be allocated to these purposes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners seeking to improve energy efficiency and comfort in their homes
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financing for energy efficiency improvements including insulation and air sealing, ENERGY STAR® heating and cooling systems, ENERGY STAR® hot water heating equipment, ENERGY STAR® appliances (note: no Energy Star compliant stoves, ovens, or microwave ovens), windows, doors, lighting and controls, programmable and smart thermostats, ceiling fans and ventilation fans, geothermal heat pumps, solar photovoltaic (capped at 50% of total loan amount), health and safety costs related to energy improvements including mold remediation and radon mitigation (up to 25% of total loan amount), and other improvements identified in a certified energy audit.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland homeowner
Credit score of 640 or greater
Debt to income ratio does not exceed 50%
Unsecured loan based on verification of credit and ability to pay
Minimum loan amount is $5,000
Work cannot have been started or purchases made prior to receiving BeSMART funding (re-financing is prohibited)
Contractor must be licensed and insured in Maryland (if applicable)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online BeSMART Loan Application and provide Driver's License, 30 days of pay stubs, and recent mortgage statement. The applicant will receive a DocuSign to privately submit Social Security number and authorize a credit report. Provide contractor estimate or retailer proposal for desired improvements. DHCD will send loan documents for signature and return. Upon execution, applicant receives a 30% down payment 2-party check (payable to applicant and contractor, or 1-party check to applicant for retail purchases). Complete the project with contractor. Both applicant and contractor sign Certificates of Completion. DHCD sends the remaining 70% 2-party check. Loan payments then begin. Borrower can choose loan term (flexible payback period, up to 10 years maximum).

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) through the Neighborhood BusinessWorks (NBW) program offers microgrants ranging from $20,000 to $50,000 to support for-profit small businesses seeking capital for growth and expansion opportunities within Sustainable Communities areas. The program provides grant funding to assist early-stage businesses in growing and expanding their operations.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Microgrants ranging from $20,000 to $50,000 based on organization's annual operating budget and subject to financial review. Total available funding is up to $2,000,000. Businesses must provide a matching contribution equal to or greater than the grant request amount. For example, if awarded a $50,000 grant, the business must contribute $50,000 of their own funds to the project. Funds can be used towards capital and operating expenses that support revenue growth from September 23, 2024, to March 23, 2025, including salary, rent, utilities, product advertising, product development, commercial real estate acquisition, and professional services. Only new expenses are eligible; existing expenses such as current rent and payroll are not eligible.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application round closed as of October 14, 2024, at 5 PM EST
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit small businesses in Sustainable Communities areas with greater than 2 and 50 or fewer full-time equivalent employees (as of September 23, 2024) and annual revenue between $50,000 and $1 million.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital and operating expenses that support revenue growth from September 23, 2024, to March 23, 2025. Eligible expenses include salary, rent, utilities, product advertising, product development, commercial real estate acquisition, professional services, increased rent and payroll for hiring new employees, new equipment, and marketing. Only new expenses are eligible; existing expenses such as current rent and payroll are not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located in a Sustainable Communities area in Maryland. Use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper at https://portal.dhcd.state.md.us/GIS/revitalize/index.html to verify eligibility by entering your business address in the incentive look-up tool.
requirements_list: Be a for-profit business
Be located in a Sustainable Communities area in Maryland
Have a matching contribution equal to or greater than the grant request amount
Have greater than 2 employees and 50 or fewer employees (full-time equivalent) as of September 23, 2024
Have an annual revenue of at least $50,000 but no more than $1 million
Be in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Be in good financial and legal standing with no past due amounts, liens, or judgments
Not be a professional services or sales-based business (Insurance, Accounting, Real Estate, Legal, Finance, etc.)

Not be a non-profit organization, cannabis-based business, pawn shop, gun shop, massage parlor, adult entertainment facility, rental real estate business, tanning salon, check-cashing facility, gambling facility, tattoo parlor, or liquor store
Not be a previous award winner of an NBW Opportunity Zone grant or NBW Business Boost grant
Full-time equivalent (FTE) calculation includes regular employees (W2s) and contractual staff (1099s)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted online through the DHCD application portal at https://apps.dhcd.state.md.us/NBWOZGrant/account/login. Applicants must create an account and provide required documentation including Articles of Organization, business bylaws, most recent annual tax return (Tax Year 2023), financial statements as of August 31, 2024, screenshot showing eligible location, proof of matching funds, Certificate of Good Standing from SDAT, and signed IRS W-9 form. Only fully completed applications will be considered for funding. Incomplete applications will be returned and processed when resources are available. The business name on the application, W-9, and SDAT certificate must EXACTLY match. Applications are evaluated based on meeting eligibility requirements and business financials. Priority funding is determined by: (1) business location, (2) impact of expansion including new employees to be hired, capital investment, and additional square footage, and (3) presentation of business financials and supporting documents. Additional priority impact attributes include: innovative businesses driving innovation or technology advancements, businesses growing in new industries, businesses focused on regional strengths, businesses leveraging partnerships with educational institutions, and Minority Business Enterprises (MBE). Award announcements will be made on a rolling basis during December 2024 to January 2025. Grant funds are expected to be paid in the February-March 2025 timeframe. DHCD will initiate the local resolution approval process with the applicant's governing executive body. Award recipients must submit a final report by March 31, 2026, detailing how funds were used with supporting documents and receipts. Awardees will be contacted nine months after receiving grant funds to complete a questionnaire and provide a one-page summary of the grant's use and impact on their business and community.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Development Block Grant Disaster Recovery Assistance - Hurricane Sandy
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal disaster recovery funding awarded to Maryland through the Community Development Block Grant Program in response to Hurricane Sandy (October 2012). The State of Maryland received a total of $28.64 million from Congress through the Disaster Relief Appropriations Act of 2013, with funds allocated to recovery activities in Somerset County and other eligible areas. Disaster Grant #1 allocated $8.64 million specifically to Somerset County (the most impacted and distressed county in the state). Disaster Grant #2 allocated $20 million for housing and economic recovery activities related to Hurricane Sandy and other eligible storm events. The program was managed by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) through its Community Development Block Grant Office.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Disaster Grant #1: $8.64 million in Community Development Block Grant funding for disaster recovery activities in Somerset County, including housing recovery (rehabilitation and replacement for low and moderate income homeowners), economic recovery (business grants and loans), public infrastructure improvements, and state administrative costs. Grant #1 was distributed across 5 phases with specific allocations: Phase 1 ($4.4M for housing, economic development, and administration), Phase 2 ($1.1M for planning and Housing Authority rental improvements), Phase 3 ($3.14M for housing, economic recovery, public services/job training, and administration). Disaster Grant #2: $20 million allocated across multiple phases for housing, economic recovery, and public infrastructure activities. Funds were provided as grants, deferred loans repayable upon sale or transfer of property, and support for business loans and grants. All funds were to be used for necessary expenses related to disaster relief, long-term recovery, restoration of infrastructure and housing, and economic revitalization. Maximum household income eligibility: 80% of area median income for Somerset County. Activities included: housing rehabilitation and replacement, business grants and loans, broadband extension and studies, infrastructure improvements (dredging, generators, well facilities), housing studies, and job training programs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: October 1, 2022 (modified deadline for expenditure of remaining funds)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, non-profits, government entities, businesses, and public housing authorities in Somerset County affected by Hurricane Sandy. Eligible applicants must be low and moderate income persons/families (household income not exceeding 80% of area median income for Somerset County). Specific eligible populations include homeowners with damaged properties, renters, business owners, watermen, public housing residents, and service organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Recovery activities from Hurricane Sandy disaster including: housing rehabilitation and replacement for low and moderate income homeowners; housing rental assistance for public housing authorities; business grants and loans for economic recovery; job training and workforce development; public infrastructure improvements (dredging, water facilities, broadband extension); planning and studies (housing needs assessments, economic opportunities analysis, broadband infrastructure studies); emergency notification systems; and state administrative costs. Funds may be provided as grants or deferred loans repayable upon sale or transfer of property.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Somerset County, Maryland (the most impacted and distressed county from Hurricane Sandy). Some phases of Disaster Grant #2 also included limited activities in Allegany, Charles, Dorchester, and Garrett counties.
requirements_list: Household income does not exceed 80% of area median income for Somerset County (as determined by HUD)
Proof of storm damage from Hurricane Sandy
Proof of homeownership or business ownership (as applicable)
No duplication of benefits - applicants cannot receive assistance from multiple federal sources for the same unmet need
Housing units must be brought up to livability code and meet current floodplain requirements
Homebuyers must obtain fixed-rate mortgages for minimum 30 years (not subprime or adjustable rate mortgages)
For house sales under disposition program: homebuyers must obtain minimum 8 hours of housing counseling from HUD-approved housing counseling agency
Public housing authorities must carry flood insurance in perpetuity
All applications processed on first come/first served basis regardless of race, national origin, or other protected class
Applicants must submit information related to household income for verification
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications were submitted through Somerset County or relevant local entities (Housing Authority of Crisfield, Economic Development Commission, etc.) depending on the specific activity. The County was responsible for procurement, payment, inspections, and approval of work. For housing rehabilitation/replacement, applicants submitted applications documenting storm damage, income verification, and property ownership. For public house disposition, the County initiated a public process with a public notice describing the selection and sale process, property appraisals to determine fair market prices, and income qualification of homebuyers using PART 5 income calculation process. For business loans/grants, applications were reviewed by the Somerset County Economic Development Commission. The County worked with consultants and state agencies to implement specific activities. Public hearings were held to discuss proposed activities and amendments to the Action Plan.

structured_extraction.program_description: Funds help strengthen Maryland's communities by expanding affordable housing opportunities, creating jobs, stabilizing neighborhoods and improving the overall quality of life. The program funds community development projects, public facilities, and economic development initiatives that benefit persons of low and moderate income, eliminate slum and blight, or meet urgent community needs.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal funds distributed by the State to non-entitlement counties, small cities, and towns for community development projects. Over a designated three-year period, the state must cumulatively use 70% of its allocation to benefit persons of low and moderate income. The State has received $7,416,560 for State Fiscal Year 2026, distributed as follows: Community Development (82% - $100,000) = $6,000,000; Special Projects (15%) = $1,094,064; State Administration (2% + $100,000) = $248,331; Technical Assistance (1%) = $74,165. Funds are awarded as gap funding for projects selected by jurisdictions. Community Development projects are funded through an annual competitive process. Special Projects are funded on a "first come, first serve" basis.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Community Development applications accepted once each year through a competitive process. Special Projects and Planning applications can be submitted at any time throughout the year after written approval is received.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Units of general local government in non-entitlement counties with populations under 200,000 and non-entitlement cities and towns with populations under 50,000. Also eligible are community-based development organizations (CBDOs), community housing development organizations (CHDOs), non-profit organizations serving low and moderate income persons, and for-profit businesses for economic development projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing (single family rehabilitation, new rental construction, acquisition and renovation and resale, downpayment assistance for homebuyers), public facilities (water/sewer systems, streets, sidewalks, flood and drainage improvements, childcare facilities, senior and community centers, shelters), economic development projects (infrastructure to support businesses, extension of utilities, building improvements, acquisition of equipment), and planning. All funded projects must meet one of three national objectives: benefit persons of low and moderate income, eliminate slum and blight, or meet an urgent need of recent origin that threatens public health and safety.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Non-entitlement counties with populations under 200,000 and non-entitlement cities and towns with populations under 50,000. Not eligible: Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, and Prince George's counties; Annapolis, Baltimore, Bowie, Cumberland, Frederick, Gaithersburg, Hagerstown, and Salisbury cities. Projects must be located in a Maryland Priority Funding Area, except for public services; single family housing rehabilitation; acquisition, renovation and sale of existing houses; downpayment assistance; or where the Secretary of DHCD determines that the project is necessary to protect public health, to alleviate personal economic hardship in an emergency situation, to promote economically integrated housing, is consistent with an overall economic development strategy, or where an exception is necessary.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an eligible non-entitlement jurisdiction (county with population less than 200,000 excluding HUD entitlement cities, or city/town with population under 50,000)
Proposed activities must be eligible under Title I of the Housing and Community Development Act of 1974
Proposed project must meet at least one national objective: benefit low and moderate income persons, eliminate slum and blight, or meet urgent community needs
Proposed subrecipient or business must be eligible
If subrecipient or for-profit business involved, grantee must conduct risk analysis to review financial and administrative capacity
Eligible non-profits must have organizational by-laws and mission statements clearly stating they primarily serve low and moderate income persons or eligible populations
For-profit businesses must be in Good Standing in the State of Maryland for economic development projects
Community Development Block Grant funds must comply with Uniform Relocation Assistance and Real Property Acquisition Policies Act of 1970 if property acquisition or displacement occurs
Environmental Review must be completed prior to initiation of project activities under National Environmental Policy Act of 1969
Projects must comply with Fair Housing and Equal Opportunity requirements and non-discrimination laws
For construction projects with $200,000 or more in HUD funding, Section 3 requirements apply (25% of labor hours from Section 3 workers, minimum 5% from Targeted Section 3 Workers)
Multi-family rental housing and certain facilities must include generators with capacity to power at a minimum lighting in common areas
Housing rehabilitation programs have maximum grant of $40,000 per house (no maximum loan amount)
Housing acquisition, renovation and resale maximum CDBG funds per house is $200,000
Housing construction or substantial rehabilitation with more than 4 rental units requires broadband infrastructure installation
Rental properties must be affordable with rents not exceeding Fair Market Rents established annually by HUD
Affordability terms for housing range from 10-20 years after occupancy depending on funding amount
Homeownership assistance requires lien placement on property for 5-10 years depending on assistance amount
Homeownership requires fixed-rate mortgages for minimum 30 years, no subprime or adjustable rate mortgages, and minimum 8 hours HUD-approved housing counseling

For infrastructure projects over $250,000 or housing rehabilitation over $250,000 per house, Build America, Buy America (BABA) requirements apply requiring domestic procurement of iron, steel, and manufactured products
If grantee spends more than $750,000 of federal funds in fiscal year, Single Audit required
Grantees must maintain written Conflict of Interest Policy
All procurement must allow for full and open competition

Professional services under $15,000 require written estimates from at least three vendors; $15,001-$50,000 require written estimates from three vendors; over $50,000 require competitive Request for Proposal with formal newspaper advertising
Construction under $2,000 requires estimates from three vendors; $2,001-$50,000 allows grantee options for advertising; over $50,000 requires formal newspaper advertising
Housing rehabilitation and renovation require competitive Request for Proposal with formal advertising or use of established qualified contractor list
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The State notifies eligible localities of fund availability and conducts training sessions on application development. For Community Development category: Applications are accepted once each year through a competitive process. Grantees must submit applications with required documentation including citizen participation plan, public hearing notice, local resolution, residential anti-displacement and relocation assistance plan, program income re-use plan, and certifications. Applications are rated and awarded through a competitive selection process. For Special Projects and Planning categories: Applications can be submitted at any time throughout the year after written approval is received from CDBG program staff. Applicants seeking funds for projects meeting the national objective of urgent need must contact CDBG staff to determine if their proposed project qualifies. If approved, supplemental pages are provided for completion. All applications must include eligible activities and demonstrate compliance with national objectives and eligibility requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: Community Investment Tax Credits support 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations by awarding allocations of State tax credits for use as incentives to attract contributions from individuals and businesses to benefit local projects and services. The program has leveraged nearly $27 million in charitable contributions to approximately 700 projects across the State.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The CITC program awards Maryland state income tax credits to incentivize donations to nonprofit organizations and their approved projects. For the FY26 round, a total of $1.75M in tax credits will be awarded, with a maximum request of $50,000 per applicant. Businesses and individuals that donate $500 or more to a qualified organization's approved project(s) can earn tax credits equal to 50% of the value of the money, goods or real property contribution. Organizations that receive an award must raise double the amount of tax credits requested (e.g., $50,000 in credits requires $100,000 in donations raised). Awardees electronically submit gift documentation to permit issuance of tax credits in the donor's name. These tax credits are in addition to the deductions on both Federal and State taxes as a result of the charitable contribution. Tax credits must be used against taxes owed for the year in which the contribution was made. All CITC award contracts have a 24-month life. For the FY26 award, the contract period begins on January 1, 2026, and ends on December 31, 2027.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 19, 2025 at 5:00 PM (EDT)
structured_extraction.program_audience: IRS designated 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations that are in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT), registered as a charity with the Office of the Secretary of State, and located in or serve residents of a Priority Funding Area (PFA). Businesses and individuals that make contributions of $500 or more are eligible to receive tax credits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects can be capital and/or operating and typically involve activities such as: Education and Youth Services, Housing and Community Development, Job and Self-Sufficiency Training, Enhancing Neighborhoods and Business Districts, Arts, Culture and Historic Preservation, Economic Development and Tourism Promotion, Technical Assistance and Capacity Building, and Services for At-Risk Populations. Budget line items may include staff costs, rent, utilities, program supplies, training, travel, construction "soft costs" such as planning, design, engineering, permitting, and direct construction expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in or serve residents of a Priority Funding Area (PFA). For capital projects, the project site must be located within a PFA boundary. For operating projects, the organization may be eligible if clients served reside within the boundary of a Priority Funding Area, with documented evidence of client residence addresses.
requirements_list: Applicants must be IRS designated 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations
Must be in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Must be a registered charity with the Office of the Secretary of State or hold a religious exemption letter
Projects must be located in or serve residents of a Priority Funding Area (PFA)
Donors must make contributions of $500 or more to be eligible for tax credits
Donors must obtain a Donor Acknowledgement Form from the nonprofit
Tax credits must be used against taxes owed for the year in which the contribution was made
Organizations must raise double the amount of tax credits requested during the 24-month award period
For capital projects, applicant must document site control with deed, lease, title/real estate settlement documents, or similar evidence
Priority consideration given to projects in ENOUGH areas, Just Communities, housing production, wealth building initiatives, and vacant property elimination
Applicant must be registered in the DHCD IGX Project Portal with complete organization records before submitting application

All required legal documents (Articles of Incorporation, Bylaws, IRS 501(c)(3) letter, Board list, Charitable Registration Letter, SDAT Good Standing status, Corporate Resolution, and Priority Funding Area maps) must be uploaded in PDF format
Applicant must provide Priority Funding Area (PFA) maps for every address where project work will occur or services will be delivered
Applicants with prior active awards from FY23 or FY24 may apply for new or different projects only
Organization must maintain annual charitable registration and good standing status throughout the award period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The FY26 CITC application round opens on May 19, 2025, and closes on June 19, 2025, at 5:00 PM. 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations apply through the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's IGX Project Portal. Applicants must first register as a user in the Project Portal (registration requests may take up to 72 hours to be approved) and complete and update their organization records and required legal document uploads before creating an application. The application must be completed and submitted entirely online through the Project Portal; only online submissions are accepted. Applications must include a project description, tasks and timeline table covering the entire 24-month award period, budget table and narrative covering all 24 months, Priority Funding Area (PFA) maps for all project locations, and all required legal and organizational documents in PDF format. For capital projects, site control documentation must be provided. Award decisions will be announced in Fall 2025. Once awarded, awardees may begin accepting donations and offering tax credits to donors starting January 1, 2026. Awardees must submit electronic Tax Credit Certification Requests within 30 days of receiving each donation and submit four semi-annual reports during the two-year award period (due July 10 and January 10).

structured_extraction.program_description: CSRAP is a state-funded rental assistance initiative that supports housing stability for families with children enrolled in Maryland community schools. The program provides emergency financial assistance to households at risk of eviction, losing housing, or experiencing homelessness.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides financial assistance for: (1) past due rent or utility bills, including late fees and court fees related to eviction; (2) moving costs and deposits needed to rent new homes, such as security deposits, application fees, first month's rent, and utility deposits; (3) up to 3 months of prospective (future) rent and/or utility assistance at a time. The maximum length of assistance a household can receive is 15 months. Assistance is provided based on need and availability of funds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families and students enrolled in community schools in participating jurisdictions who are experiencing housing instability or homelessness.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Past due rent or utility bills (including water) with associated late fees and court fees related to eviction; moving costs and deposits for new rental homes such as security deposits, application fees, first month's rent, and utility deposits; up to 3 months of prospective rent and/or utility assistance for housing stability.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program operates in Anne Arundel County, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Frederick County, Montgomery County, Prince George's County, Washington County, and Wicomico County. Assistance can only be provided to households that have a student enrolled in a community school in the county where they are requesting assistance.
requirements_list: At least one student in the household must be enrolled in a community school in a participating jurisdiction
Household must be experiencing homelessness or at risk of housing instability (such as a past due utility or rent notice, eviction notice, or unsafe/unhealthy living conditions)
Household must be responsible for paying rent or utilities in a qualifying rental unit
Be renting your home or trying to rent a new home (homeowners are not eligible)
Proof of citizenship is not required; eligibility is based on renter status and community school enrollment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications can be obtained from the local nonprofit agency supporting your county. Links to those agencies are available on DHCD's website. If you are unable to complete the application online, you can request a paper copy from the agency. Required documents include: proof of student's community school enrollment, proof of rental agreement, and invoice or proof of missed rent or utility payments.

structured_extraction.program_description: Through a statewide network of seventeen Community Action Agencies in Maryland, this program supports a range of direct services designed to assist low-income individuals and families with achieving self-sufficiency. Services address the causes and conditions of poverty and help families and individuals move toward self-sufficiency.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Congress annually appropriates funds administered at the state level. Community Action Agencies receive 90 percent of funds allocated to Maryland to operate programs and services. For FFY 2025-2026, eligible entities are allocated 93% of total CSBG funds based on a Base + Formula allocation method using FFY20 as the base, adjusted annually based on poverty, unemployment, and whether the agency serves a rural community. Poverty and unemployment data are updated every two years. The state may utilize up to 5 percent as discretionary funding to support activities and programs by Community Action Agencies or other non-profit organizations to eliminate poverty, promote self-sufficiency, and stimulate community revitalization, including training and technical assistance and coordination among agencies. Remaining funds support state administration and other approved uses.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The FY25 application round is closed. Check this page for information about future funding rounds.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Angela Fraser, Assistant Director, Division of Homeless Solutions
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income individuals and families with incomes at or below 200% of the federal poverty guidelines. Community Action Agencies that serve as designated eligible entities under the CSBG Act.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Direct services to assist low-income individuals and families achieve self-sufficiency, addressing causes and conditions of poverty. Eligible uses include training and technical assistance, community revitalization activities, coordination among Community Action Agencies, and support for activities and programs by Community Action Agencies or other non-profit organizations to eliminate poverty and promote self-sufficiency.

Additional discretionary funding applications are available through periodic funding rounds announced on the program website. structured_extraction.program_name: EmPOWER Low Income Energy Efficiency Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A low-income energy efficiency program delivered through a statewide network of local service providers. The program provides comprehensive energy efficiency services to eligible low-income households including energy conservation measures, weatherization services, and equipment maintenance. Service providers include nonprofits, local governments, and for-profit home improvement contractors. The program is administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) and includes multiple components: Whole Home Efficiency (core program), MEEHA - Multifamily Energy Efficiency and Housing Affordability Program (core program), Base Efficiency, Maryland Energy Efficiency Tune-up (MEET), and Energy Kits.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides comprehensive energy efficiency improvements at no cost to eligible low-income households. Benefits are delivered through qualified contracted service providers or through direct grants/loans to property owners. Measures include energy conservation materials, weatherization services, HVAC equipment, water heaters, lighting, appliances, air sealing, insulation, and domestic hot water improvements. The program requires certified building science professionals to determine cost-effective packages of energy-efficient improvements. Whole Home Efficiency and MEEHA programs deliver comprehensive improvements to both rental and owner-occupied homes as well as multifamily properties. Base Efficiency offers limited measures to households that do not qualify for comprehensive services. The MEET program provides equipment maintenance and tune-up services for clients who received services within the prior 5 years. Energy kits provide direct-install measures and immediate savings to new applicants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income households at or below 250% of the Federal Poverty Level and eligible service providers. Priority service to elderly persons (60+), families with children, persons with disabilities, high residential energy users, and households with high energy burden. Serves both renters and homeowners.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency improvements and weatherization services for low-income households including but not limited to: air sealing, insulation, HVAC equipment replacement (including heat pumps), water heater replacement, lighting upgrades, appliances, domestic hot water system improvements, fuel switching and electrification measures, duct sealing and insulation, window and door repairs or replacement, radon mitigation, and moisture management. Services also include equipment maintenance and tune-up for existing installations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide through all 23 counties and Baltimore City. Service is available to electrically heated or cooled clients of BGE, PE, Pepco, Delmarva, SMECO, and WGL with qualifying incomes.
requirements_list: Income at or below 250% of Federal Poverty Level
Electrically heated or cooled customers of participating utilities (BGE, PE, Pepco, Delmarva, SMECO, WGL)
Eligible building types: single-family homes, manufactured homes, apartments, and multifamily properties
Homeownership verification for owner-occupied units; landlord participation for rental properties
Income documentation required
Re-certification required if application is more than 12 months old before work begins
For multifamily projects: pre-approval process and income verification of tenants
BPI-certified energy auditor assessment required
Participants must not have received services from same funding source within certain lock-out periods (varies by funding source)
Properties must pass health and safety assessment or defer to Base Efficiency program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible households apply through their Local Weatherization Agency (LWA) or directly to DHCD. Application process includes: (1) Client intake and eligibility determination including income verification and occupancy status; (2) Energy assessment by BPI-certified professional to determine work scope; (3) Job classification into appropriate program tier (Whole Home Efficiency, Base Efficiency, MEEHA, etc.); (4) Work scope development with qualified contractor; (5) Quality Control inspection by contractor upon completion; (6) Quality Assurance inspection by DHCD staff on sample of jobs; (7) Invoice processing and payment to contractor. Lead-safe weatherization protocols required for homes built before 1978. Referral partnerships available through DHS, MES, MEA, and MDH. Energy kits sent to new individual applicants to provide immediate savings and demonstrate program benefits before comprehensive assessment.

The Maryland Housing Rehabilitation Program component is available to homeowners only; funding requests should not exceed $50,000 with a maximum initial deposit of 33% of total project cost.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Limited income homeowners and renters with utility accounts from participating companies. Applicants must have power to the home.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency improvements such as insulation in attic, floors and walls, hot water system improvements, lighting retrofits, furnace cleaning and safety repairs, refrigerator retrofit, and health and safety items. For homeowners applying for supplemental funding, also includes critical repairs such as structural, electrical, water leaks, lead, asbestos, and other general repairs to primary residence.

requirements_list: Household income must be at or below 250% Federal Poverty Level based on household size
Must have an active utility account with one of six participating companies: BGE, Delmarva Power, FirstEnergy, Pepco, SMECO, or Washington Gas
Must have power to the home

Automatically income-eligible if currently receiving benefits from Utility Bill Pay Assistance (OHEP), SNAP, TANF, SSI, HUD housing assistance, Fuel Fund Assistance, DHCD Rehab Programs, Baltimore Lead Hazard Control Program, Medicaid, MEA Energy Equity Grant, or MEEHA

For Quick Application (energy efficiency only): Must submit Client Information, Household Income Information, Energy Consent Form, and copy of most recent electric utility bill, plus copy of benefit approval notice if checking benefit programs

For Standard Application: Must submit Client Information, Household Information, Energy Consent Form, copy of most recent electric utility bill, proof of last 30 days GROSS household income, copy of Social Security card(s) for all household members, copy of Photo ID for applicant, and Zero Income Form for any household member 18+ claiming no income
For mobile home residents: Must provide copy of title or bill of sale to prove ownership

For homeowners applying for supplemental funding (critical repairs): Must provide Supplemental Financial Information (Page 6), Tax Affidavit (Page 7), Credit Pull Consent (Page 8), and complete MHRP Application Checklist including deed, current mortgage statement, property tax bill, homeowners insurance declaration page, flood insurance policy if applicable, and licensed contractor bids not exceeding $50,000 with bids no older than 60 days
Contractors must provide current MHIC license or trade license, Certificate of Liability Insurance (minimum $1M per occurrence), Letter of Good Standing, and completed W-9 form
For documented medical conditions requiring heating, cooling, or water heating: Physician's letter required
If person on deed is not on application: Must provide copy of their license or mail documenting different address; if deceased, copy of death certificate required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants have two options: (1) Quick Application for energy efficiency programs only—complete pre-application or submit paper application with basic documentation (Client Information, Household Income Information, Energy Consent Form, recent electric bill, and benefit approval notice if applicable). (2) Standard Application for all programs including heating or cooling crisis—submit more extensive documentation including income verification, Social Security cards, Photo ID, and Zero Income Form if applicable. For all applicants: Local agency will review application for completeness. If approved, local agency schedules energy audit, discusses results with applicant, schedules contractor for recommended work, and conducts post-improvement evaluation. For homeowners seeking supplemental funding for critical repairs: Submit standard application plus supplemental financial documentation and contractor bids. Incomplete applications and those missing documentation cannot be processed until complete. Mailing address for submission: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, Attn: Weatherization, 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706.

structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides an interest-bearing escrow account for all FSS participants. As employment wages increase, rent adjustments result in monthly deposits to the escrow account. Participants who successfully complete the program receive all funds in the escrow account plus interest. The contract period is 5 years, extendable for up to 2 additional years with good cause. Participants can graduate early if they complete all goals before the allotted time. Support includes financial literacy, job training, childcare, employment counseling, health services, homeownership guidance, job retention, and transportation assistance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Housing Voucher participants
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Escrow account funds can be used for homeownership down payments, vehicle repair, testing fees, and other purposes once the contract is completed. Participants can also request early access to escrow funds in urgent situations or to pursue self-sufficiency goals.

Head of household signs Contract of Participation
Complete Needs Assessment with program coordinator
Set realistic and achievable goals for self-sufficiency
Maintain suitable employment to complete contract
Be free of TANF (Temporary Assistance for Needy Families) benefits or achieve 30% of adjusted income exceeding HUD fair market rent for household

Eligible if receiving assistance under Housing Voucher programs
