structured_extraction.program_name: Federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credit Program (LIHTC)
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal tax credit program created by the Tax Reform Act of 1986 to encourage private sector investment in the construction and rehabilitation of housing for low- and moderate-income families. Tax credits are awarded on a competitive basis to nonprofit and for-profit sponsors of eligible housing projects based on criteria in the State's Qualified Allocation Plan.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credits are awarded based on a percentage of the qualified basis of each qualified low-income rental housing building. The applicable percentage is determined by the IRS annually. Project sponsors or their investor partners claim the tax credit on their federal income tax return. Tax credits provide approximately 30-40% of the qualified basis of a project, which equals the equity that sponsors/investors receive. Credits are allocated through a competitive process and are awarded to buildings that are placed in service during the applicable year or the two preceding years. The credit may be claimed over a 10-year period beginning in the year the building is placed in service. LIHTC with a present value equal to either 70% or 30% of the qualified basis of the building are provided in equal annual installments over a 10-year period. New construction and rehabilitation projects that are not federally subsidized are eligible for the 70% present value LIHTC. Projects financed with federally tax-exempt bonds, or which involve the acquisition of existing buildings (when combined with eligible rehabilitation) are eligible for the 30% present value LIHTC. Project owners must select one of three set-aside elections: (1) at least 20% of units for households at or below 50% of area median gross income (20@50 Set-Aside); (2) at least 40% of units for households at or below 60% of area median gross income (40@60 Set-Aside); or (3) at least 40% of units for households at or below 80% of area median gross income with average income not exceeding 60% of area median gross income (Income Averaging Set-Aside). Rents for LIHTC units may not exceed 30% of the applicable income limit. Housing units must be set aside for low-income residents for a compliance period of 15 years (Initial Compliance Period), plus an additional period of at least 15 years (Extended Use Period).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Determined annually by State; applications solicited in one round per year per Public Notice
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit and nonprofit sponsors of eligible housing projects and project owners developing or rehabilitating low-income rental housing. 10% of annual allocation is reserved for nonprofit sponsors. Project owners and management agents administering tax credit properties during both the initial compliance period (15 years) and extended use period (minimum 15 additional years).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction, rehabilitation, substantial renovation, acquisition combined with eligible rehabilitation, and adaptive reuse of residential rental buildings for low- and moderate-income families. Buildings must remain in compliance for a minimum of 40 years (15-year compliance period plus minimum 15-year extended use period) and provide either 20 percent of units to households earning 50 percent or less of area median income, or 40 percent of units to households earning 60 percent or less of area median income. Tax credits must support projects that meet income and rent restrictions for low- and moderate-income households.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide; all Maryland counties are eligible. Certain incentive areas including Qualified Census Tracts (QCTs) and Difficult Development Areas (DDAs) may provide enhanced credit percentages and better financing terms under federal regulations.
requirements_list: Building must be placed in service within two years after the year of allocation
Building must provide at least in part for low-income occupancy
Owner must rent either 20% of units to households with incomes at 50% or less of area median income or 40% of units to households with incomes at 60% or less of area median income
Building must remain in compliance with a minimum 40-year covenant to enforce compliance (15-year initial compliance period plus minimum 15-year extended use period)
Comply with tenant income, maximum rent levels, and low-income occupancy requirements
No finding of discrimination under the Fair Housing Act may have occurred
Building must be suitable for occupancy and meet local health, safety, and building codes
Eligible basis cannot be reduced by federal grants received
Building must be used for residential rental purposes and occupied on a non-transient basis
For nonprofit sponsors: must materially participate in the operation of the development
Project owner must select one of three set-aside elections: 20@50, 40@60, or Income Averaging Set-Aside
Project must comply with §42 of the Internal Revenue Code and all Maryland LIHTC Program requirements
Development team must meet previous project performance and credit history requirements
Site must have utility availability, appropriate zoning, and environmental assessments
Project owner must enter into Extended Low-Income Housing Covenant
For acquisition projects, may require legal or certified public accountant opinion regarding satisfaction of Ten-Year Rule
Non-competitive projects financed with tax-exempt bonds must still be evaluated against Threshold Criteria and Competitive Scoring Criteria
Market study requirements must be met including market analysis, capture rate, vacancy rates, and absorption rate
Development quality thresholds must be met for project type (new construction, rehabilitation, renovation, or adaptive reuse)
Ten percent of state's annual allocation set aside solely for nonprofit sponsors
During extended use period (post-year 15), buildings must receive physical inspections at least once every five years
Annual owner certification of continuing compliance required throughout compliance and extended use periods

During extended use period, buildings with 100% LIHTC units are exempt from annual tenant recertification requirements; other buildings may apply for exemption if they meet extended use period requirements
Tenant files must be maintained with annual income certifications and supporting documentation
Utility allowances must be reviewed and updated at least once per calendar year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications for competitive LIHTC are solicited by CDA by Public Notice in one round per year. Complete applications must be submitted with a non-refundable application fee by the deadline specified in the public notice. Projects are first evaluated against Threshold Criteria to ensure they meet basic Maryland LIHTC Program requirements and Internal Revenue Code requirements. Projects passing the threshold review are then rated and ranked using Competitive Scoring Criteria based on factors such as project feasibility, community need, and compliance with state priorities. After evaluation, recommendations are made by CDA to DHCD's Housing Finance Review Committee (HFRC), which makes recommendations to the Secretary, who has final decision authority on approvals. Approved sponsors receive either a LIHTC reservation letter (conditional commitment) or allocation depending on funding round timing. Following approval, sponsors must provide evidence of timely project completion and receive an IRS Form 8609 upon completion, documenting cost certifications. Successful applicants receive approval and letters of allocation based on the State's Qualified Allocation Plan. For projects with 50% or more of development and acquisition costs financed with tax-exempt bonds, LIHTC may be received on the entire qualified basis outside the State's annual allocation. Projects with less than 50% financed through tax-exempt bonds receive LIHTC on the appropriate portion without requiring allocation. During the 15-year compliance period, projects are monitored by CDA for adherence to program requirements. After year 15, projects enter an extended use period with monitoring transferred to Division of Credit Assurance (DCA) with less frequent inspection requirements (at least once every five years) while maintaining continued affordability compliance through a covenant extending the obligation for at least 15 additional years. Owners must provide annual certifications of compliance and comply with ongoing monitoring requirements during the 40+ year compliance and extended use periods. Threshold waivers may be granted at CDA's discretion for compelling reasons not inconsistent with the Internal Revenue Code.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that facilitates dialogue between homeowners and lenders with the help of a neutral third party (an administrative law judge from the Maryland Office of Administrative Hearings trained in mediation) to help reach a mutually satisfactory solution and potentially avoid foreclosure.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Homeowners receive mediation services with a neutral third party to facilitate dialogue between the homeowner and lender. Homeowners must pay a non-refundable $50 fee to the Circuit Court when filing the Request for Foreclosure Mediation form. The mediation must be requested within 25 days of the lender initiating foreclosure proceedings.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners whose primary residence is in foreclosure
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mediation services to facilitate negotiation between homeowner and lender to reach a mutually acceptable resolution
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Homeowner must be living in the foreclosed property as their primary residence
Only available to homeowners, not tenants of foreclosed rental or commercial properties
Request must be filed within 25 days of lender initiating foreclosure proceedings
Non-refundable $50 fee required when filing request
Request for Foreclosure Mediation form must be filed with the Circuit Court in the county or city where foreclosure action was filed
Form must also be sent to the lender's attorney
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Homeowner completes the Request for Foreclosure Mediation form within 25 days of lender initiating foreclosure proceedings, pays a $50 non-refundable fee to the Circuit Court, and submits both the form and fee to the Circuit Court in the county where the foreclosure was filed. The form must also be sent to the lender's attorney. The Office of Administrative Hearings schedules mediations based on location of the foreclosure action.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Ground Rent Redemption Loan Program provides loans to homeowners to buy out (redeem) ground leases. A ground lease is a lease for a term of years, usually 99 years, that is renewable forever and is subject to periodic payment of ground rent by the leasehold tenant to the ground lease holder. Ground rents are most prevalent in Baltimore City but are held in some other counties as well. The program was created by the Maryland General Assembly in 2007.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 0% interest loans for up to 30 years to redeem (buy out) ground leases. Maximum loan amount is $3,500, including transactional costs of up to $1,000. Transactional costs cover title search and loan closing. The redemption amount is calculated by dividing the annual ground rent fee by the capitalization rate, which depends on when the ground lease was established (rates: .04 for leases created April 8, 1884 to April 5, 1888; .06 for April 6, 1888 to July 1, 1982; .12 for July 2, 1982 or later). A lien is recorded against the property for the loan amount.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners who own and occupy the subject property as their principal residence and hold ground leases.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and redemption of ground leases. Transactional costs associated with title search and loan closing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Ground rents are most prevalent in Baltimore City but are held in some other counties as well.
requirements_list: Applicant must own the subject property
Applicant must occupy it as their principal residence
Household income cannot exceed 80 percent of the Statewide median (based on household size)
Must provide evidence of ownership (copy of deed)
Must provide evidence of ground rent (copy of recorded document)
Must provide documentation of household income
If ground lease was executed before April 9, 1884, check if it contains specific provision for redemption
Anyone named on the deed but not occupying the property must provide proof of residence elsewhere
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Obtain and complete the DHCD Ground Rent Redemption Loan application. 2. Gather required documentation including: copy of recorded deed, copy of most recent ground rent billing statement, income verification (most recent pay stubs, 2 years of federal tax returns and W-2s or Affidavit of Tax Filing Status), copy of homeowners insurance and flood insurance policies, mortgage verification or statement, most recent county and local property tax bill, and most recent bank statements. 3. Submit completed application with all required documentation to DHCD. 4. Choose a qualified title company to conduct the title search and loan closing. 5. Lien will be recorded against the property for the loan amount.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Group Home Program helps individuals, qualified limited partnerships, and nonprofit organizations construct, acquire, modify, or refinance existing housing to serve as group homes or assisted living units for eligible persons and households with special housing needs. The program is funded through state funds from the Group Home Financing Program and proceeds from tax-exempt mortgage revenue bonds under the Special Housing Opportunities Program. The objective of the program is to provide loans to sponsors to finance or refinance the costs of acquiring, constructing and modifying buildings which will provide group homes for low income, elderly, handicapped, disabled, and other citizens of the State with special housing needs. This is deemed to also include housing for homeless persons and victims of sex trafficking.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans with interest rates ranging from 0 to 7 percent depending on the source of funds and project cash flow. The target interest rate is currently 4 percent. Maximum loan term is generally 30 years, though the maximum term can be up to 40 years. Construction term may not exceed one year. Loan amounts vary by geographic location and may not exceed the appraised value of the property. For first lien position, loans may finance up to 100% of appraised value; for second lien position, up to 95% of appraised value. State Group Home Financing Program loans are typically combined with Special Housing Opportunities Program loans. Nonprofit sponsors are expected to contribute 5% toward the project; individual sponsors are required to make a 10% equity contribution. Loans may contain provisions for deferral of interest and/or principal, generally not to exceed a two-year period. Maximum loan amounts vary by county and are available on the Department's website.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are not currently being accepted. Applications will reopen at a later date.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Special Loans Program, Community Development Administration
structured_extraction.contact_phone: (301) 429-7409, Toll Free (Maryland Only): 877-218-8101, Maryland Relay for the Deaf: 800-735-2258
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, qualified limited partnerships, and nonprofit organizations providing group homes to eligible residents. For Special Housing Opportunity Program funding, nonprofits must have 501(c)(3) IRS designation. All applicants must be licensed by the appropriate Maryland licensing authority. Sponsors must demonstrate prior group home experience with comparable size and type projects, or demonstrate capacity based on other related business endeavors and prior satisfactory financial and credit management if they do not have prior group home experience.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds may be used to refinance existing group home mortgages or for all related development costs including acquisition, closing costs, appraisal and inspection fees, and modification costs. Eligible modifications include repair or replacement of major systems (heating, roofing, electrical, plumbing), accessibility modifications (ramps, grab bars), lead paint abatement, general repairs and upgrades (painting, floor coverings), and minor improvements to bring properties into compliance with state and local occupancy codes. For group homes housing four or more individuals, up to 10 percent of the building's space may be used for nonresidential uses in conformance with local zoning requirements that may offer goods or services benefiting lower income or otherwise disadvantaged persons.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located in Maryland. For Special Housing Opportunities Program financing, property must be located in a Priority Funding Area unless a waiver is granted on an exceptional basis for existing construction.
requirements_list: Property must be in good repair and in compliance with applicable State and local housing and occupancy codes, or be able to be made so with loan proceeds or other sources of funds
Appraisal must be completed by an appraiser on the Department's approved appraisers list
Property must have a home inspection acceptable to the department and cannot be more than 120 days old at time of approval
All properties built prior to 1978 must have a lead paint risk assessment prepared by a certified and accredited lead paint testing company
If Special Housing Opportunities Program financing is requested, property must be located in a Priority Funding Area unless a waiver is granted on an exceptional basis for existing construction
Residents of homes must be special needs groups such as developmentally or physically disabled, elderly, juveniles, or homeless
Sponsors must maintain 51 percent of all beds available for residents who have incomes 60 percent or less of area median income
All applicants must be licensed by the appropriate Maryland licensing authority
Nonprofit sponsors must contribute 5% toward the project
Individual sponsors must make a 10% equity contribution

Eligible Sponsors must be licensed to operate the project by the appropriate state agency and have a contract acceptable to CDA with a State agency or county government which provides operating income and/or grant funds for the project

For nonprofit organizations: audited financial statements for prior three years required; fund balance must be positive and stable with no open liens, judgments or bankruptcies; Current Assets to Current Liabilities ratio should generally be 1.10 or greater

For individual sponsors: federal income tax statements (990s) for most recent three years and personal financial statements required; D&B credit reports must show history of meeting long- and short-term credit obligations with financial risk score/credit score not higher than 3; no past due accounts, unsatisfied state or federal tax liens, or prior foreclosures or bankruptcy filings
Organization must have estimated life at least as long as the proposed term of the loan
Organization must be authorized to conduct business in Maryland and authorized to incur debt to acquire, rehabilitate or construct housing for special needs populations
Organizational documents must contain provisions prohibiting discrimination based on race, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, disability or familial status
Organization must not have defaulted on a Department or other government loan
Organization must not be on the Department's or other government debarred list
For nonprofits: 501(c)(3) status must be verified with the Internal Revenue Service
Federal Funds Notice must be completed by the borrower and executed by the seller prior to entering into a binding sales contract for all Group Home Program loan requests using federal funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit a completed loan application to the Special Loans Program at the Community Development Administration, 7800 Harkins Road, 369B, Lanham, Maryland 20706, ATTN: Group Home Financing Program. Sponsors are encouraged to arrange an initial meeting with the GHFP Manager to discuss the proposed project and review general program requirements and processing procedures. Upon receipt, the application will be date stamped and assigned a case number. A letter is sent to the Sponsor acknowledging receipt, identifying required documentation not included with the initial application, and specifying a timeframe for submitting missing documentation (generally 30 days). If missing documentation is not received within the specified timeframe, the program may withdraw the application and provide formal written notice of withdrawal. Dun and Bradstreet (D&B) or other credit reports are obtained. The file is then reviewed by the GHFP Manager for initial evaluation to determine sponsor and project eligibility. Upon completion of eligibility review and determination of funding source, the Sponsor is notified in writing. The eligibility review will generally be completed within 90-120 days of receiving a complete application (30 days to approve or deny applicant, 30 days to allow additional information to be provided, 30 days to seek HFRC approval, 30 days to close). A Federal Funds Notice must be executed prior to entering into a binding sales contract with the seller for all Group Home Program loan requests. A feasibility analysis follows, including evaluation of the development team, site, construction/rehabilitation, occupancy and income analysis, development and operating budgets, and other sources of financing. A commitment analysis is then performed, including appraisal review, plans and specifications review, loan terms establishment, and commitment approval by the appropriate authority.

structured_extraction.program_name: HAF WholeHome Critical Home Repairs Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) Homeowner Assistance Fund (HAF) WholeHome Grant helps Maryland homeowners facing financial hardship due to the COVID-19 pandemic by providing grants for critical repairs in primary residences that could lead to displacement if not addressed. Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis. This is a one-time financial assistance per household.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $10,000 per project with no minimum amount. No deed of trust is recorded as this is grant assistance. Payments will be made according to the homeowner's preference: either 33% deposit with 67% at completion, or 0% deposit with 100% at completion. There is no minimum credit score requirement. Payments or deposits made by homeowners for work or materials prior to grant approval will NOT be reimbursed.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: September 30, 2026, or until funding is fully reserved, whichever comes first
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners who have experienced financial hardship due to COVID-19 after January 21, 2020 (includes hardships that began before January 21, 2020 but continued after that date), with household income at or below 150% of County Area Median Income (AMI), and are named on the deed of their primary residence that they occupy.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Critical repairs in primary residences including but not limited to: mold/mildew remediation, asbestos removal, non-functioning heating/cooling systems (no heat/no air), electrical repairs, plumbing and septic repairs, wells, roof repair/replacement, lead paint hazard reduction/elimination, structural and maintenance issues, and trip/slip hazards.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. Income limits vary by county and household size, capped at 150% of County AMI (not to exceed US median).
requirements_list: Experienced financial hardship due to COVID-19 after January 21, 2020
Household income at or below 150% of County Area Median Income (AMI) based on household size
Must be a Maryland homeowner
Must reside in the primary residence as principal residence
Must be named on the property deed

Must provide at least one work proposal estimate for the critical repair from a licensed and insured Maryland Home Improvement Contractor, dated within the last 60 days, with photographs documenting the repairs

If other persons are named on the deed but do not live at the property, proof must be provided (copy of driver's license, utility bill, notarized statement, or other evidence they live elsewhere); if deceased, a copy of death certificate
Submit income documentation (paystubs, tax returns, award letters, unemployment documentation, or zero income statement)
Attest to COVID-19 financial hardship after January 21, 2020
One-time assistance per household
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete the WholeHome Homeowner Assistance Fund (HAF) grant application and submit with required documentation: income verification documents, proof of COVID-19 financial hardship after January 21, 2020, and at least one detailed estimate from a licensed Maryland Home Improvement Contractor dated within 60 days. 2. Contractor must complete the Bid Cover Page and provide: current Maryland Home Improvement Contractor license (or trade-specific license), Certificate of Liability Insurance (minimum $1M per occurrence), Letter of Good Standing from Maryland, and completed W-9 form. 3. Bid must include photographs documenting the critical repairs, contractor's phone number, and email address. 4. Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis. 5. Upon approval, applicant must sign: Commitment letter, grant agreement, Rehabilitation contract, W-9 form, and final invoice from contractor accepting work as completed. 6. Submit application and all documentation by email to Rehab.HAFApplications@Maryland.gov or by mail to: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA Special Loan Programs- Rehab Homeowner Assistance Fund (HAF), 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program that supports affordable housing by providing funding to state and local governments for building, buying, or fixing rental housing, owner-occupied housing, and special needs housing such as group homes.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HOME funds are typically provided as non-interest bearing or zero-interest deferred loans with flexible terms. They may also be provided as amortizing loans, recoverable grants (requiring repayment when property is sold or no longer used for low-income housing), or as grants at the State's discretion. Loan terms range from 20 to 40 years depending on the type of housing financed. For rental projects, equity sharing may be required when low-income usage is discontinued. The maximum amount of assistance to a single project generally does not exceed the amount needed to make the project viable and comply with federal HOME regulations. If the property is sold or stops being used for low-income housing, the borrower must share any equity gain with DHCD. HOME funds are targeted to serve households at or below 80 percent of the area median household income (adjusted for household size, determined annually by HUD). The State has flexibility in the use of HOME funds to address unique underwriting needs of each project.
structured_extraction.program_audience: State government agencies, local governments, local housing agencies, nonprofit organizations, and Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Building, buying, or fixing rental housing, owner-occupied housing, and special needs housing such as group homes. HOME funds may be used for soft seconds to reduce home costs, land acquisition, development costs, construction financing, group home development, single-family rehabilitation, replacement housing, tenant-based rental assistance (limited basis including security deposit assistance), and to help victims of disaster.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: HOME funds are used primarily in non-Participating Jurisdictions throughout Maryland, which include the entire State except for Baltimore City and Anne Arundel County (except the City of Annapolis), Baltimore, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, and Prince George's counties. These jurisdictions receive a direct allocation of HOME funds. The State may provide funds in Participating Jurisdictions as deemed necessary.
requirements_list: For rental housing units: residents' household incomes must be 50% or less of the area median household income (or up to 80% of AMI for targeted use)
For owner-occupied housing units: owner's household income must be 55% or less of the area median household income (or up to 80% of AMI for targeted use)
Income limits are based on household size and set annually by HUD
If using HOME funds with other CDA programs, projects must meet both CDA program eligibility requirements and HOME program federal requirements
Number of income-restricted units usually calculated by dividing the amount of HOME funds by total project cost, then multiplying by total number of units
Nonprofit organizations must be certified as Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs) to be eligible for CHDO set-aside funds (minimum 15% of State HOME allocation)
CHDO certification requirements: organizational profile, planning information, and if certified for more than two years, must have produced HOME-eligible housing within that period
Projects must comply with all federal HOME program regulations and monitoring requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Project applications may include requests for HOME funds as part of DHCD's existing housing program applications, or DHCD staff may propose the use of HOME funds during project evaluation and underwriting. For CHDO Special Reserve Fund projects, applications will be reviewed on a first-come, first-serve basis with priority given to Community Housing Development Organizations and non-profit organizations. CHDOs applying for predevelopment loans (up to $50,000) must submit project-specific assistance requests. For CHDO operating assistance, eligible CHDOs must provide recent financial statements showing yearly operating expenses and evidence of good standing. All applications require compliance with federal HOME administrative and monitoring requirements including site inspections and tenant certifications.

structured_extraction.program_name: Healthy Homes for Healthy Kids Lead Initiative
structured_extraction.program_description: Partnership initiative created in 2016 among DHCD, Maryland Department of Health, and Maryland Department of the Environment to help families reduce lead exposure in homes built before 1978 through lead removal and minor home repairs necessary to ensure lead paint remains properly sealed.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides funding for lead removal and minor home repairs necessary to ensure lead paint remains properly sealed for eligible families. The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, in partnership with the Maryland Department of Health, will pay for lead elimination from the house or apartment where the child lives or spends time, at no cost to the owner or tenant.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with children under 19 years old who have elevated blood lead levels and meet Medicaid/MCHP eligibility criteria
requirements_list: Child is under 19 years old and lives in Maryland
Child has a recent blood lead test of 5 micrograms per deciliter (µg/dL) or higher
Child is enrolled in or eligible for Medicaid/Maryland Children's Health Insurance Program (MCHP)
Child spends 10 hours or more per week in the location (home, apartment, or day care) where the lead exposure occurred

structured_extraction.program_name: Home Repairs and Energy Efficiency Improvements Programs
structured_extraction.program_description: Affordable loan programs and services to improve accessibility and home safety and save money on energy bills.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners seeking to improve accessibility, home safety, and energy efficiency
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home repairs, accessibility improvements, home safety improvements, and energy efficiency upgrades

structured_extraction.program_description: HSP helps communities across Maryland prevent and end homelessness by providing technical support and funding to Continuums of Care and Local Homeless Coalitions to coordinate homelessness services and connect people to housing programs, shelters, and other services. HSP provides over $15 million in annual funding to CoCs to deliver and organize homeless services in their local communities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HSP provides annual funding through grants to Continuums of Care and Local Homeless Coalitions. For SFY2026, approximately $15.2 million in total funding is available ($14 million in state HSP funds and $1.2 million in HUD Emergency Solutions Grant funding). Grantees must provide a 25% match. Funding is distributed to individual CoCs/LHCs based on competitive application review and actual allocation from HUD and the State. SFY2026 grant agreements have an 18-month performance period from July 1, 2025 through December 31, 2026. Funds support eight main activities: homeless prevention/shelter diversion, emergency shelter, street outreach, rapid re-housing, permanent supportive housing, HMIS, special events, and administrative costs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 25, 2025 at 5pm
structured_extraction.contact_name: LaToya Arnold-Artis, Director, Homelessness Solutions Program
structured_extraction.program_audience: Lead agencies for Maryland Continuums of Care (CoCs) and Local Homeless Coalitions (LHCs) that coordinate homeless services. Eligible applicants include: (1) HUD-approved Collaborative Applicant/lead agency of a Maryland Continuum of Care, or (2) DHCD-approved lead agency for a Balance of State CoC Local Homeless Coalition. Lead agencies may subgrant all or part of funding to government agencies or nonprofit organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Street Outreach, Emergency Shelter, Host Homes, Rapid Re-Housing, Permanent Supportive Housing, Homeless Prevention/Shelter Diversion, HMIS Data Entry and System Administration, Special Events (Homeless Resource Days and Point-in-Time Count support), and Administrative Costs. Specific eligible costs include: rental assistance, financial assistance, housing stabilization services, case management, facility operations, supportive services, workforce development integration, direct cash transfers for unaccompanied youth and returning citizens, and flex funds for landlord incentives and removal of tenant housing barriers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across Maryland. All 24 counties plus Baltimore City are eligible.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a HUD-approved Collaborative Applicant/lead agency of a Maryland Continuum of Care OR a DHCD-approved lead agency for a Balance of State CoC Local Homeless Coalition
Applicant must be a nonprofit or local government entity
Applicant must administer homeless services from a client-centered, Housing First approach
Applicant must comply with fair housing, equal access, and non-discrimination policies
Applicant must maintain a formalized grievance procedure for termination and denial of benefits
Applicant must maintain sound financial program management in accordance with federal OMB Uniform Guidance and Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP)
Applicant must maintain all books, client records, and financial documents for at least five (5) years after grant close
Applicant must use Homelessness Management Information System (HMIS) or comparable database for victim services providers
Applicant must participate regularly in Continuum of Care meetings and activities
Applicant must maintain written standards to guide work of subgrantees
Lead agencies must provide 25% match for HSP grant (may be met at community and/or grantee level)
Matching funds must be used to meet HSP goals and expended within grant year
Match must come from local or private sources; limited federal and state sources allowed (CSBG and EAP only)

All lead agencies must certify that subgrantees meet HSP requirements and will perform: (1) at least one risk assessment of all grantees, (2) monitoring and compliance visit to high-risk subgrantees, and (3) monitoring and compliance visits to medium- and low-risk subgrantees
Applicant must enroll in HMIS or comparable database and be in full compliance with HMIS implementation guidelines at time of application
New subgrantees must be in full compliance with HMIS at time grant agreement is signed
Applicant must participate in Maryland State Homelessness Data Warehouse (MSHDW)
SFY2026 applications must include two budget scenarios: (1) level funding to HSP FY24 award and (2) 30% increase above FY24 award
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must follow a multi-step process: (1) Update Organization Profile and submit supporting materials (including W-9, organizational chart, recent audit, articles of incorporation, tax exemption letter, certificate of good standing, charity registration status, and board list) by March 21, 2025 via Project Portal and email to LaToya.Arnold-Artis@Maryland.gov. (2) Complete and submit the CoC/LHC Application Narrative (8-part Word document addressing Strategy, Project Selection, System Performance, Coordinated Entry, Equity, Compliance & Quality, Youth Projects, and RRH & PSH Projects) by April 25, 2025. (3) Submit Detailed Budget Template (Excel with both level funding and 30% increase scenarios), Project List, and Project Performance Tool by April 25, 2025. (4) Submit supporting performance data including Stella P Report, 2024 System Performance Measures Report, HUD Annual Performance Report from HMIS for each renewal project, and 2024 Housing Inventory Count and Point in Time Count data by April 25, 2025. (5) All applications submitted via DHCD Project Portal with attachments. Organizations must create only one application per Continuum of Care or Local Homeless Coalition. Applications are reviewed through three stages: Threshold Review (Organization Profile), CoC/LHC Performance Evaluation (Application Narrative), and Project-Level Performance Evaluation (Project Review Tool). Training session held March 3, 2025 from 10-11am via Google Meet (recorded). Award notifications and grant agreements issued June 2, 2025. Grant period begins July 1, 2025.
