structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Housing Rehabilitation Program aims to provide affordable funding to address critical health and safety issues and bring properties into an agreement with applicable building codes and standards by offering a suite of special loans programs.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners in Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: The federal Housing Choice Voucher Program provides rental subsidies in the form of vouchers to eligible families or individuals to use toward housing payments. Public housing agencies administer the program locally for their area by creating eligibility criteria, processing applications, developing and maintaining waitlists, and verifying requirements. The program is administered statewide by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) through multiple regional offices and subcontractors.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rental subsidies provided in the form of housing choice vouchers that eligible families or individuals use toward housing payments. The voucher assistance covers the difference between the tenant's family share (tenant payment) and the actual rent charged, up to the payment standard established by the PHA. Assistance includes tenant-based vouchers that can be used to rent units of the participant's choice throughout the jurisdiction, as well as special-purpose vouchers for targeted populations such as Veterans Affairs Supportive Housing (VASH), Family Unification Program (FUP), Non-Elderly Disabled (NED2), and Mainstream vouchers. Program participation includes mandatory briefings on housing search services, fair housing rights, and mobility counseling to encourage families to choose housing in areas outside of poverty or minority concentration.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Varies by jurisdiction. For Eastern Shore (Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Talbot, Somerset, Wicomico, Worcester Counties) and Town of Elkton: April 1-30, 2026. Waiting lists are generally closed; applicants should contact their local PHA office to inquire about reopening dates and special admission categories.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 410-901-4081 or local agency. Allegany County/City of Cumberland: 301-783-1880; Frederick County: 301-600-1061; Garrett County: 301-334-9431; Eastern Shore Regional Office: 410-901-4080
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible families or individuals seeking rental housing assistance, including extremely low-income families (at or below 30% of Area Median Income), very low-income families (30-50% of AMI), low-income families (50-80% of AMI), elderly individuals, families with disabilities, and other special populations through targeted voucher programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing payments and rental assistance. Funds must be used for rent on decent, safe, and sanitary housing that meets Housing Quality Standards (HQS). Vouchers can be used in the private rental market for single-family homes, apartments, condominiums, and other eligible housing types throughout Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across Maryland, administered by local public housing agencies in each county and municipality. Program is delivered through: Human Resources Development Commission (Allegany County and City of Cumberland); Frederick County Department of Housing and Community Development; Garrett County Community Action Committee, Inc.; and Eastern Shore Regional Office serving Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, and Worcester Counties.
requirements_list: U.S. citizen or eligible immigrant status
Valid Social Security number
Family income at or below specified income limits (targeting extremely low-income at 30% AMI and very low-income at 50% AMI)
Pass tenant screening including criminal background check (with certain offenses creating ineligibility or restrictions)
Not be fleeing criminal prosecution or violating parole/probation
Family composition requirements met (single person, family groups)
No prohibited admissions criteria violations (e.g., involvement in drug-related criminal activity, violent criminal activity, or other disqualifying activities within specified timeframes)
Verification of identity and income through employment records, tax returns, bank statements, or other documentation
Compliance with program family obligations and lease requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Contact the local public housing agency that administers the program for your county or municipality using the contact information listed above. 2. Submit a preliminary application or pre-application as directed by the PHA. 3. Check your status on the Waiting List Status Portal if the list is open. 4. Applicants selected from the waiting list complete a full application at an eligibility appointment. 5. Submit verification of income, identity, immigration status, and other required documentation. 6. Attend a mandatory briefing session covering housing search services, fair housing rights, lease obligations, and program requirements. 7. Receive a voucher with a specified term (typically 120 days to find housing). 8. Search for eligible housing in the private rental market. 9. Landlord completes Request for Tenancy Approval form with unit details and proposed rent. 10. PHA conducts initial Housing Quality Standards (HQS) inspection to verify unit meets standards. 11. Landlord and tenant sign lease; PHA executes Housing Assistance Payments (HAP) contract with owner. 12. Tenant begins occupancy with PHA subsidy reducing their tenant payment contribution. Applications are subject to lottery selection for waitlist placement when lists are open. Waiting lists may be closed in some jurisdictions; contact your local office about reopening schedules and whether special categories (such as persons with disabilities, families displaced by disaster, homeless individuals) can be added while list is closed.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program providing funding and support for innovative multifamily housing development projects that test new approaches and models for rental housing in Maryland. The program provides low- or no-interest loans to local housing authorities or to county governments partnering with housing developers. Funds may also be used for projects where a county, in conjunction with a local housing authority or a housing developer, acquires existing private-sector housing to create opportunities for public housing authorities and county governments to increase the volume of housing production and reward counties pursuing innovative solutions to the problem of housing scarcity. The Fund may also be used for projects where a county, in conjunction with a local housing authority or housing developer, purchases existing privately owned housing.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low- or no-interest loans up to $2,500,000 per project. Short-term loans (3-5 years) with approximately 3% interest rate, or longer-term loans (7-10 years) with approximately 5.5% interest rate. HIPP will be subordinate loans, with positioning considered on a case-by-case basis. Loans may be used for new construction, acquisition with or without substantial renovation of rental housing including apartment buildings, townhouses, single-family homes, single room occupancy buildings, and shared housing facilities. Funds available: $5 million total for FY 2026, with DHCD selecting up to 3 projects (maximum one award per jurisdiction). Application fee: $2,500.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: May 18, 2026 at 12:00 p.m. (Noon)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public housing authorities; county governments partnering with housing developers; county governments in conjunction with a PHA or developer to acquire existing housing. Sponsors must have an ownership interest in the project's ownership entity.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding may be used for: (1) Acquisition of land and new construction; (2) Existing property with major rehabilitation; or (3) Existing multifamily properties with no major rehabilitation. Projects must provide mixed-income, cross-subsidized housing with at least 20% of units set aside for households at 50% AMI OR at least 40% of units set aside for households at 60% AMI. Eligible housing types include apartment buildings, townhouses, single-family homes, single room occupancy buildings, and shared housing facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide; projects must be located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Sponsors must be public housing authority or county government partnering with a housing developer, or a county with a PHA or developer to acquire existing housing
Sponsors must have ownership interest in project ownership entity as demonstrated by organizational chart and/or partnership agreement
Projects must be in Maryland and provide mixed-income, cross-subsidized housing
At least 20% of units set aside for households with gross annual income not more than 50% AMI OR at least 40% of units set aside for households with gross annual income not more than 60% AMI
Projects must be ready for occupancy within two (2) years of award selection date

For Preferences scoring: Project cannot use LIHTC equity or tax-exempt volume cap; affordability restrictions must remain for at least 99 years; project must remain in public ownership; project must include commitment to prevailing wage requirements
Applicants must comply with all federal and state fair housing laws and equal opportunity requirements
No tenants can be forced to move without cause in the 12 months preceding application submission
Projects must meet DHCD Multifamily Policies regarding construction standards and individual unit health and safety requirements
Application fee of $2,500 required, payable to Community Development Administration
Application fee must be submitted to: Community Development Administration, Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, Post Office Box 2524, Landover Hills, MD 20784
Completed CDA Form 202 Multifamily Rental Financing Application reflecting all project aspects including development and operating budgets and pro forma
Organizational chart showing current or proposed ownership entity structure
Development team information and qualifications documentation for developer, sponsor/owner, general contractor, architect, and property manager
Letters of intent or commitment letters for all other construction and permanent funding sources
Certifications and compliance documentation as outlined in application package
Projects meeting threshold criteria from Multifamily Rental Financing Program Guide Section 3
Submit Affirmative Fair Housing Marketing Plan using HUD-935.2A form
Development team must meet threshold requirements including previous project performance and credit history
Projects must ensure accessibility for persons with disabilities
Projects must certify to ongoing compliance, asset management, and inspections per DHCD Multifamily Policies
All project information must be registered on DHCD's Housing Registry Website
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Request electronic application folder using Electronic Submission Package Request Form in Multifamily Library. 2. Complete full Application Submission Package using CDA Form 202 and all required exhibits and certifications. 3. Submit application fee of $2,500 (separate cover) to Community Development Administration, Post Office Box 2524, Landover Hills, MD 20784. 4. Submit complete electronic application including all attachments and exhibits via Procorem WorkCenter with clear tabs for each section. 5. Ensure all required documents are completed; applications may not be retyped or modified. 6. Waiver requests, if applicable, must be submitted separately via Waiver Request Form at least 15 days prior to application deadline (by May 4, 2026). 7. Applications must be received by DHCD no later than 12:00 p.m. on May 18, 2026. 8. DHCD staff reviews submissions for completeness; incomplete applications will not be processed. 9. Scoring committee evaluates complete proposals based on Project Readiness, Location, Preferences, Innovation, Affordability, and Developer/Owner/Partner Capacity criteria. 10. Highest-scored proposal recommended to CDA Director for approval, then to Secretary for final approval and allocation. 11. One project per jurisdiction may be selected; if jurisdiction has multiple applications, highest-scoring application is selected with number of units as tiebreaker. Virtual information session available March 11, 2026 at 12:00 p.m.

structured_extraction.program_description: Housing Revenue Bonds issued under a parity bond resolution created in 1996 finance primarily multi-family housing with credit enhancement by FHA, FHLMC, GNMA, FNMA, and the Maryland Housing Fund.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Bonds issued to finance multi-family housing loans, with credit enhancement by federal mortgage insurers and the Maryland Housing Fund.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financing of multi-family housing; portfolio also includes some single family loans and group home loans.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit for Maryland residents who make their homes more accessible. Provides up to 50% of renovation costs back, up to $5,000. Applies to your own home, a family member's home, or a rental property.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to 50% of renovation costs back, capped at $5,000 per year. Credit amount depends on accessibility features added. DHCD can approve up to $1,000,000 in tax credits per year. Eligible renovations include no-step entrances, doorways with 32-inch or wider clear opening, grab bars and reinforced walls, handrails, rocker panel light switches, accessible routes, accessible handles, chairlifts and elevators, visual smoke/fire/carbon monoxide alarms, roll-in showers/tubs, accessible doorbells and light switches, railings, slip-resistant floors, lever water controls, pull-out drawers and shelves, accessible door hardware, bathroom mirrors within reach ranges, accessible parking spaces, kitchen appliances within reach ranges, and adequate maneuvering space in bathrooms and kitchens.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 1st of the current calendar year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who have completed home renovations with accessibility features
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home renovations that include accessibility features such as no-step entrances, doorways with 32-inch or wider clear opening, grab bars, handrails, rocker panel light switches, accessible routes, chairlifts, elevators, visual smoke/fire/carbon monoxide alarms, roll-in showers, accessible handles, railings, slip-resistant floors, lever water controls, pull-out drawers and shelves, accessible door hardware, bathroom mirrors within reach ranges, accessible parking spaces, kitchen appliances within reach ranges, and adequate maneuvering space (at least 30 inches by 48 inches in bathrooms and kitchens).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland residents only
requirements_list: Be a Maryland resident
File taxes in Maryland for the same calendar year you made the renovations
Have proof of payment for home renovations that include accessibility features
Submit completed application to DHCD with receipts, invoices, and before-and-after photos
Complete renovations during the previous tax year
Certify that the accessibility features claimed were paid for by the applicant
Keep documentation (invoices and receipts) to verify funds were used for intended purposes
Declare that no other funds or tax credits from other sources were received for the same renovations
Submit only one application per household
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit completed application and supporting documentation (detailed invoices, proof of payment, pre-accessibility renovation pictures, and post-accessibility renovation pictures) by June 1st of the current calendar year. Applications can be submitted online or as a paper application via email to DHCD.SLP_Documentation@Maryland.gov or by mail to Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA Special Loan Programs- Independent Living Tax Credit Application, Attention: SLP Intake Team, 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. If approved, applicants will be notified and issued a tax credit certificate by August 31st of the current calendar year. Recipients must then file an amended tax return (Form 502X) with the DHCD tax credit certification attached. A representative from DHCD may contact the applicant to gather more information during the review process.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides indoor plumbing in residential properties by offering loans to owner-occupants of single-family homes with inoperative or unsafe plumbing and to owners of rental residential properties for income-eligible households. This program helps pay for adding or fixing water or sewer systems and connecting to public systems.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans with interest rates ranging from 0% to 6% based on ability to pay. Interest rates are determined by the income of households served and projected income available to repay the loan. Maximum loan amount is $50,000. Maximum loan term is 30 years. Loans exceeding $5,000 or with deferred payments are secured by a mortgage. Deferred loans are available to borrowers with incomes at or below 50% of statewide or Washington, D.C. MSA median income, if necessary for project feasibility. Deferred amounts or portions may be forgiven on an annual basis for families with incomes below 30% of statewide or Washington, D.C. MSA median income.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of single-family homes and owners of rental residential properties with income-eligible households.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wells, septic tanks and drain fields, piping from septic system into residential building, connection expenses to public water or sewer systems including fees and assessments, plumbing fixtures and equipment including handicapped fixtures, additions/modifications/alterations for private toilet and bath facilities, sand mound systems, purification systems, percolation test costs, and alternative/innovative septic and water systems. Program funds may also address plumbing issues, water and well problems, and septic and sewer concerns as part of critical health and safety repairs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Single-family, owner-occupied houses with inoperative or unsafe plumbing
Properties must be structurally sound
Owner-occupants or rental property owners with income-eligible households
Household income at or below 80% of statewide or Washington, D.C. MSA median income for standard loans (interest rates 4.5%-6.0%)
Household income at or below 60% of statewide or Washington, D.C. MSA median income for lower-interest loans (interest rates 0%-4.5%)
Household income at or below 50% of statewide or Washington, D.C. MSA median income may be eligible for deferred payments
For rental units, project income determines loan deferment or repayment requirements
Applicants must provide proof of home ownership (deed and current mortgage statement)
Applicants must obtain the lowest qualifying bid from a licensed Maryland tradesperson or company
Total bids should not exceed $50,000
Bids should not be more than 60 days old
Licensed contractors must provide current MHIC license or trade-specific license, Certificate of Liability Insurance (COI), Letter of Good Standing, and completed W-9
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants contact their local housing office by county or the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Special Loan Programs. Applicants must complete the Maryland Home Rehabilitation Program Application and submit it along with required documentation including proof of income (most recent 2 months of paystubs or 2 years of tax returns), proof of home ownership (deed, mortgage statement, property tax bill), and contractor bids with required documentation (MHIC/trade license, Certificate of Liability Insurance, Letter of Good Standing, W-9). Applications can be submitted via email to DHCD.SLP_documentation@maryland.gov or mailed to: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA, Special Loan Programs, 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. Loans are originated, packaged and closed by the Special Loan Program's network of local administering agencies, including county housing and community development offices, nonprofit organizations, and local banks.

structured_extraction.program_description: A local designation program providing community development assistance.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development

structured_extraction.program_description: DHCD-administered grant program funded by HUD's Office of Lead Hazard Control and Healthy Homes to help Maryland homeowners and landlords remove lead hazards from their properties.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $25,000 per eligible property owner for lead abatement services performed by a licensed and accredited lead abatement contractor.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Funding available until April 1, 2029
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners and landlords
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Lead abatement services performed by a licensed and accredited lead abatement contractor
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide, except in the City of Baltimore

structured_extraction.program_name: Lead Hazard Reduction Loan and Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: State-funded program that helps make Maryland homes safer by removing or reducing lead hazards in owner-occupied single family homes and rental properties, including residential buildings and daycare centers.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance provided as either a grant or loan based on the applicant's ability to repay and location. Grants are available in certain target areas with a 20% match requirement for for-profit sponsors and 10% for nonprofit sponsors. Amortizing loans feature interest rates ranging from 0% to 7% with 20-year terms and a maximum of $25,000 per unit. Deferred loans are available at 0% interest for 20 years when underwriting shows no affordability to repay. Maximum annual sponsor amount for grants is $100,000. Loans can reach up to $25,000 per unit. Fees may be included in financing for nonprofits and owner-occupants with limited incomes (less than 80% of Area Median Income), while for-profit sponsors must pay all fees and charges.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of single family homes, landlords with residential rental properties, nonprofit sponsors, for-profit sponsors, licensed residential childcare facilities, and other individuals and non-profit organizations that own residential properties or daycare centers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Lead hazard reduction activities including door and window treatments and replacement; floor treatments; paint removal, stabilization and repainting; encapsulation; enclosure; specialized cleaning; and any innovative lead hazard reduction method approved by the department.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Grants are available in target areas with no income limits. Applicants in areas outside target areas must have household income at or below 80% of statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income. Washington, D.C. PMSA includes Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Montgomery, and Prince George's counties.
requirements_list: Applicants must be Maryland residents if owner-occupants and own and occupy the dwelling as a principal residence
Units must be in need of lead hazard reduction activity
Units must be structurally sound upon completion of lead hazard reduction activity
Units must be registered with the Maryland Department of the Environment Lead Poisoning Prevention Program
Licensed childcare facilities may also be eligible
For grants: applicants must be in a target area or plan to utilize an innovative lead hazard reduction treatment, or underwriting must show no affordability to repay a loan
Household income cannot exceed 80% of statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income (unless applicant qualifies for grant in target area with no income limits)
Clearance testing is required
All contractors must provide current MHIC License or trade license, Certificate of Liability Insurance with minimum $1 million per occurrence limits, Letter of Good Standing, and W-9 form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit completed application and supporting documentation including: income verification documents (paystubs, tax returns, bank statements, or award letters); proof of home ownership (deed, mortgage statement, property tax bill, homeowners insurance); lead-based paint disclosure acknowledgment; critical repairs bid(s) from licensed Maryland contractors (not more than 60 days old, not exceeding $50,000 total); contractor documentation (MHIC/trade license, insurance certificate, letter of good standing, W-9); and demographic data. Applications can be submitted by email to DHCD.SLP_documentation@maryland.gov or by mail to Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA, Special Loan Programs, 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. Contact Special Loan Programs at 301-429-7409, toll-free at 877-218-8101 (Maryland only), or TTY 711/1-800-735-2258 for assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: Infrastructure Financing Bonds created in 2010 provide a way for local governments to finance physical elements that constitute the public service system. Bonds finance loans to local governments with security pledged as a lien on proceeds of bond sales, local obligations, Community Development Administration's right, title and interest in all Infrastructure loans, all revenues and prepayments and pledged funds.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Bonds issued to finance infrastructure loans to local governments, secured by pledge of and lien on proceeds of bond sales, local obligations, and Community Development Administration's right, title and interest in all Infrastructure loans.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financing of physical elements that constitute the public service system for local governments.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Community Development Administration issues tax-exempt bonds on behalf of counties, municipalities and their instrumentalities to finance essential public infrastructure projects. The program provides long-term capital financing with advantageous terms for local governments that do not routinely issue bonds and have limited resources to initiate financing on their own. The program reduces issuance costs through economies of scale and by pooling local demand.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Community Development Administration issues tax-exempt bonds and loans the bond proceeds to local governments. The interest rate on local government loans is subject to market conditions at the time of sale based on the rate attained on the pooled bond issue. Local governments are responsible for repaying the debt and paying their pro-rata share of issuance costs. Loan term is set at the option of the local government but cannot exceed the useful life of the project or thirty years, whichever is less. Financing is available for projects ranging from $150,000 to $10 million or more.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland counties, municipalities, and their agencies with legal authority to construct, operate and maintain projects, pledge security and repay loans, and pledge income tax payments and shared state revenue.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Street lighting, landscaping, sidewalks and public space improvements; public safety vehicles and equipment; water production, treatment, storage and distribution systems; storm water control and sewer collection and treatment facilities; government office and meeting facilities; police, fire, transportation, education, health, recreation, maintenance and other service-related facilities; refinancing of existing debt for eligible projects
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties, municipalities, and their agencies
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland county, municipality, or their agency
Must have legal authority to construct, operate and maintain the proposed project
Must have legal authority to pledge security for and repay the proposed loan
Must have legal authority to pledge income tax payments and various other shared revenue from the State
Project must support an essential physical element of a municipality's public service system
Project must meet federal tax law requirements
Project must be undertaken by or on behalf of a local government, including its agencies
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The local government completes an application that elicits information similar to that which a bond rating agency would require to evaluate creditworthiness. When bonds are issued is influenced by the volume and frequency of participation by local governments. Technical assistance is available through the Community Development Administration to help with application completion. Those requesting technical assistance may submit an Expression of Interest form outlining the proposed project or specific questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program used to direct resources into Project C.O.R.E. investments, supporting low-income housing development.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program to further Maryland's digital inclusion efforts by enabling access to high-speed internet and expanding digital literacy through funding for digital inclusion planning, implementation activities, training programs, and public access computing centers.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Digital Inclusion Planning grants provide financial assistance for up to 50% of the cost of a Digital Inclusion Plan, with a maximum grant request of $30,000 and minimum of $5,000. Digital Inclusion Program Implementation grants provide financial assistance for up to 100% of implementation, expansion, or continuation costs, with a maximum of $75,000 and minimum of $10,000. Individual grant amounts may be reduced based on impact and ability to deploy funds.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Thursday, March 31, 2022
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments (counties and municipalities), nonprofit 501(c) organizations providing services in Maryland, and community-based anchor institutions serving covered populations including low-income individuals, aging individuals, individuals with disabilities, individuals with language barriers, racial or ethnic minorities, and individuals in rural areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Develop digital inclusion plans and implement digital inclusion activities; facilitate broadband adoption by covered populations to provide educational and employment opportunities; implement training programs covering basic, advanced, and applied skills or workforce development programs; construct, upgrade, expand, or operate public access computing centers for covered populations through community anchor institutions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; applicants must provide services within the State of Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local government (county or municipality), a nonprofit IRS-approved 501(c) entity providing services in Maryland, or a community-based anchor institution
For Digital Inclusion Planning: minimum request $5,000, maximum $30,000
For Digital Inclusion Implementation: minimum request $10,000, maximum $75,000
Applications must be fully complete at submission to be considered for funding

Must submit executive summary including project overview, population needs served, potential barriers, partners and local engagement, intended outcomes and metrics, and statement of experience and past accomplishments
Must provide scope of work and detailed budget in specified categories (operations, contracted services, travel, other funding sources)

Must include completed and signed application form, IRS Determination Letter if nonprofit, Certificate of Good Standing verification from Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation, IRS W-9 form, and Dun & Bradstreet DUNS Number
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit all required applications and supporting documents via email to OSB.MD@Maryland.gov. Include completed application form, executive summary, funding scope and budget, IRS determination letter (if applicable), Certificate of Good Standing verification, IRS W-9, and DUNS Number. All applications must be fully complete at submission.

structured_extraction.program_description: The MD-GAPS grant program is designed to assist local jurisdictions, local community-based organizations, non-profits, and anchor institutions in creating Gap Networks and Community Networks. These networks address the affordability challenge many low to moderate income households face in subscribing to the internet by helping communities close existing gaps and lay the groundwork for improved broadband access, adoption, and utilization.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Office will facilitate the award of financial assistance for up to 100% for the construction, deployment, expansion or continuation of community-based gap networks. The maximum grant request amount is $250,000 and the minimum amount is $25,000. Funds are awarded competitively and individual grant amounts may be reduced based on the impact of the applicant's intended population and ability to deploy funds responsibly and as soon as possible.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Thursday, March 31, 2022
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions, local community-based organizations, non-profits, and anchor institutions
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds are used to make available equipment, instrumentation, networking capability, hardware and software, or digital network technology for broadband services to covered populations at low or no cost. This includes building and deploying new gap networks/community networks, upgrading or expanding existing gap networks/community networks, operating and maintaining new or existing gap networks/community networks, and electronics necessary to deliver service to end users including Optical Line Terminals (OLT's), Optical Network Terminals (ONT's), routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radio equipment, antennas, access points, modems, and necessary equipment shelters.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland (statewide)
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local government (Counties or Municipalities), a foundation, corporation, institution, association, or coalition that is a not-for-profit IRS approved 501(c) entity providing services within Maryland, a community-based anchor institution, or other community-based organizations
Must be registered and in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
Eligible projects must be designed to reliably provide a minimum internet connectivity of 100 Mbps down and 100 Mbps up with exceptions as identified in the application guide
All applications must be fully complete at submission to be considered for funding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit a completed application form via email to OSB.MD@Maryland.gov with required attachments including a project summary explaining how the project will close the digital divide, executive summary, statement of experience, network design, community profile, subscriber cost information, potential barriers, partners and local engagement details, intended outcomes and metrics, schedule, and funding scope and budget. Required attachments include the completed and signed application form, IRS Determination Letter for nonprofits, Certificate of Good Standing verification from Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation, IRS W-9 form, and Dun & Bradstreet DUNS Number.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development provides funding to assist Maryland's designated and affiliate Main Street Maryland communities and Baltimore City's designated Main Street neighborhoods in building capacity to achieve their community revitalization and economic development goals in designated Sustainable Community areas throughout the state.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Operating Assistance Grants for Main Street Improvements. Grants can be used for staff and consultant services, general operating expenses, market and business recruitment strategies, marketing and advertising, placemaking initiatives, and other projects identified in the applicant's work plan as key to its Main Street efforts. Grant awards are allocated as follows: Designated Main Street Maryland Communities with full accreditation expected to receive $33,000 each; Designated Main Street Maryland Communities accredited as affiliate expected to receive $25,000 each; Main Street Maryland Aspiring Communities expected to receive $12,000 each. All projects and activities should be completed within one year; a funding match is not required. Final authorization of amounts is contingent upon approval by the General Assembly during the FY2027 legislative session.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, March 20, 2026 at 5:00 PM (EDT)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Designated and aspiring Main Street Maryland communities and Baltimore City's designated Main Street neighborhoods
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grants can be used for staff and consultant services, general operating expenses, market and business recruitment strategies, marketing and advertising, placemaking initiatives, and other operating expenses related to administering the Main Street program. Capital project costs are not supported through MIP. All projects and activities should be completed within one year; a funding match is not required.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland designated and affiliate Main Street Maryland communities and Baltimore City's designated Main Street neighborhoods in designated Sustainable Community areas
requirements_list: Applicant must be a designated or aspiring Main Street Maryland community
Applicants must be in full compliance with all existing award agreements from prior awards, including meeting all reporting deadlines
Projects and activities must align with the applicant's annual work plan
Projects and activities must contribute to the transformation strategy of the community
All projects and activities must be completed within one year
No funding match is required
First-time applicants must contact a project manager for eligibility verification
New organizations should request access and submit organizational documents at least two weeks before the application deadline
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application through the DHCD Project Portal at https://projectportal.dhcd.state.md.us/. Register as a new user first; approval may take up to 72 hours. First-time applicants must contact a project manager for eligibility verification and system access. Ensure your organization profile includes all required documents before submitting your application. Applications missing documents may be disqualified. New organizations should request access and submit organizational documents at least two weeks before the application deadline to expedite processing. Virtual application training is scheduled for Tuesday, March 3, 2026 from 1-2 PM. Individual technical assistance sessions are available by scheduling online via Calendly. Applications must align with the Main Street annual work plan.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program providing support for downtown and main street revitalization.

structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Emergency loans for eligible small businesses and nonprofits to cover renovations, repairs and replacement of furniture/fixtures/equipment, inventory replacement, loss of revenues, operating and leasing expense assistance, and other recovery-related costs including working capital.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Colleen Cord-Malone, Manager II; Aisha K. Taylor, Loan Underwriter
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based small businesses and nonprofit organizations located in commercial spaces affected by disasters.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Renovations, repairs and replacement of furniture, fixtures and equipment, inventory replacement, loss of revenues/operating and leasing expense assistance, and other costs associated with recovery including working capital.
requirements_list: Maryland-based small business or nonprofit organization
Business or organization must be located in a commercial space
Applicant must show proof of insurance status
Business must be located in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Howard County, Frederick County, or Washington County
Must show evidence of damage or loss associated with May 2018 flooding events

structured_extraction.program_description: A credit enhancement program that enables private lenders to establish a loan loss reserve fund from fees paid by lenders, borrowers, and the State of Maryland to support the growth and success of small businesses in Priority Funding Areas throughout Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans ranging from $10,000 to $1,000,000 enrolled with participating lenders. The lender, borrower, and the Maryland Capital Access Program deposit contributions into a reserve account. Typically, the borrower and lender each contribute 1.5 percent and the Program matches that amount with 3 percent, for a total of 6 percent of the original loan amount in the reserve account. Can be used for both lines of credit and term loans.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Most Maryland small businesses, including nonprofit organizations located in Priority Funding Areas
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Project financing for small businesses. Cannot be used to finance passive real estate ownership, residential or transient living facilities, institutional facilities, adult entertainment facilities, check cashing facilities, gambling facilities, liquor stores, massage parlors, pawn or gun shops, tanning salons, tattoo parlors, or for sectarian religious instruction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Maryland's Priority Funding Areas approved by the Maryland Department of Planning for State funding in accordance with the Smart Growth Act of 1997.
requirements_list: Business must be located in Maryland's Priority Funding Areas
Project must be financed through a participating lender
Loan amount ranges from $10,000 to $1,000,000
Borrower and lender contribute fees to reserve account that are matched by the State

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Facade Improvement Program (MFIP) provides funds to local governments and community development organizations for programs to improve the exteriors of commercial properties located within Maryland's Sustainable Communities. The program supports communities seeking to create consistent, attractive designs for their commercial corridors in order to bolster economic vitality and stimulate new private investments. Funds support capital costs related to facade improvements for business buildings and facilities, with local facade improvement programs designed to support the goals identified in the area's Sustainable Communities Action Plan.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Local governments, municipalities, and community development organizations apply for MFIP funding and then capitalize their own local facade improvement program to provide grants to businesses. Eligible businesses receive grants for capital improvements to commercial properties' exteriors. Individual business improvements must total between $1,000 and $50,000 of MFIP funding during a single award cycle. Eligible uses include: signage, exterior painting, storefront reconstruction, siding, exterior lighting, window and door upgrades, public-facing masonry or cornices, murals, removal of unattractive exterior finishes, and roofs. Ineligible uses include interior work, electric charging stations, solar panels, and improvements that have already received MFIP funding within the last 12 months. Predevelopment and operating expenses are ineligible. All projects must comply with the Federal Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation for properties over 50 years old and are subject to Maryland Historical Trust Act review.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, municipalities, community development organizations, and businesses located within Maryland's designated Sustainable Communities. Counties, municipalities, and community development organizations are eligible to apply for MFIP funding. Any department or office of a political subdivision may apply on behalf of its county or municipality. Final recipients of MFIP funding must be businesses located within the State's designated Sustainable Communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital improvements only to the exterior facades of commercial properties occupied by businesses located in Sustainable Communities. Eligible improvements include signage, exterior painting, storefront reconstruction, siding, exterior lighting, window and door upgrades, public-facing masonry or cornices, murals, removal of unattractive exterior finishes, and roofs. Improvements should prioritize aesthetic improvements over routine maintenance and focus on primary elevations of commercial properties. Individual business improvements must be between $1,000 and $50,000 per award cycle. Ineligible uses include interior work, electric charging stations, solar panels, improvements banned by local building codes or zoning, and improvements to vacant properties not seeking an occupancy permit.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in designated Sustainable Communities areas in Maryland. Geographic eligibility can be determined using the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper (MEDUSA). Properties must be within the State's designated Sustainable Communities.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible applicants (local governments, municipalities, and community development organizations) apply for MFIP funding to capitalize their own local facade improvement program. Local programs develop and enforce their own guidelines that comply with program requirements and include criteria for rating and awarding grants to qualified businesses. Applications supported by strong local design guidelines, dedicated staff, and track record of successful revitalization are most competitive. Once funded, awardees develop their programs and manage the grant process for local businesses. All projects undergo historic preservation review coordinated by DHCD staff. For additional information and specific application procedures, contact the Preservation Officer or refer to program guidelines and sample application documents.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides affordable funding to address critical health and safety issues and bring owner-occupied single-family homes into compliance with applicable building codes and standards.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest loans with rates from 0% to 6% based on applicant income and ability to repay. Generally, maximum loan is $50,000 (or up to 110% of home equity, whichever is less). Maximum loan term is 30 years. Loans over $5,000 or with deferred payments are secured by mortgage (deed of trust). Families with income at or below 50% of area median income may qualify for deferred payments. Minimum loan amount is $5,000. No minimum credit score required, but active bankruptcy or foreclosure must be dismissed for minimum 2 years. Maximum initial deposit is 33% of total project cost.

structured_extraction.program_description: A nationwide initiative administered by the U.S. Treasury created under the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act. The program provides federal tax incentives for investment in distressed communities designated as Opportunity Zones over the next 10 years. Maryland has 149 designated Opportunity Zones. The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development administers the program with support from the Maryland Department of Commerce.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three types of federal tax incentives are available: (1) Temporary Tax Deferral - allows investors to defer inclusion in taxable income of capital gains reinvested into a Qualified Opportunity Fund (QOF). The deferred gain must be recognized on the earlier of either the date on which the Opportunity Zone investment is sold or December 31, 2026; (2) Step-Up in Basis - for capital gains reinvested in a Qualified Opportunity Fund, the basis of the original investment is increased by 10% if held for at least 5 years, and by an additional 5% (for a total of 15% basis increase) if held for at least 7 years, thereby excluding up to 15% of the original gain from taxation; (3) Permanent Tax Exclusion - a permanent exclusion from taxable income of capital gains from the sale or exchange of an investment in a qualified Opportunity Fund if held for at least 10 years. Note: The permanent exclusion applies only to gains accrued from the investment in the Opportunity Fund after the initial investment, not to the original capital gains invested.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Investors seeking to invest capital gains in economically-distressed communities designated as Opportunity Zones
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Investment in eligible property located in an Opportunity Zone through a Qualified Opportunity Fund (QOF), which is set up as either a partnership or corporation. Investments can be made in: (1) Stock or Partnership interest in a Qualified Opportunity Zone business, or (2) Qualified Opportunity Zone business property (tangible property used in a trade or business in the QOZ). A QOF must invest at least 90% of its assets into Qualified Opportunity Zone property.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Economically-distressed communities designated as Opportunity Zones in Maryland - low-income census tracts with individual poverty rate of at least 20 percent and median family income no greater than 80 percent of the area median. Maryland has 149 designated Opportunity Zones, with each county in the state having at least one Opportunity Zone.
requirements_list: A Qualified Opportunity Fund must be a corporation (Inc., LLC, S Corp) or a partnership
A Qualified Opportunity Fund must self-certify as a QOF by completing and submitting Form 8996 to IRS
A Qualified Opportunity Fund must invest at least 90% of its assets into Qualified Opportunity Zone property
For a QOZ business: at least 50% of its gross income must be from the active conduct of a trade or business within the QOZ
For a QOZ business: at least 70% of its tangible property must be QOZ business property
For a QOZ business: no more than 5% of its assets can be nonqualified financial assets
For a QOZ business: it may not be a 'sin' business (certain businesses described in Section 144(c)(6))
QOZ business property must be purchased after December 31, 2017

QOZ business property must come into original use with the QOF or QOZ Business or be substantially improved (substantial improvement equals 100% of the value of the assets, excluding land value for real estate)
Capital gains must be invested in a Qualified Opportunity Fund within 180 days of realization
Investment must be held for the applicable period to qualify for tax benefits (5 years for 10% basis step-up, 7 years for additional 5% basis step-up, 10 years for permanent gain exclusion)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Investors must: (1) identify eligible capital gains to defer; (2) establish or identify a Qualified Opportunity Fund (which must self-certify with Form 8996 to the IRS); (3) invest the capital gain amount in the Qualified Opportunity Fund within 180 days; (4) make an election to defer the gain on their federal income tax return (reported on Form 8949). For entities seeking to operate as a Qualified Opportunity Fund: (1) organize as a corporation or partnership; (2) complete and submit Form 8996 to the IRS for self-certification; (3) ensure 90% of assets are invested in Qualified Opportunity Zone property. Investors can claim the deferral on their federal income tax return for the taxable year in which the gain would have been recognized without deferral.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's statewide initiative administered by the Department of Housing and Community Development in partnership with the Department of Commerce and the Maryland Technology Development Corporation. SSBCI is a federal program, administered by the states, that expands access to capital to small businesses. The program supports businesses with limited opportunities for growth, targeting communities and areas with high concentrations of small, micro, and Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individual (SEDI) businesses. The program offers flexible loans to catalyze small businesses across the state, with special focus on projects with significant community impacts, including job retention or creation, child care access, fresh food access, and community revitalization.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_prioritized_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: SSBCI is a direct loan program. Flexible loans with focus on maximizing community benefit. Loan amounts: minimum $500,000 and maximum $5 million. Loan terms: up to 30 years, with senior or subordinate loan positions available. Interest rates determined by underwriting analysis. Requires minimum 1:1 private capital match. Personal guarantees required from owners with greater than 20% equity interest. Adequate collateral required. Total project costs cannot exceed $20 million. Program fees: $250 application fee, $250 closing fee, and 1% origination fee.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses with fewer than 500 employees, micro-businesses, and Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individual (SEDI) businesses with limited opportunities for growth.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Costs to sustain or expand a small business, such as purchasing machinery or equipment, and working capital; and owner-occupied real estate acquisition or renovation (renovation projects must be at least 51% owner-occupied upon completion, and new construction must be at least 60% owner-occupied upon completion). Ineligible uses include: passive real estate (acquiring/holding property for passive investment or renovating space for a third-party tenant); refinancing existing debt with the same lender; tax repayment (cannot pay delinquent federal or state income taxes unless repayment plan is in place, and cannot pay trust/escrow taxes); equity buyouts (cannot purchase ownership interests from current owner except for majority ESOPs or worker co-ops); lobbying activities; federally guaranteed loans (cannot use SSBCI funds to credit-enhance loans already federally guaranteed such as SBA loans); conflicts of interest; and prohibited refinancing of tenant improvement loans from a landlord.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. The program targets communities and areas with a high concentration of small, micro, and Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individual (SEDI) businesses.

structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides tax-exempt bond financing for construction and permanent loans to increase the construction and rehabilitation of multifamily rental housing for families with limited incomes. The program leverages federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits and accepts a variety of financing structures. Financing options include FHA-CDA Risk Sharing, GNMA MBS, Freddie Mac Tax Exempt Loans, Cash Collateral, and FNMA MBS Collateral structures.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax-exempt bonds and notes provide construction and permanent financing. Financing options include: (1) FHA-CDA Risk Sharing (40-year bonds, 40-year amortization), (2) GNMA MBS with 40-year or 17-year bonds and balloon options, (3) Freddie Mac Tax Exempt Loans (17-year terms, 35-year amortization), (4) Cash Collateral/GNMA MBS structures with 2-year construction notes, and (5) FNMA MBS Collateral with immediate or forward start options (17-year terms). Tax-exempt bond final maturity ranges from 17 to 40 years depending on credit enhancement structure, with mortgage amortization periods of 35-40 years. Interest rates are based on Community Development Administration's bond rate plus market adjustments, with estimated all-in permanent mortgage rates ranging from approximately 5.35% to 6.62%. Construction periods typically range from 20-24 months. Loan terms are generally 30 to 40 years for permanent financing. A first lien position is generally required for all bond loans. All loans funded with tax-exempt bonds must comply with federal requirements established for tax-exempt revenue bonds. Bond amounts may differ from loan amounts; Bond proceeds must satisfy the 50% test for Tax Credits and be secured 100% by cash collateral.

structured_extraction.program_name: Multifamily Energy Efficiency and Housing Affordability Program (MEEHA)
structured_extraction.program_description: MEEHA provides funding to reduce electric or gas consumption and greenhouse gas emissions in affordable multifamily rental housing developments. The program supports energy efficiency improvements, electrification measures, and limited health and safety or incidental repairs. It includes two tracks: EmPOWER for broader energy efficiency and affordability, and the Greenhouse Gas Reduction Program (GHGRP) for larger buildings seeking electrification measures. Gas reducing measures are available for properties in Baltimore Gas and Electric Company (BGE) or Washington Gas Light Company (WGL) utility territories. The GHGRP track supports replacing fossil fuel equipment with electric equipment and alternative energy generating systems in buildings with at least 35,000 gross square feet.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant or loan funding. EmPOWER track: Loans offered at 0% interest with deferred payments. Funding provided as work is completed and verified. Minimum 20% of households at 80% AMI or less. Projects with 5+ years affordability qualify for Tier 1; projects with 15+ years affordability qualify for Tier 2 (higher maximum funding). GHGRP track: Grants only, up to $15,000 per dwelling unit with project cap of $1.25 million, provided on reimbursement basis as work is completed. Minimum 51% of units at 80% AMI or less for 15+ years. All projects monitored for affordability compliance throughout the compliance period.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on an ongoing basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of affordable multifamily rental housing developments. GHGRP track requires buildings with at least 35,000 gross square feet of floor area or two or more buildings with combined gross floor area of 35,000 square feet or more.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy conservation and decarbonization measures (ECMs) including energy efficiency or weatherization upgrades to building shell, HVAC or water heating systems, lighting, appliances, and fenestration. Electrification measures replacing fossil-fuel systems with electric-only systems. Limited health and safety or incidental repairs in projects completing measures that reduce electric or gas consumption. Health and Safety measures address indoor air quality (IAQ) and mold issues. Incidental Repair is for work required to allow installation of or protect program-funded energy saving measures. Total funding for Health and Safety and Incidental Repair combined cannot exceed 10% of total energy efficiency funding. Alternative energy generating systems such as solar photovoltaics (GHGRP). Total funding for Electrification Costs cannot exceed 10% of total electrification funding.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide for electric consumption reduction measures. Gas reducing measures available in Baltimore Gas and Electric Company (BGE) or Washington Gas Light Company (WGL) utility territories only. For GHGRP, projects must be Covered Buildings under Maryland Department of the Environment's Building Energy Performance Standards (BEPS).

GHGRP: Minimum 51% of units at 80% AMI or less for minimum 15 years
All building sizes and configurations eligible for EmPOWER including single family units as group project, individually metered, or master metered buildings

Energy audit completed by Qualified Energy Professional (QEP) from DHCD's QEP List for rehabilitation projects; must comply with BPI Multifamily Building Analyst standards
Energy certification review completed by Qualified Energy Professional for new construction projects
Sampling protocol: Inspect sample of units (10% minimum, 5 units minimum, up to 20 units maximum) including one representative unit from each unique type
Ventilation compliance: Post-retrofit condition must meet current ASHRAE 62.2 ventilation standards
Measure costs must be based on actual contractor bids including materials, equipment, and installation
If affordability designation does not exist, Program will create regulatory agreement to be executed and recorded

Complete application package required including: application form, utility bills, consent form, deed with legal description, SDAT ownership/status checks, MBE Plan, ACH Direct Deposit Form, affordability proof, and W-9 Form
GHGRP track: Must set up Energy Star Portfolio Manager account and provide baseline benchmarking report
GHGRP track: Third party verification report required
GHGRP track: Annual energy use benchmarking reports required for minimum of two years after construction completion
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications accepted on an ongoing basis with no set deadline. Process: (1) Owner submits completed MEEHA application package electronically to MultifamilyEnergy.DHCD@Maryland.gov, including application form and all required exhibits; (2) For GHGRP, applicant sets up Energy Star Portfolio Manager account and provides baseline benchmarking report; (3) Owner commissions a Qualified Energy Professional (QEP) from DHCD's QEP List to complete an energy audit for rehabilitation projects or energy certification review for new construction projects; (4) QEP performs comprehensive, unbiased whole building energy audit in compliance with program guidance and BPI standards, including sampling and inspecting representative units and ASHRAE ventilation calculations; (5) QEP completes MEEHA Funding Request using DHCD's Hancock Mobile Intake Tool (MINT, when operational) or DHCD's Rehab Funding Request Form, with owner approval; (6) Qualified Energy Professional submits Funding Request to DHCD on behalf of project owner; (7) DHCD reviews and underwriting process; Department may require additional documents; (8) DHCD finalizes the Funding Request; (9) DHCD creates a funding agreement (grant or loan agreement) to be executed; (10) Project installs funded energy efficiency/greenhouse gas reduction measures; (11) DHCD releases funding after equipment is installed and inspected (or on reimbursement basis for GHGRP); (12) Project enters affordability compliance period after construction is completed and is monitored for compliance; (13) For GHGRP, applicant provides annual Portfolio Manager benchmarking reports for minimum of 2 years post-completion. Utility provider authorization required to release energy use information.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Development Administration issues bonds to fund loans for business projects located in priority funding areas or Sustainable Communities. The Neighborhood Business Loan Program (NBLP), launched in 2017, builds on over 20 years of the Neighborhood BusinessWorks (NBW) small business lending program. Qualified business projects include acquisition and permanent financing of commercial and mixed use real estate, refinance of stabilized commercial and mixed use projects, and non-profit facility loans for acquisition, rehabilitation and new construction. The program is designed as a "gap" lender and uses flexible lending terms. CDA may make senior or subordinate loans, or a combination of both, with the intent to securitize senior loan portfolios as collateral for debt purchasers.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Bond-funded loans for business project acquisition, permanent financing, refinancing, and non-profit facility development in priority funding areas and Sustainable Communities. The program offers competitive financing structures with flexible lending terms. For-profit borrowers require minimum 10% equity contribution; non-profit borrowers require minimum 5% equity contribution. Maximum financing is 90% Combined Loan-to-Value (CLTV) for for-profit borrowers and 95% CLTV for non-profit borrowers. Loans must maintain a minimum 1.50 Debt Service Coverage Ratio (DSCR) throughout the loan life. Upfront costs include 0.5% to 1% upfront financing fee, $25,000 for DHCD legal counsel fee, plus normal real estate and loan closing fees. Annual interest override is minimum 0.60% for debt portfolio administration and investor reporting, plus 0.40% loan servicing and asset management fee. CDA may provide top loss coverage up to 30% of loan value, which can be reinsured by the Maryland Housing Fund (MHF). Senior loan portions are intended to be securitized and sold to private investors.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact the CDA to discuss their business project and eligibility. The program has an online application process to facilitate loan intake and underwriting. All CDA-funded business loans over $250,000 are reviewed and recommended for approval to the Secretary of DHCD by the 5-member NBW Loan Review Committee. All NBLP CDA business loan underwriting is reviewed and recommended for approval to the Secretary of DHCD by the 7-member Housing Finance Review Committee (HFRC). CDA business lending underwriters perform comprehensive loan underwriting for all CDA-funded business loans, subject to internal and external credit committee approval. For non-CDA loans seeking credit enhancement from MHF, CDA staff reviews and approves the external lender underwriting package. Construction projects receive field monitoring by CDA engineering staff, and asset management with quarterly interim financial reviews and annual audited financial statements.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equipment purchases (refrigeration, shelving, etc.), renovation and build-out, facility upgrades, capital needs related to inventory expansion (non-prepared foods), working capital involved with expansion or renovations/construction, and infrastructure/technology for SNAP/EBT setup.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Areas with a Maryland Community Business Compass (MCBC) Fresh Food Gap Score of 60% or higher. Exceptions may be granted on an individual basis. Note: Your business does not need to be listed on the Maryland Community Business Compass to be eligible for the NourishMD grant program. However, if you don't see your business on the Maryland Community Business Compass and would like to add it, please email compass@maryland.gov.
requirements_list: For-profit or nonprofit food retailer
Serve a community with a Maryland Community Business Compass (MCBC) Fresh Food Gap Score of 60% or higher
Operate at least 5 days per week, year round (farmer's markets/on-farm markets exempt from 5-day requirement but must operate year round)
Employ a maximum of 500 workers
Be registered and in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Currently or plan to offer fresh, frozen, or minimally processed healthy foods
Dedicate at least 20% of inventory or food-sales space to healthy food items

Eligible retailers include grocery stores, corner stores, farm stands, farmers' markets, food co-ops, delivery retailers, and small food-focused stores (no more than 25% of gross sales from alcohol/tobacco products)
Provide detailed written plan describing use of grant funds (not to exceed 2 pages)
Provide information demonstrating compliance with healthy food criteria
Submit one year of business tax returns or audited financial statements (or alternative documentation if operating less than one year)
Submit relocation and expansion documentation if applicable (lease agreement, letter of intent, or proof of site control)
A $250 processing fee is required for all applications and may be paid directly from awarded grant funds if approved
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed application through the online application portal. The application period opens January 20, 2026 at 12:00 p.m. EST and closes February 20, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. EST. All required documentation must be included at the time of submission; incomplete applications will not be reviewed until all missing components are submitted and verified. Applications are reviewed February–March 2026 for completeness, impact, and alignment with program priorities. The Review Committee makes funding determinations in April 2026. Award notifications are sent in May 2026, and award agreements begin processing. The Board of Public Works approves grants and disbursements are made in June 2026.

structured_extraction.program_name: Operating Assistance Grants - Technical Assistance Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: The Technical Assistance Grant (TAG) program assists nonprofit organizations and local governments in Maryland engaged in community and economic revitalization efforts. The program provides funding for operating costs associated with administering community and economic revitalization programs, including salaries, professional services contracts, technology costs, and other related administrative expenses.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants provide funding for operating costs related to administering community and economic revitalization programs, including salaries, professional services contracts, technology costs, and other related administrative expenses. Maximum grant request is $50,000 with no required funding match. All projects or activities should be completed within one year. An initial advance of up to 25% of the total award amount is permitted for the first payment request, with no supporting documentation required. Subsequent reimbursements must include evidence of expenditures such as paid invoices, contracts, or other documentation to substantiate reimbursement. A minimum request for reimbursement is $1,000. Awardees are strongly encouraged to enroll in the State of Maryland's Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) payment system.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, March 20, 2026 at 5:00 PM (EDT)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations and local governments in Maryland engaged in community and economic revitalization activities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating costs related to administering community and economic revitalization programs, including salaries, professional services contracts, technology costs, and other related administrative expenses. Projects and/or initiatives should align with local Sustainable Community Action Plans and/or support activities related to capital projects receiving funds from other Department or state agencies. Capital project costs are not supported.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in or serve residents of a Priority Funding Area. Applicants can use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper tool to determine if their organization and/or project/program is in a Priority Funding Area (PFA).
requirements_list: Applicant must be a nonprofit organization or local government engaged in community and economic revitalization activities
Projects must be located in or serve residents of a Priority Funding Area
Projects should align with local Sustainable Community Action Plans or support activities related to capital projects receiving funds from other Department or State agencies
Maximum grant request is $50,000
All projects or activities should be completed within one year
Capital project costs are not supported

Nonprofit applicants must submit evidence of nonprofit status (Bylaws, Articles of Incorporation, IRS Determination Letter), evidence of good standing from Md. State Department of Assessments and Taxation, and evidence of charitable registration from Md. Secretary of State

Current Operating Assistance Grant Program awardees must be in full compliance with all existing award agreements, including meeting all reporting deadlines and submitting required final reports and payment requests
A progress report is required 6 months from the grant agreement execution date or whenever a payment request is submitted
Final report is due no later than 30 days after the award agreement's expiration date
Awardees must draw down at least 50% of awarded funds within six months of award execution and all awarded funds by the agreement expiration date
All project-related records must be maintained for a minimum of three years after the official close-out of the award
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Register as a new user in the DHCD Project Portal at https://projectportal.dhcd.state.md.us/. Registration requests may take up to 72 hours to be approved. New organizations should request access and submit organizational documents at least two weeks before the application deadline to expedite processing. 2. First-time applicants must contact a project manager for eligibility verification and system access. 3. Complete the application online through the DHCD Project Portal by the deadline. 4. Applications are evaluated using a single 5-point scoring scale reflecting the overall strength and readiness of the application (0 = Not Evident, 1 = Minimally Meets Expectations, 3 = Somewhat Meets Expectations, 5 = Strongly Meets/Exemplary). 5. Projects in ENOUGH areas may receive up to 10 bonus points. Projects in Just Communities areas will receive 10 bonus points. 6. Review teams may conduct site visits and/or meetings with applicants. 7. Upon approval, DHCD will notify successful applicants through the Project Portal with official award letters. 8. Award recommendations are subject to review by the Secretary of DHCD and final authorization of award amounts is contingent upon approval by the General Assembly. 9. Awardees execute the Award Agreement through DocuSign within five business days of receipt. The authorized signatory must be the executive director of a nonprofit, the highest elected official of a municipality, or an officially designated representative with documented delegation of authority. 10. Upon execution and satisfaction of all Special Conditions, funds are activated in the Project Portal for award management activities. Virtual training is available on March 4, 2026.
