structured_extraction.program_description: Own Your Future is an initiative of the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) to provide financial assistance to empower small businesses to purchase a property to operate in while generating wealth. Funding for the initiative is provided through the federal State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI) program.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Senior or subordinate loan positions available with flexible loan terms focused on maximizing community benefit. Terms of up to 30 years. Loan amount must be at least $500,000 and no more than $5 million. Interest rates are determined by underwriting analysis. Applicants must provide a minimum of 1:1 private capital match for every dollar of the DHCD loan. Personal guarantees required from all owners with more than 20% equity interest. Total project costs cannot exceed $20 million.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses with fewer than 500 employees seeking to purchase, construct, or renovate commercial real estate.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Costs to purchase, construct, or renovate commercial real estate, including: buying the space where the business currently operates, moving to a new location, purchasing property for the first time (for businesses without a storefront such as e-commerce or food trucks), or buying property as part of an expansion. Renovation projects must be at least 51% owner-occupied upon completion, and new construction must be at least 60% owner-occupied upon completion.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: Business must have fewer than 500 employees
Project is not 100% residential (mixed-use projects may qualify)
Provide a minimum of 1:1 private capital match
Loan amount must be at least $500,000 and no more than $5 million
Personal guarantees required from all owners with more than 20% equity interest
Total project costs cannot exceed $20 million
Renovation projects must be at least 51% owner-occupied upon completion
New construction must be at least 60% owner-occupied upon completion

Business cannot be adult entertainment facilities, check cashing facilities, gambling facilities, gun shops, liquor stores, massage parlors, pawn shops, tanning salons, tattoo parlors, or cannabis businesses
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schedule a consultation or contact DHCD to learn more about the program. Apply online using the application portal at https://apps.dhcd.state.md.us/nbwapplication. Visit dhcd.maryland.gov/Business or email dhcd.businesslending@maryland.gov or call 301-429-7822.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Partnership Rental Housing Program expands the supply of affordable housing for low-income households through partnerships between State and local governments. The program finances new construction and acquisition or rehabilitation of rental housing (apartments, townhouses, single-family homes, single room occupancy buildings, and shared housing facilities) for households with incomes at or below 50% of statewide median income, and for individuals with disabilities or special needs with incomes at or below 30% of Area Median Income.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans for rental housing development with deferred repayment for up to 40 years as long as the local government entity continues to own the housing and rents it to income-eligible households. Loan amounts are limited to $75,000 per unit for large projects and up to $2 million (without a per unit cap) for small projects (40 units or fewer). Loan repayment may be accelerated if income and use restrictions are not maintained. Any profits from sale of the project must be used for other low-income housing purposes.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on rolling basis; contact for additional information
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, housing authorities, entities partially owned by local governments or housing authorities, and non-governmental entities serving individuals with disabilities or special needs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction and acquisition or rehabilitation of rental housing including apartment buildings, townhouses, single-family homes, single room occupancy buildings, and shared housing facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland (statewide), with ongoing funding acceptance and evaluation based on readiness to proceed and availability of funds.
requirements_list: Local government must contribute land or equal value from non-state resources
Local participant must manage the project or arrange for another party to manage it
Resident households must contribute maintenance or other services to the facility, grounds, or neighborhood
Occupants must have gross income not exceeding 50% of statewide median income (or 30% of Area Median Income for disabilities/special needs units)
Tenant Contributed Services must be arranged for occupants (not required for disabilities/special needs units)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Requests for Partnership Rental Housing Program funding are accepted on an ongoing basis. Applications are evaluated and processed based on meeting the program purpose, readiness to proceed, and availability of funding. If requesting Partnership Rental Housing Program funding in conjunction with other department funds, the application requirements and deadlines of the other funding sources must be met.

structured_extraction.program_description: Activates vacant buildings, supports small businesses, creates jobs, improves commercial corridors, and increases local economic activity by providing financial support to place-based economic development organizations working to improve the vitality of Maryland's commercial corridors. Grants target investments to activate vacant spaces in business corridors and support commercial investment in downtowns, Main Streets and other business districts. Designated place-based economic development organizations apply and then sub-grant the funding to businesses for rental assistance, renovation and equipment.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant awards provided to eligible place-based economic development organizations (including nonprofits and local government entities). Funding is provided for operating costs and project activities, up to $300,000 per applicant. Operating funds (up to 15% of grant request) can be used for staff costs, professional services, marketing, and promotion directly related to administering Project Restore 2.0. Project activity funds support activation of vacant commercial properties through: rent payments, interior/exterior renovation, furniture, fixtures, and equipment for small business tenants. Grants are not on a reimbursement basis; funding for operations is provided after award agreement execution, and project activity funding is disbursed when Requests for Payment are approved, which occurs before construction/purchasing begins. Sub-grantees (small businesses) receive support through place-based organizations and can use funds for rent, renovation, and FF&E only. FY2024 total available: $8.0 million. Grant term: June 2024 through December 31, 2025. All funds must be expended and businesses must be operational by grant term end.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY2024 deadline: April 24, 2024 at 5:00 PM EST. Currently closed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Place-based economic development organizations (including nonprofits with specific missions in economic and community development such as Main Street Maryland programs or economic development associations, and local government entities such as towns, cities, or counties). Small businesses are not eligible to apply directly but may receive sub-grants through awarded place-based organizations. Individual nonprofits with missions other than economic development may be eligible as sub-grantees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Place-based organizations may use grants for: (1) Operating costs (up to 15% of award) for staff costs, professional services, marketing, and promotion directly related to administering Project Restore 2.0; (2) Project activity costs at vacant commercial properties including rent payments, interior/exterior renovation, furniture, fixtures, and equipment. Sub-grantees (small business tenants) may use funds for rent, interior/exterior renovation, furniture, fixtures, and equipment only. Ineligible uses include: operating costs for sub-grantees, building acquisition/purchase, new construction, vehicles, water/sewer infrastructure upgrades (other than renovation plumbing), office space for the nonprofit applicant (except if expanding into vacant space in a Sustainable Community), spaces in shopping malls/industrial/office parks, reimbursement for pre-award costs, and short-term pop-ups. Funds are stackable with other State grants.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland. All awarded organizations and vacant properties must be located in DHCD-designated Sustainable Communities.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a place-based economic development organization: a nonprofit with specific mission in economic/community development (such as Main Street Maryland programs or economic development associations) OR a local government entity (town, city, or county). Local governments in every county are eligible.
IRS-determined nonprofit status required at time of application (501(c)(3) status not specifically required). Local governments are automatically eligible.
Organization must have at least 0.5 FTE staff at time of application.
No minimum time-in-operation requirement for nonprofits, but applications scored on demonstrated ability to complete similar projects within grant timeline.

Vacant commercial properties must be vacant at time of application (no executed lease with tenant). No minimum vacancy period required. Property does not need to be entirely vacant; individual vacant suites within multi-tenant buildings are eligible.
All properties must be located in DHCD-designated Sustainable Communities at time of application.

Properties must be in downtown or historic commercial corridors with focus on street-level retail supporting walkable business districts. Spaces in shopping malls, industrial parks, or office parks are ineligible. Shopping center spaces on commercial corridors may be eligible if they improve walkability and street-level retail.
Each eligible entity may submit only one application.

If a nonprofit previously received Project Restore funds in FY22 or FY23, it cannot receive funds for the same property location but may be eligible for expansion to new locations or for different properties if otherwise compliant.
Organization applying must have bylaws and Board/leadership agreement if applying for properties outside typical service geography.
Sublease for vacant space cannot be signed prior to application date.

Legal businesses in good standing with the state are eligible as sub-grantees, including cannabis businesses, boutique hotels, AirBnBs (if business-owned), and art galleries. Landlords may be sub-grantees but lease must specify how Project Restore funds support tenant (rent, fit-out, etc.). Building owner with separate LLC for operating business may be eligible.
Sub-grantee businesses receiving past Project Restore awards are subject to specific eligibility rules regarding location changes, compliance status, and operational history.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through Maryland OneStop portal. Process includes: (1) Pre-application: Organizations should confirm eligibility, identify vacant commercial corridor properties in Sustainable Communities, and gather documentation. (2) Application submission: Provide organization information, strategy for economic development in district, list of specific vacant properties (1-3 properties recommended), property condition assessments with photos, preliminary business/sub-grantee identification, project timeline, budget and funding sources, organizational capacity documentation, and equity framework demonstration. (3) Threshold review: DHCD reviews applications for eligibility on required criteria. (4) Scoring: Applications meeting threshold eligibility are scored by two DHCD staff members on 100-point scale based on organizational readiness, equitable process creation, project alignment with organizational strategy, and advancement of Project Restore 2.0 goals. Applications with highest scores recommended for funding. (5) Award notification and grant agreement execution expected by June 2024 for FY2024 round. (6) Post-award: Awardees must submit Request for Payment/Progress Report for each property (before funds are spent), Completion Report by property when businesses are operational (with U&O permit, photos, receipts, MHT review), and Final Report for organization within 30 days of grant term end. All applications reviewed after deadline; no rolling review. Training sessions offered regionally across state.

The program is designed to be compatible with tax-exempt or taxable bond financing, low-income housing tax credits, and other private or public funds.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans with a term of up to 40 years, bearing interest at 2 percent per annum, repayable from cash flow. Maximum loan amount does not exceed $2 million. Loans may be used for acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, and development costs including lender fees, architectural and engineering fees, market studies, appraisals, legal fees, and other costs directly related to housing development.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Housing Development Programs, Community Development Administration
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit, limited profit, nonprofit developers, nonprofit organizations, county governments, municipalities, and local housing authorities developing rental housing projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, and development costs including lender fees, architectural and engineering fees, market studies, appraisals, legal fees, and other costs directly related to housing development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: New construction projects must be located in Priority Funding Areas.
requirements_list: Eligible residents must have incomes of no more than 60 percent of area median income
Owner must reserve the same proportion of units for eligible tenants as the Rental Housing Program Funds represent of total project financing
Newly constructed or rehabilitated rental housing eligible including congregate housing, single-room occupancy, emergency shelters and shared living facilities
Projects may be restricted to elderly residents
New construction projects must be located in Priority Funding Areas
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted at designated times during the year and are evaluated against criteria established by the Department. Priority is given to projects that restrict units to tenants with incomes below 60 percent of median income, restrict units for more than 40 years, provide tenant service packages, use non-State funds in addition to State funds, provide quality housing in a good location, and are sponsored by teams with demonstrated development and management ability.

structured_extraction.program_description: Rental Housing Works provides subordinate gap financing for the creation and preservation of affordable rental housing financed through the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Multifamily Bond Program and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credit Program. The program creates jobs and strengthens the Maryland economy by bridging financing gaps in affordable housing projects.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Subordinate gap financing loans with a maximum of $2.5 million per project (waivable to the extent necessary to make a project financially feasible and viable as determined by the Department and in accordance with Section 42 of the Internal Revenue Code). Loans feature a 40-year term, 2% simple interest, and payments limited to 75% of annual cash flow during the permanent loan period. Loans are structured as Deed of Trust Notes with Surplus Cash and Contingent Interest provisions. Contingent interest is calculated as a percentage (the greater of the loan's percentage of total project costs or 20%) of surplus cash or borrower net proceeds upon capital events (sale, refinancing, transfer) or at loan maturity. No regular interest accrues during the construction loan period. Principal payments begin during the permanent loan period from surplus cash equal to an applicable percentage (typically 50% until developer fee is paid, then a lower percentage). Payments are made on the first day of specified months. Loans are due upon sale, refinancing, property transfer, or default. Funding comes from State general obligation bonds.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on an ongoing basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers and organizations creating or preserving affordable rental housing projects that also receive financing through the Multifamily Bond Program and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Gap financing for affordable rental housing creation and preservation projects. Funds must be used in conjunction with the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's tax-exempt bonds and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Project must be financed using Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Multifamily Bond Program and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits

Required zoning for use and density of development must be in place at application time with proper documentation (such as a letter from the local zoning office, approved PUD resolution, or local jurisdiction's equivalent)
Award of competitive public and private funding sources necessary for project financial feasibility must have been made
Project's projected Full Time Equivalent must be documented using the Rental Housing Works Full Time Equivalent Job Calculator
Board of Public Works approval required
Projects must meet threshold criteria and scoring requirements for bond loans
Projects must proceed according to agreed-upon processing timeline and schedule
Completed CDA Form 202 must be submitted with RHW funds clearly identified and conforming to RHW limitations
Development or site plan approval is not required at application, but conditional use or special exception approval must be obtained before closing
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis in conjunction with Multifamily Bond Program and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credit applications. Applicants must complete the Application Submission Package with: (1) completed CDA Form 202 identifying RHW funds and conforming to RHW funding limitations; (2) written documentation of required zoning for use and density (letter from local zoning office, approved PUD resolution, or equivalent); (3) evidence that awards of any competitive sources of public and private funding necessary for financial feasibility have been made; (4) completed FTE Job Calculator showing full-time equivalent jobs to be created (an FTE equals 2,080 hours per year); and (5) certification to the RHW Application Submission Package. The standard Application Submission Package for Multifamily Bond Program, LIHTC, and other DHCD funding must be submitted in advance or at the same time as the RHW application. The department tracks applications by date of receipt, reviews them in conjunction with Multifamily Bond Program applications, and evaluates based on threshold criteria and scoring guidelines. Projects that pass threshold are scored using evaluation criteria in the guide. Kick-off meetings are scheduled after scoring is complete. Projects are funded on a 'first-ready, first-served' basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: A loan participation program designed to assist small businesses with working capital and owner-occupied real estate acquisition. The program offers below-market rates and can lend up to $5 million for businesses seeking new locations or expansion opportunities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Senior or junior debt with SSBCI portion ranging from $350,000 to $5,000,000. Up to 30% program match available. Interest rates based on underwriting analysis. Flexible loan terms up to 30 years depending on use and loan amount. Flexible applicant cash contribution required. Personal guarantees and collateral required. May include prepayment lockout period.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses operating in Maryland with less than 500 employees, with priority given to very small businesses (fewer than 10 employees) and SEDI-owned or operated for-profit or nonprofit Maryland-based small businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Owner-occupied real estate acquisition or renovation; mixed-use projects combining residential and commercial uses; machinery and equipment; costs associated with sustaining or expanding a small business in manufacturing, service, retail, office, or mixed-use industries.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business located or to be located in a CDFI Investment area in Maryland.
requirements_list: Less than 500 employees
Proof of private capital match with target ratio of 4:1 (80-20) for non-SEDI/VSB or 2.3:1 (70-30) for SEDI/VSB
Minimum required private capital to SSBCI funds match of 1:1
Personal guarantees and collateral required
Business viability and potential impact on the neighborhood
Readiness to proceed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants complete an SSBCI Neighborhood BusinessWorks loan application package through the online application portal at https://apps.dhcd.state.md.us/nbwapplication. Applicants must register and login to access the application system. Upon submission, applicants receive confirmation and are evaluated based on underwriting guidelines. Upon approval, applicants receive a commitment letter from the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development. Loan approval requires meeting all underwriting guidelines. Applicants must execute necessary legal documents prior to loan disbursement.

structured_extraction.program_name: SSBCI NBW Loan to Lender Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A program designed for Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs) to relend to small businesses. The program provides targeted loans of up to $500,000 combined with required private capital match, with a focus on businesses owned and operated by Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individuals (SEDI), Very Small Businesses (VSB), and those in CDFI Investment Areas. The Maryland Neighborhood BusinessWorks Loan Participation Program (NBWLPP) seeks to establish partnerships with CDFIs as approved lenders to originate and administer small business loans and provide flexible financing for start-ups and new and existing business expansions throughout the State, with a focus on CDFI investment areas.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: CDFIs receive SSBCI Loans ranging from $2,000,000 to $15,000,000 sized based on CDFI capacity. For non-SEDI businesses and those with 10 or more employees, targeted private capital match to SSBCI funds ratio of 4:1 (80% private, 20% SSBCI). For SEDI businesses or those with fewer than 10 employees, targeted private capital match to SSBCI funds ratio of 2.3:1 (70% private, 30% SSBCI). CDFIs must have 20% capital at risk (federal requirement). SSBCI Loans bear interest at 0%-2% with terms up to 7 years and annual renewal options. CDFIs then provide SBLs (up to $250,000 unless prior written approval) to small businesses at interest rates not to exceed 18%, with terms up to 5 years. Individual SBLs to small businesses can include working capital, equipment acquisition, real estate down payments, renovations, and other business expansion costs. Lenders are responsible for origination, underwriting, servicing, asset management, and technical assistance. Applications processed on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing - applications accepted on rolling basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs) serving small businesses owned and operated by Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individuals (SEDI) and very small businesses with fewer than 10 employees located in CDFI Investment Areas. CDFIs must demonstrate financial stability, experience in small business lending, ability to leverage private capital, and capacity to provide technical assistance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: For eligible small business borrowers: working capital, marketing/planning/feasibility studies, real estate acquisition down payment, minor renovations, minor leasehold improvements, machinery and equipment acquisition, and other costs associated with opening or expanding a small business. Ineligible uses include residential/housing businesses, facilities like hospitals or universities, and adult entertainment, gambling, gun shops, liquor stores, pawn shops, tanning salons, or tattoo parlors.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: CDFI Investment Areas in Maryland. Priority given to businesses located or locating in CDFI investment areas.
requirements_list: CDFI status and certification required
Financial stability and good standing with the State and the Internal Revenue Service
Experience in administering a small business loan program including origination, credit and compliance underwriting, loan servicing, post-closing asset management and monitoring
Ability to leverage eligible required private capital as a match to SSBCI funding
Capacity to comply with SSBCI Statutes, Regulations and Policies as well as DHCD requirements
Readiness to provide adequate resources and staff to start making small business loans within 90 days of closing the SSBCI Loan
Ability to provide technical assistance to small business borrowers
Outreach capabilities to very small businesses (VSBs) and socially and economically disadvantaged individual (SEDI) led businesses
Minimum 20% capital at risk (federal SSBCI requirement)
Minimum required private capital to SSBCI fund match of 1:1
SSBCI funding restricted to small businesses with fewer than 500 employees
SSBCI funding capped at $5,000,000; total financing cannot exceed $20,000,000
Ability to originate and fund small business loans with terms up to 5 years at rates not exceeding 18%
Compliance with monthly, quarterly and annual reporting requirements
No discrimination in origination, underwriting, servicing, or administration of loans based on race, color, religion, sex, handicap, familial status, or national origin
Lenders cannot have equity interest or security interest in SBL borrowers
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: CDFIs submit the SSBCI NBW Loan to Lender application (Appendix A) to DHCD at dhcd.ssbci@maryland.gov or to the Department of Housing and Community Development, 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706. The application must include organizational information, description of lending experience and capacity, explanation of how SSBCI funds will be leveraged with private capital, proposed SBL program details with demographic/geographic/industry targets, loan products and terms, outreach capabilities, technical assistance plans, and required documentation (annual report, financial statement, 501(c)(3) documents, last 3 years tax returns). Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis. Once approved, the CDFI receives a commitment letter from DHCD reflecting the SSBCI Loan amount, required private capital match, and proposed funding timetable. SSBCI Loans must be closed in accordance with documentation provided by the Maryland Office of the Attorney General.

structured_extraction.program_description: Section 811 Project Rental Assistance expands affordable housing for low-income adults with disabilities by providing project-based rental assistance tied to specific units in approved rental housing. The program helps eligible residents live in stable housing with access to supportive services. It is authorized under the Frank Melville Supportive Housing Investment Act of 2010 and provides Extremely Low Income Persons with Disabilities and Extremely Low Income households with at least one Person with Disabilities with decent, safe and sanitary rental housing through the use of Rental Assistance Payments to Owners. This federally funded grant is a partnership with the Maryland Department of Disabilities and the Maryland Department of Health.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Project-based rental assistance to subsidize the contract rent of eligible participants. The rental assistance payment is calculated as the difference between the Contract Rent and the Tenant Rent (based on 30% of income or other HUD standards). Section 811 is a rental assistance program, not a loan program. Eligible properties receive project-based rental assistance, and units are rented to eligible adults with disabilities ages 18-61 referred by the Maryland Department of Disabilities. Participating properties must have at least 5 housing units and receive financing from DHCD (through Low-Income Housing Tax Credits, State Rental Housing Funds, or similar programs). Administrative costs are allowable at up to 8% of the rental assistance grant amount.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on rolling basis; contact for additional information
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rental housing projects receiving federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits or State Rental Housing Funds; eligible residents are non-elderly adults ages 18-61 with qualifying disabilities who receive Medicaid and have household income at or below 30% of Area Median Income (extremely low-income households). Property owners and developers of multifamily rental properties with at least 5 units.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental assistance to subsidize contract rent for eligible units in approved rental housing properties. Funds pay the difference between contract rent and the tenant's rent contribution (based on 30% of adjusted income, 10% of gross income, welfare rent for recipients, or $25 minimum rent—whichever is greater). Administrative costs (up to 8% of grant) may support program planning, development, operations, infrastructure, and technology.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Projects must be located in priority funding areas. Applicants may indicate preferences for up to 5 counties of residence.
requirements_list: Projects must receive federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits or State Rental Housing Funds, or financing from DHCD or other approved housing agencies
Properties must have at least 5 housing units
Eligible residents must be between ages 18 and 61 (non-elderly) at time of lease signing
Eligible residents must have a qualifying disability as defined by HUD
Eligible residents must receive Maryland Medicaid and be eligible for community-based long-term services
Eligible residents must have household income at or below 30% of the Area Median Income (extremely low-income)
Eligible residents must be referred by the Maryland Department of Disabilities (MDOD)
Housing must be a rental property (not restricted to persons with disabilities exclusively; PRA units may not comprise more than 20-25% of total units in property)
Properties must meet Uniform Physical Condition Standards (UPCS)
Properties must comply with Fair Housing Act, Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act, Americans with Disabilities Act, and Title VI of Civil Rights Act
New construction and substantial rehabilitation projects must meet energy efficiency and water conservation standards
Units receiving PRA assistance cannot currently have existing use restrictions for persons with disabilities
Units cannot have received project-based Section 8 or other long-term operating housing subsidy within 6 months prior to PRA assistance
Units cannot be subject to use agreements requiring housing for persons 62 or older
Applicants must not be registered sex offenders or have conviction for production of methamphetamine on federally assisted property
Lease agreements must use HUD Section 811 Project Rental Assistance Model Lease
Pre-1978 housing with children under 6 must comply with Lead Safe Housing Rule
Properties must comply with Davis-Bacon wage requirements if 12+ units are assisted and construction is not yet complete
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Program Administration: DHCD administers the Section 811 PRA program in partnership with Maryland Department of Health (MDH) and Maryland Department of Disabilities (MDOD). For eligible residents: 1) Case managers conduct outreach to potential applicants through case management agencies and Medicaid waiver programs; 2) Eligible applicants apply through a web-based Waitlist Registry system (www.socialserve.com) maintained by MDOD; 3) Applications receive date/time stamps upon submission; 4) MDOD Waitlist Manager reviews and approves applications; 5) Referrals are made to available units based on applicant priority category, county preference, and application date/time stamp; 6) Property managers conduct criminal background, credit, and rental history screening; 7) Units are offered to approved applicants with highest priority and earliest application date; 8) Applicants have approximately 2 weeks to complete and submit property applications. For properties/owners: 1) DHCD meets with an Interagency Committee to review projects that align with program goals; 2) Committee includes representatives from MDOD and MDH; 3) DHCD selects projects for participation based on project viability, alignment with state housing initiatives, and likelihood of PRA-eligible tenant demand; 4) DHCD issues a Reservation Award Letter confirming eligibility for funding; 5) Owners execute Rental Assistance Contracts (RACs) with DHCD specifying number of assisted units and payment terms; 6) Use Agreements are recorded on properties; 7) Owners comply with tenant selection procedures approved by DHCD; 8) Rental assistance payments are made monthly through HUD's Line of Credit Control System (eLOCCS) and TRACS system.

structured_extraction.program_name: Shelter and Transitional Housing Facilities Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides capital financing for emergency shelters and transitional housing facilities that provide housing and support services to households to prevent homelessness and assist households to live independently. A "Harm Reduction" approach is strongly considered for supportive services. The Program provides grant funds to nonprofit organizations and local governments for new construction, acquisition, and rehabilitation of housing and for the purchase of capital equipment.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants for new construction, acquisition, rehabilitation of housing, and purchase of capital equipment for transitional housing and emergency shelters with supportive services. Grant funds may cover up to 50% of total project costs generally, or up to 75% under certain conditions. Sponsors must maintain projects as transitional housing or emergency shelter for 15 years or repay the grant. Equipment and furnishings must have a life expectancy of at least 15 years with normal maintenance, be unlikely to become technically obsolete for 15 years, be of durable construction, and be necessary to accommodate the functions for which the structure is intended. Ineligible uses include refinancing existing debt, financing portions of buildings not providing housing for the homeless, financial transaction costs for syndicated sales, replacing furnishings in existing facilities, and providing operating assistance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeless or at-risk homeless households and individuals. Applicants must identify the specific homeless target population they expect to serve (e.g., families, women and children, single males, victims of domestic violence).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction, acquisition, rehabilitation of housing, and purchase of capital equipment for transitional housing and emergency shelters. Eligible activities include: acquiring land and buildings; necessary studies, surveys, plans, specifications, appraisals, environmental impact reports; site preparation; labor and materials for construction and rehabilitation; acquisition of machinery, equipment, and furnishings; architectural/engineering services; and fees and premiums for real estate development including bonds, insurance, and other acceptable costs. Projects may include other uses such as traditional rental housing or nonresidential uses, but Program funds only cover transitional housing units and necessary operating space.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide (Maryland). All projects involving new construction must be located in a Priority Funding Area (PFA), which includes: all incorporated municipalities with some exceptions; all areas between Baltimore beltway and Baltimore City limits and Washington DC beltway and DC boundary; all areas designated as Sustainable Communities; Federal and State enterprise zones; areas designated by county governments as PFAs; and certified heritage areas within locally designated growth areas.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization or local government

Nonprofit organizations that receive Low-Income Housing Tax Credits and form a limited partnership or limited liability corporation to own the project are eligible provided the nonprofit is the sole managing general partner and responsible for project management
Projects must be for transitional housing or emergency shelters
Eligible projects include apartments, condominiums, townhouses, single family detached homes, single room occupancy facilities, and group or shared housing
Supportive services must be provided for residents and must be specifically oriented to meeting the needs of the homeless target population
Residents must be homeless households and individuals (defined as households without permanent housing lacking resources to obtain it and in imminent danger of homelessness)
Applicants must identify the specific homeless target population to be served and continue serving that designated population throughout the 15-year funding term
Local government letter of support required for all projects
Local government letter certifying project location in a Priority Funding Area (PFA) required for all new construction projects
Sponsor must agree to maintain project as transitional housing or emergency shelter for 15 years or repay the grant
Grant funds generally may not exceed 50% of total project costs, or up to 75% under certain conditions
Applicants must submit a plan outlining funding sources for services and operating expenses during the term of the project
Applicants must submit copies of commitment letters, agreements, or other documents identifying sources of funding for services to be provided
Services may not be funded through the Program
Service providers must be identified and any services offered must be clearly defined
All roofing projects must comply with State roofing policy (minimum 20-year, no-dollar-limit warranty for replacement; 60-year life cycle cost analysis for new construction)
Project may not use funds to further sectarian religious instruction or in connection with sectarian religious buildings or programs
Minority Business Enterprises (MBEs) should be solicited and hired for all contracts, with State goal of at least 29% certified MBE participation
Applicant should solicit and hire Maryland resident businesses for project design and construction
LEED green building technologies encouraged
Maryland Historical Trust consultation required; Trust must issue approval letter before State will disburse funds
Forest Conservation Program applies to construction on land greater than 40,000 square feet
All prospective contractors must be checked against debarment list

Equipment and furnishings must have life expectancy of at least 15 years with normal maintenance, be unlikely to become technically obsolete for 15 years, be of durable construction, be heavy enough to prevent easy removal (except chairs), not be intended to replace adequate items already on hand, be necessary to accommodate intended functions, and not be elaborate or extravagant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are subject to threshold requirements and acceptance review. Processing includes underwriting and construction review for projects involving new construction or substantial rehabilitation. The Department will conduct a viability review and commitment review. The Maryland Department of Human Resources' Office of Transitional Services or the Department of Health Office of Health Care Quality will review the adequacy and sufficiency of proposed supportive services programs. Maryland Historical Trust must complete its review and issue approval before funds are disbursed. Department's Construction Management staff will conduct thorough review of all construction-related items for projects involving new construction or substantial rehabilitation.

structured_extraction.program_description: The program preserves and improves single-family properties by bringing owner-occupied homes up to applicable building codes and standards or a minimum housing quality standard. Funding addresses critical health and safety issues including mold, gas leaks, roof repairs, asbestos abatement, lead abatement, plumbing issues, electrical hazards, structural repairs, and accessibility improvements.

Loans in excess of $5,000 or with deferred payments are secured by mortgage. Loans serving families with incomes at or below 50 percent of the statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income may have deferred payments if necessary for project feasibility. The maximum loan term is 30 years. Loans are used for critical repairs and property rehabilitation to address health and safety issues and bring properties into compliance with applicable building codes and standards.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Sustainable Communities Program provides a specific geographic designation for local areas to support community development, revitalization, and sustainability through coordinated strategies. The program gives local governments resources to improve older communities and promote growth that is environmentally, economically and socially responsible. The program combines resources for historic preservation, housing and economic development under a single designation, focusing on infrastructure improvements, multimodal transportation, and development that strengthens existing communities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Sustainable Communities program provides designated communities with access to an interagency revitalization toolbox of financing programs and tax credit incentives. Communities receive designation (valid for five years) that qualifies them for multiple state and federal programs including: Community Legacy Program (capital funding for business retention/attraction, homeownership, commercial revitalization); Neighborhood BusinessWorks (gap financing loans for small businesses and nonprofits); Strategic Demolition Fund (grants for demolition and land assembly); Operating Assistance Grants (grants for operating and technical assistance costs); National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund (funding for grey field development); Seed Community Development Anchor Institution Program (grants/loans for anchor institutions); Main Street Maryland Program (technical assistance and training); Baltimore Regional Neighborhood Initiative (BRNI - additional place-based designation for Baltimore-area communities); Maryland Façade Improvement Program (funds for commercial property exterior improvements); Job Creation Tax Credit (income tax credit with enhanced benefits: $5,000 per job vs. $3,000, with 25 job threshold vs. 60); Enhanced Local Tax Increment Financing (TIF) Authority (expanded use of TIF for historic preservation, environmental remediation, demolition, parking, affordable housing); Low Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC - additional points in application review); Sustainable Maryland Certified (20 points toward 150-point certification); Water Quality Financing Administration Programs (preferential access to revolving loans and grants); State Highway Administration programs (Transportation Alternatives and Safe Routes to School); Sidewalk Retrofit Program (preferred funding for sidewalk construction/replacement); and Kim Lamphier Bikeways Network Program (additional points for bicycle projects).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling applications; new designation applicants must meet with program staff before applying
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments (municipal or county)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The Sustainable Communities designation enables communities to access state revitalization programs and resources for historic preservation, housing development, economic development, infrastructure improvements, multimodal transportation, and strengthening existing communities. Communities with this designation are eligible to apply for certain state programs such as Community Legacy and Strategic Demolition Fund. Designated areas qualify for preferential access or enhanced benefits from multiple state and federal financing programs administered by the Department of Housing and Community Development, Department of Environment, Department of Transportation, and State Highway Administration.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All designated Sustainable Communities must be within a Priority Funding Area and demonstrate a targeted approach toward revitalization. Eligible areas are within or near town centers or transportation centers.
requirements_list: Entire area must be within a Priority Funding Area
Proposed community should be within or near a town center or transportation center

Obtain local government resolution supporting both boundary designation and Action Plan
Proposed Plan must be consistent with other existing community or comprehensive plans
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Schedule a meeting with Program staff (for new designations only) before applying. Request an Application Template by emailing Tynan Stevenson at tynan.stevenson@maryland.gov with subject line 'Sustainable Communities [New Designation or Renewal] Application – [Community Name] - [Sponsoring Jurisdiction]'. 2. Panel presents application to Governor's Smart Growth Subcabinet for final approval. 5. Once approved, designation is valid for five years. Applications accepted on a rolling basis.

structured_extraction.program_name: UPLIFT (Utilizing Progressive Lending Investments to Finance Transformation)
structured_extraction.program_description: UPLIFT is a public-private partnership that increases homeownership opportunities in underserved areas by covering the appraisal gap—the difference between the cost to develop a property and its market sale price. The program funds qualified development teams to acquire, develop, build, and sell quality affordable housing in low-income census tracts and designated Sustainable Communities, with state funding covering the gap between construction costs and affordable sale price. UPLIFT also strengthens neighborhoods by encouraging social connections among residents and supporting Legacy Homeowners in designated areas.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: UPLIFT provides gap financing in the form of soft promissory notes to cover the difference between the cost to build or renovate a property and the price at which it can be sold on the market. This allows developers to build and sell quality affordable housing in communities affected by redlining and disinvestment. The State covers the appraisal gap through UPLIFT funding, which is deployed as loans. The developer receives gap financing to make the property economically viable for affordable sale. Homebuyers acquire fee simple title using a combination of down payment, down payment assistance, first mortgage loans (including Maryland Mortgage Program), other acceptable subsidies, and a soft promissory note from the Department. For projects in ENOUGH Areas or Just Communities, enhanced terms may be available.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis, reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis as long as funding is available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit and for-profit developers and builders, community-based organizations, public housing authorities, local jurisdictions, and other entities working on residential development projects in targeted low-income areas and historically redlined communities. Projects must demonstrate capacity to successfully execute and have acceptable site control.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Gap financing for acquisition, development, construction, and sale of quality affordable housing in targeted neighborhoods. Funds cover the difference between development costs and market sale price to make affordable housing economically viable in historically redlined communities. Funds can support new construction or substantial rehabilitation of vacant or dilapidated properties in low-income census tracts designated as Maryland Sustainable Communities. Additionally, UPLIFT supports neighborhood engagement and may coordinate with other DHCD programs to strengthen communities and support Legacy Homeowners.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Low-income census tracts (50% of households with incomes below 60% of Area Median Income or poverty rate of 25% or more) and designated Maryland Sustainable Communities in Maryland. Specific qualified areas are identified in the UPLIFT Qualified Areas Map at: UPLIFT Qualified Areas (arcgis.com). New construction projects cannot be located in FEMA Flood Zone Areas unless a waiver is approved with appropriate documentation or mitigation plans.
requirements_list: Projects must be located in both a Low-Income Census Tract and a Maryland Sustainable Community area
Projects must be composed of newly constructed or formerly vacant structures to be substantially rehabilitated
Development team must include Lead Developer with controlling position and demonstrated experience comparable to proposed project scope

Each primary team member (developer, general contractor/builder, architect, Neighborhood Engagement Facilitator, marketing/sales entity) must have significant participation experience in comparably scaled projects
All corporations, LLCs, or limited partnerships must submit audited, reviewed, or compiled financial statements prepared per GAAP
Individuals providing guarantees must submit personal financial statements
Lead Developer must be ultimately responsible for successful project completion
Development team must have acceptable credit history and current financial capacity to execute the project
Projects must meet all threshold criteria including site control, zoning compliance, environmental assessments, utilities, and appraisal requirements
Marketing and sales must include affirmative fair housing practices and homebuyer acquisition strategies
Projects must address neighborhood engagement and community connections
New construction projects must not be located in FEMA Flood Zone Areas (Zone C and X require waivers with engineer documentation or flood mitigation plans)
Construction must meet one of the following energy/environmental standards: EPA Energy Star/WaterSense/Indoor AirPlus, Enterprise Green Communities, LEED, NGBS Green Promise/Earthcraft

Development costs and fees must be reasonable and meet underwriting limits; construction cost limits are currently $190/SF for new construction and $195/SF for rehabilitation (cottage, single family, semi-detached, townhomes)

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 0: Review UPLIFT Program Guide, compile project details and timelines, schedule and complete Pre-Application Meeting, submit pre-application materials at least two business days before meeting. Step 1: Complete UPLIFT Electronic Application Submission Request Form to receive Dropbox folder access. Step 2: Download Application Documents Package from UPLIFT website and complete all seven application parts: (1) General Elements, (2) Development Team, (3) Project Economics, (4) Project Location/Area, (5) Design and Construction, (6) Marketing and Sales, (7) Neighborhood Engagement. Step 3: Submit $1,000 non-refundable application fee per project via ACH or check to DHCD Central Cashier (proof of payment required with application). Step 4: Upload all application documents to Dropbox in correct subfolders, complete and sign Final Submission Checklist, and verify all documentation is current (usually within 12 months). Step 5: Submit applications both electronically (via Dropbox) and physically (hard copy to Brien O'Toole, 7800 Harkins Rd, Lanham, MD 20706; notify UPLIFT team of expected arrival date). Applications must include two complete copies with all attachments and exhibits; materially incomplete applications will not be evaluated. Step 6: DHCD conducts threshold review to ensure compliance with all threshold criteria; if materially incomplete or unable to meet criteria, Department will contact applicant to discuss and advise on curing issues. Step 7: Applications passing threshold review are scored against Evaluative Criteria in five areas: Development Team Experience/Capacity, Project Impact, Leveraging Resources, Readiness to Proceed, and Design Quality. Step 8: Project Kick-off Meeting generally held 45-60 days after complete application submission to determine underwriting schedule. Step 9: Final Underwriting Submission (FUS) using prescribed packages updating financing, design, construction, and marketing elements. Step 10: Internal UPLIFT Loan Committee reviews and makes recommendation to Secretary; Housing Finance Review Committee (HFRC) provides approval. Step 11: If recommended for approval, Secretary issues Commitment Letter specifying terms and conditions for closing. Step 12: Secretary's determination authorizes commitment and investment of resources; Office of the Attorney General coordinates closing. Step 13: Initial financing closing with satisfactory submission of closing checklist items. Step 14: Construction Kick-off Meeting shortly after closing and Notice to Proceed issuance to coordinate construction phase processes, marketing, and occupancy requirements. Projects that do not continue to meet Threshold Criteria or materially change from approved underwriting may be withdrawn from processing. Applicants rejected may request reconsideration in writing within seven calendar days to Director of Community Development Administration.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally-funded program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development that provides weatherization services to eligible low-income households across Maryland. Services are delivered through a statewide network of Local Weatherization Agencies and subgrantees, including Community Action Agencies, nonprofits, and local governmental agencies. The program reduces energy costs for low-income families by increasing the energy efficiency of their homes through installation of energy conservation measures using advanced technologies and testing protocols, while also addressing health and safety issues. Services are provided through local weatherization agencies in each territory.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides energy-conservation improvements and weatherization services at no cost to eligible households. Services include comprehensive energy audits, blower door air infiltration reduction, insulation in attics/floors/walls, hot water system improvements, high-efficiency HVAC installation or repair, furnace cleaning/tune-up, lighting retrofit to energy-efficient fixtures, safety repairs, and health and safety items. Additional services may include weatherization readiness funds to address deferral conditions (structural repairs, plumbing/electrical/heating issues, moisture/mold problems, pest infestations, and other health/safety conditions) before weatherization work commences. Average cost per unit under DOE Formula funding is approximately $7,496; under BIL funding approximately $6,000. All work includes 100% quality control inspections and comes with a one-year warranty on labor and materials.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-eligible homeowners and renters in Maryland, with priority given to individuals over 60, those with disabilities, those with children in the home, and households with high energy usage or energy burden. Contractors, nonprofits, and local government agencies also participate as service providers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Weatherization services and energy efficiency improvements including: energy conservation measures such as air sealing, insulation, heating and cooling system repairs or replacements, water heater improvements, lighting retrofit, furnace repairs and replacement, health and safety improvements, and weatherization readiness activities to address deferral conditions. Funds may also be used for training and technical assistance to subgrantees, program administration, and monitoring activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide through local weatherization agencies. Service areas are divided among eight regional local weatherization agencies serving 23 counties and Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Household income must not exceed 60% of State Median Income (SMI) or 200% of Federal Poverty Level (FPL), whichever is higher
Automatically income-eligible if currently receiving Utility Bill Pay Assistance through OHEP, SNAP, TANF, SSI, or HUD housing assistance programs
Automatically income-eligible if received assistance under SSI, TANF, or MEAP within the last 12 months
Must be a Maryland resident
Must submit an application to apply for services
Household must own or occupy a dwelling unit in Maryland
Property owners must enter into written contracts with the local weatherization agency for work to be completed
For DOE WAP: subgrantees must be a Community Action Agency or other public or nonprofit entity as recognized by federal and state laws
For DOE WAP: nonprofit organizations must have an active board of directors and be organized in accordance with applicable Maryland laws
Subgrantees must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) and provide a valid UEI number
Subgrantees must maintain active SAM registration with current information during the period of federal award or application
Energy auditors must be certified building science professionals (BPI certification required)
All weatherization work must comply with Standard Work Specifications (SWS) and Maryland's field guide standards
For multifamily buildings (5+ units), Davis-Bacon Act compliance applies; such buildings cannot be serviced with Bipartisan Infrastructure Law (BIL) funds but can receive regular annual DOE WAP funds
Health and safety conditions must be addressed appropriately; homes may be deferred if conditions cannot be resolved in a cost-effective manner
For at-risk occupants (with medical conditions documented by a physician), additional measures such as air conditioning installation may be allowable when other funds are leveraged
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your Local Weatherization Agency (LWA) to submit an application or complete an interest form through the DocuSign form. Contact information is available through the Department's website or by calling the main program phone line. Once eligibility is determined, the local agency will schedule an energy audit inspection to identify necessary energy-conservation improvements. The application must be certified by the local agency. After certification and approval, an energy audit is conducted within 30 days. Based on audit results, a work plan is developed and work is completed according to program standards. 100% quality control inspections are performed on all completed units. Clients determined to be ineligible or whose homes are deferred due to health and safety conditions may appeal the decision to a higher level within their local agency. Re-certification of applications is required if more than 12 months have passed without beginning work. Applications are accepted on a continuous basis during the funding period.

structured_extraction.program_description: Apprenticeship Maryland is a Career and Technical Education (CTE) program of study for students ages 16 and older, designed to prepare students for sustainable employment and further education. The program is piloted in Frederick and Washington Counties and is now being made available to all school systems for adoption. Participating students start in their junior year and complete at least one year of related classroom instruction and a minimum of 450 hours of work-based training under the supervision of an eligible employer. Students receive paid, mentored work experience with a work-based learning plan and formal agreement among the student, school, and employer. Career pathways include Manufacturing and Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) related fields as well as traditional occupations.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Students receive a minimum of 450 hours of paid on-the-job training (OJT) and at least one year of related technical instruction (RTI). Students are paid at least minimum wage. Upon completion of all program requirements, students receive a State Skill Certificate signed by the Secretary of the Maryland Department of Labor. Programs are approved by the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Council (MATC) and delivered through a registered Apprenticeship sponsor in partnership with local school districts. Students receive credit to meet high school graduation requirements and can receive a jumpstart into an existing adult apprenticeship or fulltime employment. Adult apprentice programs may include help with college tuition.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Secondary students ages 16 and older seeking paid career-connected learning opportunities starting in their junior year, and adult apprentices
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paid on-the-job training and related technical instruction in registered apprenticeship positions across Manufacturing, STEM, and traditional occupations

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For students and families: Talk to your school's Apprenticeship Maryland coordinator or career-connected learning coordinator to explore opportunities, eligibility, and scheduling. Once selected for a position, the coordinator ensures the Youth Apprentice Agreement is complete and signed by all parties. For employers: Work with a Maryland Department of Labor Navigator to complete and submit the Eligible Employer Application to the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Council (MATC). Provide an opportunity for Labor and school representatives to visit the work site. Obtain Labor approval before hiring youth apprentices. Employers must interview and hire youth apprentices for a minimum of 450 hours, pay at least minimum wage, identify required skills and knowledge, provide instruction in required competencies, provide safety instruction, assign mentors and skilled trainers, allow release time for mentors/trainers to attend relevant trainings, comply with Youth Apprenticeship Agreement requirements, and comply with all applicable state and federal child labor laws.

structured_extraction.program_name: Broadening Options and Opportunities for Students Today (BOOST) Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The BOOST Scholarship Program provides scholarship awards for students who qualify for free or reduced-price school meals (FARMs) to attend a participating nonpublic school. Priority is granted to students who qualify for FARMs and received a BOOST scholarship award during the previous school year, as well as their siblings. During the 2025-2026 school year, scholarship awards were granted to nearly 2,800 low-income students across 19 jurisdictions in Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarship awards sent as checks to participating nonpublic schools to credit students' tuition. Award amounts depend on household income (expressed as a percentage of federal poverty level), academic level, financial assistance provided by the school, and available funding. The BOOST Advisory Board determines base award amounts and additional awards for students receiving special education services. Awards cannot exceed the tuition owed after accounting for any school-provided discounts and any other financial aid the student receives. For fiscal year 2027, approximately $9,000,000 in funding is available for an estimated 2,500 scholarship awards.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Nonpublic school applications: March 6, 2026. Parent applications: May 8, 2026 (no later than 11:59 p.m. EDT) for the 2026-2027 school year.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Allison Sanborn, Program Manager; James Clark, Administrative Support
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students who qualify for free or reduced-price meals (FARMs) and are entering grades kindergarten through 12th grade (Pre-K students are not eligible) at participating nonpublic schools in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and required fees for enrollment at participating nonpublic schools. Funds may not be used for transportation or meals. The scholarship award may be reduced if it exceeds the tuition owed to the school after accounting for school-provided discounts and other financial aid.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland. Participating nonpublic schools are located in 19 jurisdictions across Maryland (approximately 178 schools).

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Nonpublic schools submit online applications by March 6, 2026 to confirm participation through Submittable. 2. Parents/guardians complete the online BOOST Scholarship application by May 8, 2026 through Submittable, providing child information and uploading 2025 Federal 1040 tax returns. 3. MSDE reviews applications for eligibility and completeness on a rolling basis. 4. After May 30, 2026, all application data is compiled and ranked by household income as a percentage of federal poverty level and submitted to the BOOST Advisory Board. 5. The BOOST Advisory Board convenes in summer 2026 to determine award values and any special education awards. 6. Eligible parents/guardians receive notification by email of award offers and must accept or decline by the deadline. 7. Participating schools confirm student enrollment and upload required documentation (IEP, IFSP, or 504 Plan if applicable). 8. MSDE prepares scholarship checks which are printed by the Office of the Comptroller of Maryland. 9. Schools receive FedEx shipments with checks for confirmed students. 10. Parent/guardian must endorse the back of the check at the school. 11. The scholarship check is deposited by the school to the student's tuition account. Awards continue to be offered as parents decline, with the final deadline for new awards being December 11, 2026.
