structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education
structured_extraction.assistance_description: LEAs reserve 15 percent of IDEA Part B Section 611 and Section 619 funds to provide educational and behavioral evaluations, services, and support including evidence-based literacy instruction; professional development and educational and behavioral evaluations, services, and supports; and to address factors and policies contributing to significant disproportionality. Funding supports systemic awareness, stakeholder engagement, self-assessment, root cause analysis, implementation drivers (staffing, training, coaching, consultation, performance evaluation, data systems), job-embedded professional learning, comprehensive evaluation systems, and strategic expenditure planning. Allowable costs include coaching and mentoring services, extended contracts/hours for staff, general education teacher salaries for intervention delivery, guidance counselor and school psychologist salaries for behavioral interventions, professional development services, RTI/MTSS coordinator salaries, social worker salaries, substitute teacher salaries, staff travel, tutoring services, computing devices for intervention delivery, instructional materials and software for interventions (not core curriculum), and special education teacher salaries for Tier 2 and Tier 3 interventions. Non-allowable costs include student transportation, core curriculum activities, universal screening costs, special education eligibility evaluations, occupational/physical therapy services, office equipment, furniture, rent/occupancy costs, and alternative education programs that replace core programming.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Gary W. Richardson, MBA, Branch Chief, Resource Management and Monitoring; Demetria White, Interagency Specialist
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local education agencies (LEAs) in Maryland identified by the State as having over-identification of students with disabilities by racial or ethnic group in identification, placement, or disciplinary removals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational and behavioral evaluations, services, and support including evidence-based literacy instruction; professional development; addressing root cause factors contributing to significant disproportionality; systemic awareness and leadership development; stakeholder engagement; self-assessment and data review; proactive and responsive action planning; implementation drivers including staffing, training, coaching, consultation, staff performance evaluation, data systems, progress monitoring, and fidelity evaluation; results-based and job-embedded professional learning; comprehensive evaluation of plan outcomes; and aligned expenditures. Not permitted: student transportation, core curriculum activities, universal screening for all students, special education eligibility evaluations, occupational/physical therapy for related services only, office equipment, furniture, rent or occupancy costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: LEA must be identified by the State as having one or more subgroups of students evidencing a risk ratio of greater than 2.0 for two or more consecutive years (unless the risk ratio declines by a defined amount of 0.15 if less than 4.0 and 0.5 if over 4.0 from one year to the next)
LEA must address factors contributing to the significant disproportionality
LEA must address and review a policy, practice, or procedure identified as contributing to the overidentification
LEA must reserve 15 percent of IDEA Part B Section 611 and Section 619 funds for CCEIS
LEA must build systemic awareness and leadership supports through a local implementation team
LEA must establish a diverse stakeholder group inclusive of external and internal partners
LEA must engage in self-assessment and data review to determine root cause factors
LEA must identify structure of results-based and job-embedded professional learning experiences
LEA must develop comprehensive system for evaluation of plan outcomes with emphasis on fidelity and measurable student outcomes
LEA must align projected expenditures with specific actions to mitigate root cause factors

LEA must complete a self-assessment tool recommended by MSDE (such as IDEA Data Center Equity, Inclusion, and Opportunity Rubric; Addressing Root Causes of Disparities in School Discipline; or Assessing and Improving Special Education Program Review Tool)
LEA must submit programmatic and fiscal documentation including MSDE Grant Budget C-1-25 forms and Budget Detail Forms
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Identification: LEA is identified as having significant disproportionality by the Maryland State Department of Education based on risk ratio data (greater than 2.0 for two or more consecutive years) in identification, placement, or disciplinary removals of students by racial or ethnic group. 2. Plan Development: LEA develops comprehensive CCEIS Plan including formation of Local Implementation Team with diverse stakeholders; completion of self-assessment using MSDE-recommended tool; root cause analysis examining decision-making processes and procedures; and development of Planned Response Actions (PRAs) addressing identified root causes. 3. Plan Components: Plan must include data analysis tables, narrative self-assessment findings, identification of specific schools/regions with disproportionality, PRAs with measurable goals and interim benchmarks, detailed budget with allowable costs, and supporting fiscal documents (MSDE Grant Budget C-1-25 and Budget Detail Forms). 4. Submission and Approval: LEA submits complete plan package with required signatures from Local Director of Special Education, Chief Academic Officer, Finance Officer, and Superintendent, along with MSDE signatures from Equity Specialist, Programmatic Liaison, Fiscal Liaison, and Resource Management and Monitoring Branch Chief. 5. Reporting: LEA submits Interim Progress Reports (January 31 following interim reporting period) and Final Progress/Cumulative Variance Report (November 30) documenting intervening supports provided, progress toward measurable outcomes, and budget expenditures. 6. Amendments: LEA may submit programmatic amendments throughout the year if activities require revision based on progress monitoring data, with updated budget documentation and all required signatures.

structured_extraction.program_description: The CCEIS program provides guidance and resources to local education agencies for developing early intervention services plans that coordinate comprehensive services for students identified as in need of intervention to prevent referral to special education. LEAs identified by the State as having significant disproportionality must reserve 15 percent of IDEA Part B Section 611 and Section 619 funds to implement a comprehensive system of proactive and responsive actions to address root cause factors contributing to significant disproportionality with respect to identification, placement, and/or disciplinary removals.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education
structured_extraction.assistance_description: CCEIS is a federally mandated program requiring Local Education Agencies (LEAs) with significant disproportionality to reserve 15 percent of IDEA Part B Section 611 and Section 619 funds. These funds support a comprehensive system of proactive and responsive actions addressing root causes of significant disproportionality in identification, placement, and disciplinary removals. Funds may be used for professional learning and job-embedded coaching for staff, implementation of academic and behavioral interventions, review and adjustment of policies and procedures, and monitoring of implementation. Allowable costs include coach/mentor salaries (non-instructional), extended contracts for staff, general education teacher salaries, professional development services, RTI/MTSS coordinator salaries, substitute teacher salaries, tutoring services, instructional materials and software (for intervention delivery only), and computing devices for intervention delivery. Unallowable costs include core curriculum, universal screening, student transportation, special education evaluations for eligibility, furniture, and rent/occupancy costs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 11, 2025 (Self-Assessment Section Only); July 15, 2025 (SFY2026 Full Plan Submission); No later than May 15, 2026 (SFY2027)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local Education Agencies (LEAs) identified by the State as having significant disproportionality in identification, placement, and/or disciplinary removals of students by race/ethnicity. LEAs must engage diverse stakeholder groups including district and school-level administrators, special education and general education coordinators, school-based staff, parents, and community members in plan development and implementation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: CCEIS reserved funds must be used to identify and address factors contributing to significant disproportionality for identified categories of analysis. These factors may include lack of access to scientifically-based instruction, economic/cultural/linguistic barriers to appropriate identification or placement, inappropriate use of disciplinary removals, lack of access to appropriate diagnostic screenings, and differences in academic achievement levels. Funds serve two groups: (1) children not currently identified as requiring special education but needing additional academic and behavioral support in general education, and (2) children currently identified as requiring special education or related services (funds cannot be used exclusively for this group). Activities must include review and/or adjustments to policies, procedures, and practices; identification of academic and/or behavioral interventions as preventative or corrective actions; and professional learning and job-embedded coaching for personnel capacity-building.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland - applies only to Local Education Agencies identified by the Maryland State Department of Education as having significant disproportionality or at-risk populations; available to all Maryland counties
requirements_list: LEA must be identified by the State as having significant disproportionality (risk ratio greater than 2.0) in identification, placement, and/or disciplinary removals by race/ethnicity, or be addressing at-risk areas proactively
Identify and engage diverse stakeholder group for plan development and implementation team

Conduct programmatic self-assessment and root cause analysis using an MSDE-approved self-assessment tool (IDEA Data Center Success Gaps Rubric, National Center on Safe Supportive Learning Environments Disciplinary Disparities Risk Assessment Tool, or WestEd Program Review Tool)
Complete analysis of data from multiple sources including process implementation fidelity data, historical trend data, and other recent system data
Determine root causes supported by data and within LEA control
Identify specific schools/feeders/regions for focused support based on data analysis

Develop Planned Response Actions addressing all identified root causes, including review/adjustment of policies and procedures, implementation of academic and/or behavioral interventions, and professional learning/job-embedded coaching
Submit self-assessment section by April 11, 2025 for approval before proceeding with full plan development

Submit complete CCEIS Plan by July 15, 2025, including approved self-assessment, all Planned Response Actions, CCEIS Plan Map, budget tables, and required MSDE budget documents (Grant Budget C-1-25 and Budget Detail Form)
CCEIS declaration form submission indicating whether LEA opts to combine 611 and 619 CCEIS funds
Establish LEA Implementation Team meeting at minimum quarterly frequency
Ensure all proposed activities align with approved root causes and categories of analysis
Monitor progress toward addressing root causes using specified data sources and tools
Time and effort records must be kept if special education staff deliver Tier 2 and Tier 3 interventions
Local system must track computing devices and ensure usage aligns with approved CCEIS Plan narrative and budget
Local system must determine allocable costs when software includes both universal screening and intervention components
Notify MSDE regional fiscal liaison upon plan submission
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. BEFORE DEVELOPMENT (Ongoing): Identify and engage diverse stakeholder group; gather and summarize data; select and complete MSDE-approved self-assessment tool; analyze data to determine root causes. 2. DURING DEVELOPMENT AND SUBMISSION: Draft self-assessment narrative; identify schools/feeders for focused support; identify possible responses aligned with root causes; determine feasibility of implementation; finalize proposed responses; determine measures and tools for monitoring progress; determine costs and funding sources; check allowability of costs; describe costs in plan aligned with activities and root causes; submit plan to MSDE secure server. 3. AFTER SUBMISSION: Notify LEA's MSDE regional fiscal liaison of completed submission; engage with MSDE for feedback and revisions; resubmit within agreed timeline; receive final approval notification to Special Education Director. LEAs develop CCEIS plans following state guidance and template, submit CCEIS Declaration Form indicating whether LEA opts to combine 611 and 619 CCEIS funds. Key submission dates: April 11, 2025 (Self-Assessment Only), July 15, 2025 (Full Plan SFY2026), May 15, 2026 (SFY2027). MSDE provides feedback, technical assistance, and approval throughout process. All submissions uploaded to MSDE Secure File Transfer site (MOVEit).

structured_extraction.program_description: Farm to school enriches the connection communities have with fresh, healthy food and local food producers by changing food purchasing and education practices at schools and childcare sites. The program includes procurement of local foods, education initiatives related to local foods and nutrition, and hands-on school gardening experiences. The program promotes healthy eating habits among students and the community, supports local farmers (particularly those who have been historically disadvantaged), influences economic development in Maryland's regions, and fosters environmental stewardship.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program facilitates local food procurement, educational opportunities, and school gardening initiatives through multiple support mechanisms. It provides competitive grants for training, operations, planning, school garden development, and partnership building. The program offers a 5% price preference for locally-grown foods, allowing schools to purchase local products that cost up to 105% of the lowest responsible bid. Technical assistance is provided to farmers interested in selling to schools through a database of participating producers. The program was developed with support from a 2021 U.S. Department of Agriculture grant to enhance local food integration into school meals and has been legislated in Maryland since 2008. Key support includes the Jane Lawton Farm to School Program, which promotes the sale of Maryland-grown farm products to schools and encourages school meals and classroom programs related to agriculture and nutrition.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local Education Agencies (school districts) and childcare sites seeking to integrate local food procurement and educational opportunities, particularly those in low-income neighborhoods and schools serving diverse populations
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Local food procurement for school meals and childcare sites, educational programming related to local foods, gardening, nutrition and cooking, school garden development, training and technical assistance for producers, school garden development, and partnership building
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland; local sourcing considered within Maryland or potentially within 400 miles of the Maryland delivery site
requirements_list: LEA must be interested in procuring local foods for school meals
Producers must be farmers/ranchers operating in Maryland or within 400 miles
GAP (Good Agricultural Practices) certification may be required by some LEAs
Commitment to include local foods in school meals regularly and consistently, beyond special tastings
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools and producers interested in participating should contact the Maryland State Department of Education, Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs. The program facilitates connections between local producers and schools through a database of farmers interested in selling their products to schools. Local Education Agencies work with local producers to establish purchasing agreements and incorporate local foods into meal planning. Technical assistance is available to both schools and farmers to support implementation.

This program provides United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) food items to eligible schools and child care facilities, including public schools, private non-profit schools, and residential child care institutions.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: USDA provides domestically grown and produced foods to schools at reduced cost, reducing school food expenses by approximately 20%. structured_extraction.program_name: IDEA Part B Local Application for Federal Funds (LAFF)
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal grant that requires each Maryland local education agency (LEA) and public agency (PA) to develop and submit an application for the expenditure of federal funds in support of special education to provide a free appropriate public education (FAPE) for children and students with disabilities. The LAFF ensures that all children with disabilities have available to them special education and related services designed to meet their unique needs and prepare them for further education, employment, and independent living.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Formula-based federal IDEA Part B Section 611 (Grants-to-States for school-age children ages 3-21) and Section 619 (Preschool Grants for children ages 3-5) funds provided to LEAs and public agencies. Funds must be used to pay excess costs of providing special education and related services to children with disabilities, including personnel development, instructional support delivered in various settings, technology for case management, and special education in accordance with students' Individualized Education Programs (IEPs). Funding allocations vary by LEA/PA based on formula. Funds must supplement, not supplant, state and local education funding.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: May 15, 2026, no later than 5:00 p.m. EDT
structured_extraction.contact_name: Gary W. Richardson, MBA, Director, Resource Management & Monitoring
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland local education agencies (LEAs) and public agencies (PAs) serving students with disabilities ages 3-21
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds may be used for: personnel development and training for special education and related services staff; special education, related services, and supplementary aids and services provided according to students' IEPs; technology for recordkeeping, data collection, and case management activities. Funds may not be used for: all costs directly attributable to educating students with disabilities (general education costs), supplanting existing services, capital improvements, or pre-award costs without written approval. Specific allocations support: IDEA Part B Passthrough (Section 611 for ages 3-21; Section 619 for ages 3-5), Parentally Placed Private School Children with Disabilities (PPPSCD) services, Comprehensive Coordinated Early Intervening Services (CCEIS) for disproportionate LEAs, Special Education Citizens Advisory Committee (SECAC) activities (not to exceed 10% for supplies/materials), Family Support Services, and Consortia arrangements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties; available to all eligible LEAs and public agencies throughout the state.
requirements_list: Local education agency or public agency status meeting IDEA eligibility criteria (34 CFR §§ 300.201-300.213)
Active registration and status on federal System for Award Management (SAM) website with assigned Unique Entity Identifier (UEI)
Policies, procedures, and programs in effect consistent with state policies established under 34 CFR §§ 300.101-300.174
Maintenance of Effort (MOE) compliance—budgeted expenditures for upcoming fiscal year must equal or exceed actual expenditures of preceding fiscal year
Recipient assurances compliance for special education and related services
Federal certifications compliance
General Education Provisions Act (GEPA) Statement submission addressing equitable access and participation
Compliance with programmatic and fiscal regulations including 2 CFR Parts 200 and applicable IDEA provisions
Timely and meaningful consultation with Special Education Citizen Advisory Committee (SECAC), parents, and community partners in development of application
For Parentally Placed Private School Children: thorough Child Find process, timely consultation with private school representatives, proportionate share calculation, documented services

For Comprehensive Coordinated Early Intervening Services (CCEIS): applicable to LEAs identified with significant disproportionality based on race/ethnicity (identification, placement, or disciplinary removal)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Download the LAFF electronic application from the Resource Management and Monitoring Branch website. 2. Develop the application with meaningful public input from the Special Education Citizen Advisory Committee (SECAC), parents, community partners, and educators. 3. Complete the application form, including Proposal Cover Page (signed by Superintendent/Head of Agency), budget narratives, and all required appendices. 4. Submit CCEIS Root Cause Analysis by April 10, 2026 (if applicable). 5. Upload complete application in PDF format to the designated shared folder on the MSDE MOVEit Secure File Transfer website using file naming convention: PBG_LEA.ID_2026_LAFF_App.pdf 6. Notify assigned Fiscal Grants Liaison of upload completion. 7. Submit all required supplemental documents (Family Support Services Template if applicable, CCEIS Plans by July 15, 2026 if applicable, Excess Costs Template by January 31, 2027, and other supporting documentation). 8. Applications must be complete with all required appendices or review and approval may be delayed. All submissions follow MSDE procedures and compliance requirements for federal IDEA funds.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Local Application for Federal Funds (LAFF) under Part B provides federal funding to local educational agencies (LEAs) and public agencies to support special education and related services for students with disabilities ages 3-21 in Maryland. The program is designed to ensure that all children with disabilities have available a free appropriate public education (FAPE) that emphasizes special education and related services designed to meet their unique needs and prepare them for further education, employment, and independent living.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grant funding distributed through the SFY 2024 LAFF application process to local educational agencies and public agencies for special education services. Funds are formula-based allocations under IDEA Part B Section 611 (serving ages 3-21) and Section 619 (Preschool, serving ages 3-5). Funds may be used for: personnel development, special education and related services, supplementary aids and services, appropriate technology for recordkeeping and case management, family support services, early intervening services, secondary transition services, and comprehensive coordinated early intervening services (CCEIS). Funding must be used to supplement (not supplant) state, local, and other federal funds and is limited to paying only the excess costs of providing special education services.

structured_extraction.contact_name: Ibijoke Owolabi, MBA, CPA (Branch Chief); Gary W. Richardson, MBA (Secondary Contact)

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Special education and related services, early childhood services, secondary transition services, family support services, comprehensive coordinated early intervening services (CCEIS), personnel development, technology for recordkeeping and case management, services to parentally placed private school children with disabilities (PPPSCD), and Special Education Citizens Advisory Committee (SECAC) activities. Funds must be used only to pay excess costs and to supplement (not supplant) existing state, local, and other federal funds.

Excess Cost documentation per 34 CFR 300.16 and Appendix A

CCEIS (Comprehensive Coordinated Early Intervening Services) Plan Template submission by June 30, 2023 if applicable

Interim Progress/Cumulative Variance Reports and Final Progress/Cumulative Variance Reports

Parentally Placed Private School Children with Disabilities (PPPSCD) procedures and documentation if applicable
GEPA Section 427 compliance statement addressing equitable access for students with special needs

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Register and maintain active UEI status on SAM.gov. 2) LEAs submit the SFY 2024 LAFF Application electronically with all required signatures in PDF format to MSDE MOVEit Secure File Transfer Website by June 30, 2023 at 5:00 p.m. EDT, using naming convention: PBG_LEA.ID_2024_LAFF_App.pdf. 3) Submit completed GEPA Section 427 form as appendix. 4) Submit MSDE Grant Budget C-1-25 and Budget Detail Forms with supporting budget documentation. 5) For applicable areas, submit Local Implementation for Results (LIR) plans by August 15, 2023, including Early Childhood LIR, Secondary Transition LIR, and/or Access-Equity-Progress LIR. 6) Submit CCEIS Plan Template by June 30, 2023 if LEA is identified as having significant disproportionality. 7) Submit Family Support Services Plan if LEA receives FSS allocation. 8) Provide PPPSCD plans and documentation including timely and meaningful consultation with private schools. 9) Submit interim progress reports by January 31, 2024, and final reports by November 30, 2025. 10) Maintain complete documentation for MOE, Excess Cost, and fiscal compliance throughout grant period.

Have a child diagnosed by an audiologist or other medical professional as Deaf or Hard-of-Hearing from birth to age 21 who has not yet graduated from high school

If applying for hearing aids, must not have insurance coverage for hearing aids, or be experiencing delays or difficulties acquiring or replacing hearing aids, or need a hearing aid trial before purchasing personal aids or receiving a cochlear implant

structured_extraction.program_description: The Compensatory Learning Improvement Grant (CLIG) is the consolidated mechanism through which local jurisdictions receive various federal and State funds to implement local early intervention programs for Maryland's Infants and Toddlers Program (MITP) under the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA). The program provides funding for services and supports for infants, toddlers, and preschool children (Birth through Age 4) with disabilities and developmental delays and their families, including historically underrepresented populations (minority, low-income, homeless, inner city, rural children, and children in foster care).
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding to support early intervention services for infants and toddlers with disabilities and their families. Funds are distributed through multiple sources: IDEA Part C funds, IDEA Part B Section 611 funds, IDEA Part B Section 619 Preschool funds, Maryland State General Funds, Blueprint for Maryland's Future funds, Additional IDEA Federal Funds, Federal Medicaid Reimbursement Funds, and State Incentive Grant (SIG) funding. Funding allocations are formula-based and vary by Local Lead Agency (LLA) or Public Agency (PA), based on the Part C Annual Child Count of children served on an Individualized Family Service Plan (IFSP) and the Part C Annual Referral Count. Funds can support early intervention services, specialized instruction, related services, family support services, direct services not otherwise provided by public sources, expansion/improvement of existing services, professional development and training, administrative and staff positions, contractual services, supplies and materials, and adaptive equipment. At least $5,000 of Part C allocation must support a Family Support Coordinator for children birth-age 3.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No later than 5:00 p.m. EDT on May 15, 2026
structured_extraction.contact_name: Gary W. Richardson, Director, Resource Management & Monitoring
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local Lead Agencies (LLAs), which may be a Local Education Agency (LEA) or Local Health Department (LHD), and Local Interagency Coordinating Councils (LICCs) administering Maryland's Infants and Toddlers Program (MITP). Each Maryland jurisdiction must appoint a Local Lead Agency to implement local early intervention services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support for early intervention services including specialized instruction, related services, and family support services for infants and toddlers with disabilities ages birth to 4. Funds support: direct service provision not otherwise funded by public sources; expansion and improvement of existing early intervention services; enhancement of local program capacity to identify, evaluate, and meet needs of all children including historically underrepresented populations; Family Support Coordinator positions and activities; professional development and training; administrative and staff positions; contractual services; supplies and materials; adaptive equipment; family engagement and transition activities; and parent workshops strengthening understanding of IDEA rights and transition practices. Part B Section 619 Family Support Services funds are designated for transition-related activities for children ages 3-kindergarten and must include employment of a parent of a child with a disability on a salaried or contractual basis.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide; each jurisdiction must appoint a Local Lead Agency responsible for implementing early intervention services in that jurisdiction. All Maryland jurisdictions are eligible, and local programs must consider effectiveness and impact of their outreach, referral, intake, evaluation, and program development activities to ensure all families of children with delays and disabilities gain access to high-quality early intervention services, with analysis disaggregated by race and ethnic group.
requirements_list: Designated Local Lead Agency (LLA) status (either LEA or LHD)
Valid SAM.gov registration with Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) Number and screenshot evidence
Local Lead Agency (LLA) designation from local governing authority (letter, executive order, proclamation, or other official notification)

Local Interagency Agreement signed by local Superintendent of Schools, Health Officer, Director of Department of Social Services, and director of any other participating local public agency; valid through June 30, 2024 or as required

Local Interagency Coordinating Council (LICC) involvement with at least 3 parent members, representatives from LEA, health department, social services, service providers, personnel preparation, elected official, Head Start, and child care representatives; must meet at least 4 times per fiscal year
Completion of Recipient Assurances (State Assurances) form signed by authorized head of agency
Federal Certifications regarding lobbying, debarment, suspension, other responsibility matters, and drug-free workplace
General Education Provisions Act (GEPA) Section 427 Form addressing equitable access and participation
Assurance of Local Capacity signed by Local Lead Agency Head
LICC Review Statement signed by LICC Chairperson
LICC Membership Directory
Local Infants and Toddlers Program (LITP) policies and procedures
Establishment of fiscal control and fund accounting procedures in accordance with 2 CFR § 200
Comprehensive budget documentation generated by SFY Budget Submissions Workbook with all required signatures

Early Intervention Program Plan addressing infrastructure development, personnel development, equity and access, Child Outcomes Summary process, and Comprehensive System of Personnel Development (CSPD)
Family Support data and plan for birth-age 3 and age 3-kindergarten services
Data analysis demonstrating fiscal control and compliance with non-supplant requirements
Program participation data analysis, including disaggregated data by race/ethnicity to identify barriers to access
Aggregation of information from LITP partner agencies
Compliance with IDEA Part C (34 CFR Part 303) and Maryland regulations (COMAR 13A.13)
Compliance with Civil Rights Act, EDGAR, GEPA, and ADA
Accessible facilities for individuals with disabilities
Public awareness and outreach strategies
Procedures to ensure timely resolution of interagency disputes
Maintenance of Early Intervention records for each child
Parent opportunity to participate in development of CLIG application
Retention of all grant financial records for five years or longer
Submission of required semiannual and final programmatic and financial reports
Prior written MSDE approval before implementing programmatic changes
Prior written MSDE approval for budget realignments of $1,000 or 15% of total expenditure (whichever is greater)
Annual financial and compliance audit if expending $750,000 or more in federal funds (or $1,000,000 or more per 2 CFR § 200.501)
Compliance with Section 508 of Federal Rehabilitation Act for web-based or technology-based instructional products
Non-use of federal funds to supplant State and local funds
Participation of all signatory agencies in the system of early intervention services including Maryland Online IFSP and MITP Tracking/Data Collection System
Submission of Public Awareness Plan if required based on performance on SPP/APR indicators #5 or #6
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Download the SFY CLIG Application and Grant Information Guide from the MSDE website. 2. Complete the application electronically including cover page with UEI information, Local Early Intervention System Contact List, and LICC information. 3. Develop and complete the Early Intervention Program Plan addressing required data, analysis, and strategies for infrastructure development, personnel development, equity and access, and Child Outcomes. 4. Gather all required appendices including signed Recipient Assurances, Federal Certifications, GEPA Section 427 Form, Local Lead Agency designation, Local Interagency Agreement, Assurance of Local Capacity, LICC Review Statement, LICC Membership Directory, LITP policies and procedures, and Linking Funds to Program Improvement Chart. 5. Generate complete budget documentation using the SFY CLIG Budget Submissions Workbook with all required signatures. 6. Compile program participation analysis disaggregated by race/ethnicity and identify barriers to access. 7. If required, submit a Public Awareness Plan. 8. Combine all components into a single comprehensive application package. 9. Save the completed application as a PDF file with filename following MSDE MOVEit naming conventions. 10. Submit by uploading the PDF to the local program's designated shared folder on the MSDE MOVEit Secure File Transfer Website by the deadline. 11. Applications must be complete with all required signatures to be considered filed and reviewed. Incomplete applications will not be reviewed.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Medicaid Home and Community-Based Services Waiver for Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (Autism Waiver)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Autism Waiver provides community-based, long-term, person-centered therapeutic services and support to eligible children and youth with Autism Spectrum Disorder to enable home and community living as an alternative to institutional care. Services are delivered through approved Medicaid providers statewide.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Autism Waiver provides seven types of community-based services: Intensive Individual Support Services (IISS) - one-on-one assistance based on the child's need for interventions and support to help children acquire, retain, and improve self-help, socialization, communication, daily living, functional living, behavior management, and adaptive skills; Therapeutic Integration (TI) or Intensive Therapeutic Integration (ITI) - structured programs outside school hours providing therapeutic activities and expressive therapies for children with socialization, isolation, hyperactivity, impulse control, and behavior challenges; Respite Care - short-term supervision and assistance with activities of daily living for relief of caregivers; Environmental Accessibility Adaptations (EAA) - funding for physical adaptations to the home necessary for health, welfare, and safety; Family Consultation (FC) - individualized consultation and training for the child's family; Adult Life Planning (ALP) - family-centered education and support in accessing adult community services; and Residential Habilitation (Regular or Intensive) - community-based residential placement for children requiring highly supervised and supportive environments with the goal of returning the child to the home. Participants receive Service Coordination/targeted case management and access to full Medical Assistance benefits including health insurance, prescription coverage, dental care, physician and hospital care, home health, laboratory services, disposable medical supplies, durable medical equipment, and mental health services.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 45 days from the date of the application letter from MDH; 30-day deadline to provide updated/additional information if not added to waitlist; 15-day deadline to submit information after Final Notice
structured_extraction.contact_name: Autism Waiver Helpline / Maryland State Department of Education Division of Early Intervention and Special Education Services
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children and youth ages 1 through the end of the school semester when the child turns 21 years old with an educational classification of Autism or a diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder who reside in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services support home and community living alternatives to institutional care, including therapeutic interventions, family training and consultation, residential placement, respite care, and physical home adaptations necessary for health, welfare, and safety.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide; eligible children and youth must reside in Maryland.
requirements_list: Be a resident of Maryland
Be between the age of 1 and 21 years old
Have a current educational classification of Autism or a diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder

Receive early intervention or special education services identified through one of the following: an Individual Family Service Plan (IFSP) for ages 1-5; an Individual Education Program (IEP) in an early childhood or Kindergarten setting for ages 3-5; or an IEP with 15 or more hours of special education and related services and/or 1:1 adult supports per week for first grade through exit from high school
Meet an institutional Level of Care for Intermediate Care Facilities for individuals with Intellectual Disabilities (ICF-IID) and choose to receive Autism Waiver services as an alternative
Be able to be served and safely maintained in the home and community with Autism Waiver services
Meet financial eligibility for Medical Assistance with monthly income not exceeding 300% of Supplemental Security Income (SSI) benefits and countable assets not exceeding $2,000
Choose the Autism Waiver as the waiver that best meets the child's needs

Military Exception: Dependents of US Military Service members invited to apply to the Autism Waiver while the family is out of the state for military services shall be offered an opportunity to apply upon request when they return to Maryland and meet all technical eligibility requirements
Maintain eligibility by using at least 5 hours of Autism Waiver services per month
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Contact the Autism Waiver Helpline at 1-866-417-3480 to register on the Autism Waiver Registry. Provide child's name, date of birth, address, county of residence, contact information, and confirm Autism Spectrum Disorder diagnosis and IFSP or IEP status with at least 15 hours of special education/related services per week (1st grade and above). 2. MDH vendor conducts initial screening during intake call based on parent self-report. If technical eligibility criteria are met, name is added to Registry and MSDE is notified with letter sent to family. If not met, family is not added to Registry but given 30-day deadline to provide updated/additional information. 3. MSDE verifies technical eligibility: resident of MD, under age 21, Autism Spectrum Disorder diagnosis, IFSP or IEP with 15 hours of special education/health-related services. 4. If verified, child's name is added to Autism Waiver Waitlist and confirmation letter sent to family. 5. When a vacancy occurs, MDH sends an invitation letter to apply. Family has 45 days to accept invitation, establish contact with AW Contact at local education agency (LEA), complete technical eligibility checklist, and submit financial application. 6. Family works with AW Contact to confirm technical, financial, and medical eligibility. 7. Receive notification of eligibility from the State. If eligible, letter includes start date to begin Autism Waiver services. 8. Attend multidisciplinary team meeting to develop a Plan of Care. Application materials include Medical Assistance (MA) Financial Application, Parental Rights and Responsibilities, AW Contact List, and Application Documentation Checklist. Flowchart describing the application process available in English and Spanish. Parents must ensure all demographic information remains up to date and contact the Helpline to report any changes.

structured_extraction.program_description: The NSLP provides nutritionally balanced, low-cost, or free lunches to children each school day. Schools receive federal reimbursement for meals that comply with USDA nutrition standards. The program has expanded access to fresh fruits, vegetables, whole-grain menu items, and reduced sodium and saturated fat content. Maryland has adopted the federal Smart Snacks standards and the 2020-2025 Dietary Guidelines for Americans, effective July 1, 2025. The program provides access to nutritious lunches and snacks to students in participating public and private nonprofit schools and residential childcare institutions.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal reimbursement to schools for providing nutritionally balanced meals to eligible students at no charge or reduced price. Free meals are available to children from families at or below 130% of the federal poverty level. Children from families between 130-185% of poverty level receive reduced-price meals (free due to Maryland Cares for Kids Act). Children in CEP schools, MMFA schools, Head Start, Even Start, categorically eligible children (including homeless, migrants, runaways, foster children), and directly certified Medicaid recipients receive free meals. Effective July 1, 2023 through June 30, 2024, income eligibility thresholds are established for household sizes 1-8 with specific monthly, twice-per-month, every-two-weeks, and weekly income limits. For households with multiple income sources at different frequencies, all income must be annualized for comparison to annual guidelines.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children and students attending participating Maryland public schools, approved non-profit private schools, and residential childcare institutions. All 24 Maryland public school systems and 22 non-profit private schools and residential childcare institutions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: School lunch meals that meet USDA nutrition standards and Maryland Nutrition Standards for All Foods Sold in School, including whole grain-rich foods, fruits, vegetables, dairy products, and protein foods with specified calorie, sodium, fat, and sugar limits. Nutritious lunches and snacks meeting USDA nutrition guidelines.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All 24 Maryland public school systems and 22 non-profit private schools and residential childcare institutions. Maryland statewide.
requirements_list: School must participate in the NSLP
Children must attend a participating school
Children from families at or below 130% of federal poverty level qualify for free meals
Children from families between 130-185% of federal poverty level qualify for reduced-price meals
Categorical eligibility through participation in SNAP, Temporary Assistance Cash, or status as homeless, migrant, runaway, or foster child
Direct certification through Medicaid participation
Attendance at CEP school provides free meals regardless of household income
Enrollment in Head Start or Even Start provides free meals
Attendance at MMFA participating school provides free breakfast

Household income documentation required for free and reduced-price applications, compared against annual, monthly, twice-per-month, every-two-weeks, or weekly income eligibility guidelines depending on income frequency
Meals must comply with USDA nutrition standards and Maryland Nutrition Standards including Smart Snacks requirements
Foods sold during school day (12:01 am through 30 minutes after end of school day) must meet specified calorie, sodium, fat, and sugar limits

structured_extraction.program_description: State aid program that provides tuition reimbursement for students placed in nonpublic special education schools through the Individualized Education Program (IEP) process. The State's share of the cost is calculated in accordance with Education Article §8-415 of the Annotated Code of Maryland. The program covers both MSDE-approved day and residential programs as well as individual placements in non-approved or out-of-state special education programs. The Maryland State Department of Education provides tuition assistance for local school systems and nonpublic special education schools for the placement of children with disabilities in nonpublic educational programs, as required by Education Article §8-406 and §8-415 of the Annotated Code of Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State reimbursement for tuition costs of nonpublic special education placements. The State's share is calculated according to Maryland law (Education Article §8-406 and §8-415). Reimbursement covers standard education and related services, extended school year services, residential services when appropriate, and specific related services/supplemental aides as outlined in the student's IEP. Students placed in these schools are included in enrollment counts with a special code (09) indicating nonpublic placement. Eligible placements include MSDE-approved day and residential programs as well as individual placements in non-approved or out-of-state special education programs when deemed appropriate by the IEP team. Reimbursement is calculated on a per-diem rate basis.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing program with specific submission deadlines depending on entry/discharge/revision dates
structured_extraction.contact_name: Sheila F. Philip, JD, Section Chief, Nonpublic Special Education
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local Education Agencies (LEAs) and school districts placing students with special education needs in nonpublic special education schools
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition costs for students placed in nonpublic special education schools including: standard education and related services, extended school year services, residential services (day and residential programs), and billable related services such as audiology, counseling, occupational therapy, physical therapy, psychological services, speech-language pathology, one-to-one aides, and behavioral modification services as specified in the student's IEP.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: IEP team must determine placement is appropriate and in the least restrictive environment
Placement must be in a MSDE-approved program or approved for individual placement
IEP must include measurable annual goals with benchmarks or short-term objectives
Documenting school must provide letter stating they can implement FAPE in the least restrictive environment
For individual/non-approved program placements: agreement/decision for mediated or due process cases must be provided
LEA Special Education Supervisor/Director or designee must verify all application information and assure compliance standards are met
Cost sheet must accompany each application
For new/renewal individual placements: IEP team minutes supporting placement must be submitted
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. LEA Special Education Supervisor/Director determines appropriate nonpublic placement through IEP team process. 2. Gather supporting documentation including IEP, cost sheet (required), and for individual placements: IEP team minutes, school letter confirming FAPE implementation, and mediation/due process agreements if applicable. 3. Complete NTAP application form (available for MSDE-approved programs or individual placements). 4. Submit completed application and cost sheet to MSDE within specified timelines. 5. MSDE conducts demographic and program review, approves or denies reimbursement request. Timelines for submission: ESY or entry dates in July/August submit by September 30; entry dates September 1 to June 2 submit within 30 calendar days of entry date; entry dates June 3-30 submit by July 7; discharge applications submit within 30 calendar days of discharge date; service revision applications submit within 30 calendar days of revision date. Written notice required if unable to meet timeline.

structured_extraction.program_name: Pathways in Technology Early College High School (P-TECH) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: P-TECH schools are innovative grade 9 to 14 public schools that create clear pathways from high school to college and career for young people from all academic backgrounds. Students graduate with a high school diploma and a no-cost, two-year associate degree in six years or less.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Students receive a no-cost two-year associate degree along with high school diploma, one-on-one mentoring, workplace visits, skills instruction, paid summer internships, and first-in-line consideration for job openings with partnering companies.
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school students from all academic backgrounds, grades 9-14
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Education and workforce development pathway including high school and associate degree completion, mentoring, internship support, and job placement consideration.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Administered through MSDE as a competitive grant process for school systems, community colleges, and businesses to establish P-TECH sites.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal funding program that expands opportunities for every student to explore, choose, and follow career and technical education programs of study and career pathways to earn valuable credentials. Provides funding to local school systems, community colleges, the Juvenile Services Education System, the Adult Correctional Education System, and other affiliates to support CTE programs of study in accordance with state plan priorities and federal law requirements.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grant funding distributed to eligible recipients (local school systems, community colleges, Juvenile Services Education System, Adult Correctional Education System, and other CTE affiliates) to support the development and delivery of high-quality career and technical education programs of study. Funding supports CTE programs that align to high-skill, high-wage, and in-demand careers; lead to earning industry-recognized and postsecondary credentials; and provide career-based learning experiences requiring application of academic and technical knowledge and skills in work settings. Funds may be used for program development, instructional improvements, equipment, professional development for educators, student support services, work-based learning opportunities, and assessment activities.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications must be fully completed and approved by July 1st of each year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local school systems, community colleges, Juvenile Services Education System, Adult Correctional Education System, and other CTE education affiliates seeking to provide high-quality career and technical education programming to secondary and postsecondary students
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports CTE programs of study, including programs that align to high-skill, high-wage, and in-demand careers; lead to earning industry-recognized and postsecondary credentials; and provide career-based learning experiences that require application of academic and technical knowledge and skills in a work setting. Funds may support curriculum development, instructor professional development, equipment and facility improvements, student support services, work-based learning and apprenticeship programs, assessment and credential attainment activities, and services for special populations to ensure equitable access.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties are eligible. Maryland does not have tribally controlled colleges or universities, Indian Tribes, or Tribal organizations. Charter schools in Maryland are included in the local school system for Perkins funding purposes.
requirements_list: Local school systems and eligible recipients must complete a Comprehensive Local Needs Assessment (CLNA) every other year to evaluate capacity to offer high-quality CTE programming and identify improvement areas
Submit a Local Application outlining how federal funds will be used to improve CTE instruction and student access to quality programs

Meet or make progress toward performance levels on required core indicators for secondary and postsecondary programs, including graduation rates, academic proficiency, postsecondary placement, credential attainment, and non-traditional program concentration

Ensure all CTE programs of study meet Size, Scope, and Quality criteria, including alignment to high-skill, high-wage, and in-demand occupations; industry standards; and equitable access for all students

Provide equal access to CTE programs and activities for all students, including special populations, individuals with disabilities, economically disadvantaged students, and students preparing for non-traditional fields
Establish and maintain Local Advisory Councils and Program Advisory Committees with diverse stakeholder representation
Demonstrate alignment of CTE programs with state and local labor market data and workforce development needs
Meet annual data-reporting requirements and Program Quality Index reviews
Provide professional development for teachers, faculty, counselors, and support personnel to improve student learning outcomes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To qualify for Perkins V funding, eligible recipients must: (1) Conduct a comprehensive evaluation of current CTE programming capacity by completing a Comprehensive Local Needs Assessment (CLNA) every other year. The CLNA examines labor market alignment, student participation and persistence, program performance, and educator recruitment and retention. (2) Assemble a diverse stakeholder team including secondary and postsecondary administrators, teachers, faculty, counselors, business and industry representatives, workforce development board members, parents, students, and representatives of special populations. (3) Analyze local, regional, and state labor market data to ensure CTE programs align with high-skill, high-wage, and in-demand career fields. (4) Review and assess student participation and performance data disaggregated by demographics and special population status. (5) Evaluate program performance against state-determined performance targets. (6) Identify priority improvement areas and develop S.M.A.R.T.I.E. goals (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound, Inclusive, and Equitable). (7) Complete and submit a Local Application detailing how federal funds will be used to implement improvement strategies. The Local Application must clearly connect identified needs to proposed activities, budget, and expected outcomes. (8) Obtain approval from the State Director of Career and Technical Education or designee prior to July 1st of each year. Approved applications receive Perkins V funding to implement proposed CTE improvements.

structured_extraction.program_description: An initiative designed by the local school system to address the needs of individual students or groups of students who are at high risk of placement in a nonpublic special education school. The partnership utilizes wrap-around supportive services within the public school setting and is especially beneficial for school systems building local capacity to address specific, immediate needs.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local School Systems and students at high risk of placement in nonpublic special education schools
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wrap-around supportive services within the public school setting to prevent placement in nonpublic special education schools
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: A funding agreement between a Local School System and a Maryland State Department of Education-approved nonpublic special education program for serving students with significant and intensive needs in the Least Restrictive Environment. The program enhances Individualized Education Program services for students in their community and is especially beneficial for students with short-term needs, requiring alternative special education programs, experiencing crisis, or awaiting more intensive placement. The Public/Private Partnership supports inclusion and facilitates the provision of a Free Appropriate Public Education (FAPE) in the least restrictive environment.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Payment is based upon the tuition for a specified number of full-time equivalent (FTE) seats. The State partnership tuition contributions are calculated and based on the actual number of full-time equivalent seats used over the course of the school year. Reconciliation is finalized at the close of each fiscal year; the MSDE funds only the actual number of FTE seats that have been used. The Public/Private Partnership must be cost neutral to the State. The State's cost cannot exceed the cost for the equivalent number of placements through the traditional nonpublic tuition assistance program.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications submitted to the MSDE by June 1 annually
structured_extraction.contact_name: Sheila F. Philip, JD; MSDE Division of Early Intervention and Special Education Services, Nonpublic Special Education Section Chief
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local School Systems and students with significant and intensive special education needs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding agreement to serve students with significant and intensive needs in special education settings in the Least Restrictive Environment. Supports short-term placements, access to public school instruction and activities, and transitioning of students to less restrictive programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: MSDE Public/Private Partnership Application (Due annually by June 1)
Public/Private Partnership Agreement or Contract
Budget completed by the nonpublic provider utilizing the MSDE budget packet
The MSDE Public/Private Partnership Fiscal Worksheet
Application must be submitted at minimum of thirty (30) calendar days prior to request for State funding for each fiscal year
Mid-year enrollment report and outcome data report submitted to MSDE by January 15
End-of-year enrollment report or outcome data report submitted to MSDE by June 1
Biannual monitoring data submission as outlined in Student Attendance List
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Local School Systems should initiate discussions with MSDE regarding new proposals by February 1. 2. Collect data supporting the need for the program. 3. Outline a basic proposal and timeline for implementation. 4. Identify the potential location to house the partnership. 5. Contact the MSDE Division of Early Intervention and Special Education Services, Nonpublic Special Education Section Chief to explore availability of funds and finalize an action plan. 6. Submit MSDE Public/Private Partnership Application, Partnership Agreement/Contract, budget, and fiscal worksheet by June 1. 7. MSDE provides notice of intent to fund by July 15. 8. Finalized and signed contracts submitted to MSDE prior to release of State funds. 9. Submit mid-year and end-of-year reports on schedule.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free online professional development course in the Science of Reading fundamentals.
