structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) provides annual grants to qualified non-profit organizations that provide enriching educational programs to Maryland students. Eligible programs provide learning experiences that align with the State's curricular and educational priorities and cannot be replicated in the classroom. These educational opportunities emphasize experiential learning and one-on-one support services, including free or reduced admission, full-day and residential field trips with hands-on activities, mentoring, and tutoring. Pre- and post-visit activities for teachers can be used to connect the experiences to the classroom curriculum. Professional development opportunities for teachers that link the SAI programs to the classroom are also funded. Currently, there are 57 organizations in the SAI program. In fiscal year 2024, approximately 440,000 Maryland students and teachers were served through this program.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grants to qualified non-profit organizations for educational programs providing experiential learning and one-on-one support services. Funds may be used for: salaries, wages, and stipends for direct service to students and educators; supplies and materials to implement the educational program; outreach, engagement, informational, and marketing tools to expand reach; equipment necessary for direct service to students and teachers; and contractual expenses. Funds must be used within the fiscal year for which they are granted. Funds may not be used for construction or capital improvements, transportation of students, utilities or operating costs, or food. Approximately $6,706,449 is available, with an estimated 60-65 grants to be awarded.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, June 13, 2025, no later than 5:00 p.m. EDT
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified non-profit organizations that provide enriching educational programs to Maryland students. Applicants must be a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization in good standing that provides direct service to Maryland students and teachers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational programs that provide experiential learning and one-on-one support services, including free or reduced admission, full-day and residential field trips with hands-on activities, mentoring, tutoring, pre- and post-visit activities for teachers, and professional development opportunities for teachers. Allowable uses: salaries, wages, and stipends for direct service; supplies and materials; outreach and marketing tools; equipment; and contractual expenses. Not allowable: construction or capital improvements, transportation of students, utilities or operating costs, and food.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide (all Maryland counties)
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization in good standing and incorporated or registered under the laws of Maryland
Must provide direct service to Maryland students and teachers
Must submit a Fiscal Impact Statement describing the educational program, amount of funds requested, populations to be served, educational goals and objectives, and anticipated outcomes
Must provide names of members of an independent governing board
Must provide proof of 501(c)(3) status
Must provide a copy of the most recent independent annual audit or internally generated financial statements
Must provide evidence of active liability insurance coverage
Must submit a detailed operating budget indicating less than 50% of budget comes from state grants (except Baltimore Zoo), specifying all sources of income and all expenditures

Must provide evidence of direct service to Maryland school groups or individuals with disabilities, including data on student age levels, projected numbers of students and teachers to be served statewide and by jurisdiction
Must demonstrate how educational programs align with MSDE's educational and curricular priorities
New applicants must provide evidence that the program is not new and has a track record of success
All applicants must set programmatic goals that are specific, measurable, ambitious yet attainable, realistic, and time-bound
All applicants must provide an evaluation plan for programmatic goals with clear data collection methods
Must provide description of proposed educational enrichment program including targeted grade levels, areas of educational focus, and related curricular standards
Must have an outreach plan including steps to reach historically underserved populations
Must provide a project timeline with key activities and implementation phases
Must identify key personnel with titles, responsibilities, and tasks
Must provide itemized budget with detailed line-item descriptions grouped by category (Salaries & Wages, Contracted Services, Supplies & Materials, Other Charges, Equipment, Transfers)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted electronically through MSDE. Timeline: Grant Information Guide released May 1, 2025. Customer service support sessions held May 5 and May 23, 2025, where MSDE personnel review program requirements and provide application walk-throughs. Applicants download the electronic application, complete it with all attachments, and save as one PDF file. Applications must be submitted by email to sai.applications@maryland.gov by 5:00 p.m. EDT on June 13, 2025. MSDE reviews applications on a rolling basis using a standardized scoring rubric. Applications are pre-screened for submission requirements. Review committee evaluates applications in July. Results communicated to State Superintendent in July and State Board of Education in August. Final approval determined by Governor's budget bill, released January-April 2026. Grant period runs July 1, 2026 – June 30, 2027.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally-funded, state-administered program that provides free nutritious meals to children and teens 18 years and younger in low-income areas during the summer months when school is not in session. The program merges summer activity and enrichment programs with federal meal reimbursement, providing continued access to nutritious meals to support children in economically disadvantaged areas.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program reimburses providers who serve free healthy meals to children and teens in low-income areas during the summer. Two meal service models are available: SUN Meals (on-site meals and activities) and SUN Meals To-Go (multi-day meal boxes for pickup, requiring registration).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children and teens 18 years and younger in low-income areas during summer months
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free meals served to eligible children and teens during summer months when school is not in session
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Low-income areas throughout Maryland
requirements_list: Organization must become a SUN Meals site by contacting the sponsoring organization for their county
Must serve free healthy meals to children and teens 18 years and younger
Meals must follow USDA meal patterns and nutrition requirements
For SUN Meals To-Go sites, registration is required to receive meals
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply as a SUN Meals site, contact the sponsoring organization for your county. Contact information is provided for all 24 Maryland counties.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Teachers of Promise program strategically leverages the knowledge, skills, and experiences of Teachers of the Year and other distinguished educators by pairing them with promising pre-service students from colleges and universities across Maryland. The program provides pre-service teachers with mentorship opportunities, professional development, and networking with seasoned teachers to support their transition into teaching careers in Maryland public schools.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides mentorship through pairing pre-service teachers with Maryland Teachers of the Year, Milken Educators, and other award-winning educators. Mentorship includes storytelling, classroom observations, and resource sharing. The program features an annual day-long Teachers of Promise Institute event (held April 19, 2024) with keynote addresses from the Maryland State Superintendent and distinguished educators, panel sessions featuring first-year teachers, veteran teachers, and current students, wellness sessions, and networking opportunities. The program facilitates online partnerships between mentees and mentors throughout the spring and summer until the new teacher is placed in their school.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pre-service students in their final year of college or university who are majoring in education and plan to teach in Maryland public schools. Students are nominated by Maryland colleges and universities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional development through mentorship with veteran and award-winning educators, access to classroom observations, networking with experienced educators, participation in the annual Teachers of Promise Institute event featuring keynote addresses, panel discussions with first-year and veteran teachers, and wellness sessions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Pre-service students must be from Maryland colleges and universities and plan to teach in Maryland public schools.
requirements_list: Students must be in their final year of college or university
Students must be majoring in education
Students must plan to teach in Maryland public schools in the fall
Students must be nominated by their Maryland college or university
Five to seven students are nominated from each participating Maryland college and university annually
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Maryland colleges and universities nominate 5-7 of their top students majoring in education to participate in the program. Nominees are matched with Maryland Teachers of the Year, Milken Educators, and other award-winning educators. Once matched, pre-service students and mentors begin an online partnership that continues throughout the spring and summer, including participation in the annual Teachers of Promise Institute event held in April, until the new teacher is placed in their school.

structured_extraction.program_description: Funding for Local Education Agencies (LEAs) participating in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP) or Seamless Summer Option (SSO) to develop high-quality, appealing standardized recipes for schools using local agricultural products in collaboration with Maryland chefs. LEA grant awards support staff time for training and recipe tasting events, and purchase of food and supplies. The goal is to create four new standardized recipes (Vegetable Side Dish, Chicken or Fish Bowl, Vegetarian Bowl, and Entrée Salad) that align with students' flavor preferences and are realistic for schools to implement. MSDE is working with chefs from Prince George's Community College's Department of Wellness, Culinary Arts, and Hospitality. Grant partners also include Maryland SNAP-Ed and the Maryland Department of Agriculture.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding provided to LEAs for staff time related to training and recipe tasting events, and to purchase food and supplies for these events. Funds support: (1) Salaries/wages to hire substitute school nutrition staff to allow staff to attend training; (2) Stipends for staff time to attend training activities outside normal work hours; (3) Food and nutrition equipment and smallware costs (not to exceed 5% of total grant award) such as crinkle cutters, peelers, food processors, knives, roasting pans, and utensils; (4) Food costs for grant-related training and taste tests (not to exceed 20% of total grant award), which must comply with Buy American provisions. Equipment cannot exceed 5% of the LEA subgrant total. Food expenditures cannot exceed 20% of LEA subgrant total. The feedback from tasting events is used by state partners to modify recipes to align with students' flavor preferences.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 22, 2022, no later than 5:00 pm EST
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local Education Agencies (LEAs) participating in the National School Lunch Program or Seamless Summer Option during School Year 2021-2022, in good standing
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Salaries/wages to hire substitute school nutrition staff to allow staff to attend training; stipends for staff time to attend training activities outside normal work hours; food and nutrition equipment and smallware costs (not to exceed 5% of total grant) such as crinkle cutters, peelers, food processors, knives, roasting pans, and utensils; food costs for grant-related training and taste tests (not to exceed 20% of total grant) in compliance with Buy American provisions; consumable costs for grant-related training and taste tests. Development of training and nutrition education resources related to recipes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: LEAs must be participating in NSLP or SSO during 2021-2022 and in good standing

LEAs must commit participation of up to three schools; if more than one school is selected, at least two must serve different grade levels (with certain exceptions approved for grade level distribution)
LEAs must select schools enrolled as Team Nutrition Schools; schools must be registered prior to application submission
Each participating school must prepare at least one of the chef-designed recipes and host at least two student taste tests per recipe between Spring 2022 - Spring 2023
Schools must achieve an 85% acceptance rate from students for each of the four recipes
LEA must designate a Grant Coordinator to serve as primary liaison with MSDE and grant partners and manage subgrant funds
Grant Coordinator must participate in periodic virtual meetings with grant partners and facilitate logistics for all training and tasting events
LEA must menu and serve at least one of the final recipes in a reimbursable meal at participating schools by end of grant
LEA must submit quarterly reports on utilization of subgrant funds
LEA must collect and submit data and feedback from recipe tasting events using templates provided by MSDE
LEA must secure photographs, training attendance records, data, and success stories for MSDE quarterly progress reports to USDA
Funds must comply with Buy American provisions for food purchases
Equipment cannot exceed 5% of total subgrant award
Food expenditures cannot exceed 20% of total subgrant award
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must: (1) Identify up to three schools to participate that are registered as Team Nutrition Schools participating in NSLP or SSO; (2) Complete a School Agreement Form for each participating school, requiring signatures from School Principal, Kitchen Manager/Cafeteria Supervisor, and a third school staff member (e.g., School Health Council member, Title 1 Coordinator, or Community Coordinator); (3) Complete the Team Nutrition Grant Application including all required components (school listing, recipe selection from four available recipes: Vegetable Side Dish, Chicken or Fish Bowl, Vegetarian Bowl, and Entrée Salad; budget with narrative; and school agreements); (4) Complete the Team Nutrition Budget Form (Excel); (5) Obtain signatures on LEA Agreement Form from Superintendent, Food and Nutrition Services Director, and LEA Grant Coordinator; (6) Submit completed application saved as PDF with all required attachments to NutritionTraining.MSDE@maryland.gov. MSDE will review applications for eligibility and completeness, score applications using selection criteria based on free/reduced-price lunch percentage, rural location, and Qualified Opportunity Zone designation. Approximately ten LEAs will be awarded grants based on scores. Award notifications sent by email in spring; processing of official Notice of Grant Award begins May 1, 2022 and takes 4-6 weeks. Estimated number of grants: 10, with additional grants possible if funds available.

structured_extraction.program_name: Training Series for Maryland Multilingual Learner Family Coordinators
structured_extraction.program_description: Professional learning training series for Maryland multilingual learner family coordinators covering topics including asset-based approaches, cultural humility, culturally responsive practices, language access, advocacy, and disability awareness. This six-session series is delivered virtually and includes recordings, transcripts, presentation materials, and follow-up resources for self-paced learning.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Six one-hour virtual professional learning webinars delivered by subject matter experts including Debra Suarez, PhD (Executive Director of Uplifting Teachers, LLC, President of TESOL International Association, and adjunct professor at Johns Hopkins University). Sessions include: (1) An asset-based approach to bilingualism/multilingualism; (2) Engaging families with cultural humility and sensitivity; (3) Culturally and linguistically responsive strategies for family leadership; (4) Language access for families of children who are multilingual learners; (5) Empowering families of children who are MLs to advocate for their children; (6) Supporting families of children who are MLs with suspected or identified disabilities. Training materials include virtual recordings, full transcripts, PowerPoint presentations, hands-on engagement activities, reflection questions, group discussion topics, action planning resources, and access to toolkits and external resources. Participants can view recordings at their own pace and in their own contexts.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland multilingual learner family coordinators and other educational personnel who interact with and serve multilingual learners and their families in Maryland public schools.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The training materials and resources can be used by family coordinators and educational personnel to enhance their professional knowledge and skills in: supporting multilingual learner students and their families; implementing asset-based approaches to bilingualism and multilingualism; engaging families with cultural humility and sensitivity; delivering culturally and linguistically responsive services; ensuring language access; advocating for multilingual learner rights; and supporting families whose children have suspected or identified disabilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to all Maryland counties
requirements_list: Participants should be Maryland multilingual learner family coordinators or educational personnel who serve multilingual learners
Access to internet for virtual webinar participation
Ability to participate in one-hour virtual training sessions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Participants access the training through the Maryland State Department of Education website. Virtual training sessions are recorded and can be accessed at any time by participants in their own contexts. Participant feedback surveys are administered at the end of each webinar session via browser popup. Participants should keep their browser open to complete the brief survey after each session.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grant program for agricultural innovation and equipment in Washington County. The Washington County Department of Business and Economic Development offers information and resources on various agriculture incentives and financial programs including grants, loans, and technical assistance for agricultural enterprises, equipment purchases, land acquisition, and value-added agricultural products.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Washington County provides information and coordination for multiple agricultural assistance programs including MARBIDCO loans (low-interest equipment and real estate financing up to $300,000-$1,000,000), USDA Rural Development Grants (Enterprise grants $10,000-$500,000 for planning, equipment, facilities), USDA Value-Added Producer Grants ($75,000-$250,000), USDA Farmers Market Promotion Program (grants $50,000-$500,000 with 25% match required), Maryland Market Money Program (dollar-for-dollar match for SNAP/EBT purchases at farmers markets), and various other state and federal programs for agricultural equipment, conservation practices, land acquisition, energy efficiency, and rural business development.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: December 6, 2024
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural enterprises, farmers, beginning/young farmers, food processors, forestry businesses, urban farmers, rural small businesses, and nonprofit organizations in Washington County and rural areas of Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equipment purchases, real estate/land acquisition, working capital, building construction and renovation, conservation best management practices, energy efficiency improvements, renewable energy systems, processing and marketing of value-added agricultural products, feasibility studies and business plans, training and technical assistance, and community economic development projects

requirements_list: Agricultural or resource-based industry enterprise
Small and emerging businesses generally employ 50 or fewer new employees and have less than $1,000,000 in projected annual gross revenues
For certain programs: commercial lender participation required

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Washington County Department of Business and Economic Development at (240) 313-2280 or kkeadle@washco-md.net for information on specific agricultural assistance programs available. Washington County serves as a resource and coordinator for multiple MARBIDCO, USDA, and state-administered programs. Applicants should contact the program administrator for each specific program they are interested in, as application processes vary. The Tri-County Council for Western Maryland (www.tccwmd.org) also provides information on funding and grant opportunities for Washington County businesses.

structured_extraction.program_description: Encourages landowners to voluntarily enter into an Agricultural Land Preservation District in which the land will not be developed for a period of ten years. Participants receive protection from nuisance complaints through the Right to Farm Ordinance, become eligible to sell Development Rights Easements through MALPF, and receive a property tax credit.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners receive property tax credits for farmland, farm buildings, and partial tax credit for the home. The credit amount is 100% of County Real Property Tax levied on agricultural land, woodlands, and agricultural structures (excluding residential dwellings), and 50% of the County Real Property Tax on residential dwellings and one acre surrounding them, not to exceed 50% of the tax on $150,000 of assessed fair market value. The landowner receives protection from nuisance complaints through the Right to Farm Ordinance, becomes eligible to sell agricultural preservation easements to the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF), and retains eligibility for family, owner's, or child's lot releases from the district agreement. The district agreement runs with the land for a minimum of ten years from the date of recording, even if the property is sold or transferred during that period. Tax credits are not cumulative and cannot exceed 100% of total County Real Property Tax for the property.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural landowners in Washington County, Maryland seeking to preserve agricultural land and receive property tax credits
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Land preservation through voluntary 10-year development restrictions. The land must be kept in agricultural use and may not be subdivided or developed for industrial, commercial, or residential purposes (except limited personal eligibility options). Property tax credits apply to farmland, farm buildings, and a partial credit for the home.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland. Land must be outside water and sewer service areas and outside of growth areas.
requirements_list: Landowner must voluntarily enter into the district program
Land must not be developed for a period of ten years
Property must be used for commercial agricultural production
Minimum 50 acres standalone or 20 acres if contiguous to other districts
Minimum 50% of soil classes I, II, and III
Must be outside water and sewer service areas
Must be outside of growth areas
Land may not be developed or subdivided for industrial, commercial, or residential use except for certain personal eligibility options
No subdivision or division of land without County written approval
No non-agricultural buildings or structures except as approved by County

Soil erosion and water quality practices contained within a soil conservation plan approved by the local soil conservation district must be implemented and completely installed within 10 years of the district establishment date

Property owners must accept agricultural practices and operations including noise, odors, dust, machinery operation, storage and disposal of manure, and application of fertilizers, soil amendments, herbicides, and pesticides
Agreement must be notarized and recorded in County Land Records
Applies to all current titled landowners at time of execution
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Contact the Washington County Planning Department's Agricultural Land Preservation personnel. 2. Complete the Agricultural District Intake Form with property information including acreage, location, deed names, and farming operation details. 3. Submit application for designation as an Agricultural Preservation District. 4. County reviews property for eligibility (acreage, soil composition, location relative to service areas). 5. Upon approval, execute the notarized Agricultural Preservation District Agreement between the Board of County Commissioners and the landowner(s). All titled landowners must sign or provide a notarized resolution if the property is owned by a business entity. 6. Agreement is recorded in Washington County Land Records, establishing the 10-year restriction and tax credit eligibility. 7. After establishment, landowners may apply to MALPF to sell an agricultural preservation easement. 8. After 10 years, landowners may request termination by submitting a Release and Termination document.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides incentives and financial programs for agricultural businesses in Washington County, including loan programs through MARBIDCO, grant programs, farmland acquisition assistance, food access programs, and access to federal funding opportunities for farm acquisition, equipment, working capital, value-added processing, market development, and renewable energy.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Multiple programs available including: MARBIDCO loans (Maryland Resource-Based Industry Financing Fund: 2.25% for land/equipment up to $250,000-$750,000; Rural Business Equipment Fund: 5.25% up to $100,000; Vineyard/Hops/Orchard Planting Fund: 4.50% up to $100,000; Forestry Equipment Fund: 4.75% up to $150,000; Rural Business Energy Efficiency Improvement Loans: 4.50% for $2,500-$30,000); Grant programs including Maryland Urban Agriculture Commercial Lending Incentive Grant (up to $10,000), Maryland Value Added Producer Grants ($2,500-$10,000), and USDA grants (FMPP $50,000-$500,000, LFPP $25,000-$500,000, RBDG $10,000-$500,000, VAPG $75,000-$250,000); Farmland acquisition programs for beginning farmers; food access programs providing dollar-for-dollar matches for SNAP/EBT purchases; youth apprenticeship programs; and federal programs for renewable energy, water quality conservation, and market development.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Varies by program; USDA Community Food Projects deadline in June; MVAPG offered once per year; program-specific deadlines apply
structured_extraction.contact_name: Washington County Department of Business Development
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural producers, farmers, beginning farmers, forest products businesses, food and fiber processors, rural businesses, agricultural cooperatives, urban farmers, seafood and livestock processors, timber processors, rural nonprofits, students in career pathways, and entities in Washington County and rural Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Land acquisition, equipment purchases, working capital, capital assets with 7+ year useful life, facility construction, energy efficiency improvements, renewable energy systems, agricultural conservation easements, farm operations and investments, value-added processing and marketing, direct-to-consumer market development, business planning and feasibility studies, market research, training and technical assistance, inventory, marketing and advertising, and water quality conservation measures
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County and rural areas of Maryland (rural area defined as territory not within 50,000+ population city boundaries and immediately adjacent urbanized areas)
requirements_list: Eligibility varies by specific program
Crop producer, agricultural cooperative, seafood or livestock processor, or timber products processor for some programs
Minimum 2 years in business for certain programs (e.g., MVAPG-CAO)
Hemp fiber processors eligible if in business in Maryland on/before June 30, 2020
Value-added product requirement for value-added producer programs
Matching funds required for grant programs (typically 15-100% of grant amount; USDA programs typically 25% match, CFP requires 100% match)
Third-party energy audit recommendation required for energy efficiency loans
Commercial lender participation required for MUACLIG
Beginning farmer status required for farmland acquisition programs
Small acreage program targets 10-49 acre farms
Small and emerging businesses: 50 or fewer new employees and under $1,000,000 projected annual gross revenues
Minimum loan amounts apply for some MARBIDCO programs (e.g., $15,000 for Rural Business Equipment and Working Capital Loan Fund)
FMPP/LFPP projects must develop direct producer-to-consumer or intermediary local/regional food business markets
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Programs administered through Washington County Department of Business Development and MARBIDCO. Applicants should contact the department or specific program administrators. For MARBIDCO programs, applications submitted to MARBIDCO office or county agricultural land preservation program office. USDA programs require applications through respective federal agencies (USDA AMS, USDA Rural Development, NIFA). Matching funds documentation required for grant programs. USDA VAPG applicants must receive federal award before MARBIDCO matching funds distributed. Verification of matching funds required for all applicable programs. Contact Tri-County Council for Western Maryland (www.tccwmd.org) for additional funding opportunities and guidance.

structured_extraction.program_description: Federally funded program that provides grants to eligible entities for projects related to economic opportunities, workforce development, critical infrastructure, natural and cultural assets, and leadership and community capacity building in Appalachia.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to eligible entities for projects addressing economic development, workforce education and skills, critical infrastructure (broadband, transportation, water/wastewater systems), and community capacity building. Projects require a 50% match, and matching funds must be identified and committed at time of application. Applicants must submit the Preliminary Project Description (PPD), ARC Project Budget and Funding Sources Worksheet, and supporting documentation demonstrating organizational capacity and measurable outcomes aligned with ARC's five strategic investment goals and Maryland's state objectives and strategies.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY27 Project Submission is April 3, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible entities in Washington County seeking to advance community and economic development
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects related to economic opportunities and entrepreneurial development; workforce education, skills, and health; critical infrastructure including broadband, transportation, and water/wastewater systems; natural and cultural heritage asset development; and leadership and community capacity building. Priority areas include technology development, broadband, education and workforce development, tourism, energy, recovery ecosystems, and traditional infrastructure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland, located in Appalachia
requirements_list: Project must relate to one of ARC's five strategic investment goals (Building Appalachian Businesses, Building Appalachia's Workforce Ecosystem, Building Appalachia's Infrastructure, Building Regional Culture and Tourism, or Building Community Leaders and Capacity)
Project must be aligned with Maryland's State Objectives and Strategies for 2024-2028
50% match required; matching funds must be identified, committed, and documented with commitment letters at time of application
Projects must demonstrate measurable, quantifiable outputs and outcomes with defined achievement timeframes
Submission of Preliminary Project Description (PPD) and ARC Project Budget and Funding Sources Worksheet with supporting documentation
Organizational capacity documentation describing ability to administer federal grants and recent awards
Project should reference any plans or economic documents showing consistency with overall economic development strategy
Applicants should identify minimum ARC funding amount needed for project viability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit Preliminary Project Description (PPD), ARC Project Budget and Funding Sources Worksheet, and supporting documentation to the Office of Grant Management by April 3, 2026. Projects are reviewed and ranked by Washington County Commissioners, then submitted to Tri-County Council for Western Maryland for regional ranking. Top-ranking projects receive an invitation in early Fall to submit a formal grant application to the Appalachian Regional Commission, due by November 15. The review committee may reduce funding requests to allow maximum number of Washington County projects to be funded.

Nonprofit organizations are exempt from permit fees; other organizations may be charged an annual fee not exceeding $5,000.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Receipts from bingo must be used for charitable purposes as approved by the county commissioners. Bingo cannot be conducted for profit.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: Financial support provided to charitable organizations within Washington County that provide services which improve the community and quality of life for Washington County citizens. The program implements a prioritized approach to funding local non-profits based on addressing specific community needs, with emphasis on efficient use of funds and achieving results-based programmatic outcomes. Priority service areas for FY 2027 include: Families and Children ($494,400), Domestic Violence ($386,400), Arts & Cultural ($135,600), Seniors ($136,800), Recreation ($33,600), and Other ($13,200), totaling $1,200,000 in available funding.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grant allocations determined by the Board of County Commissioners during the budgeting process. For FY 2027, $1,200,000 is available with allocations to six priority service areas. Grant awards are disbursed in four quarterly installments (25% each quarter) beginning July 2026. All grant funds must be expended between July 1, 2026, and June 30, 2027, and cannot be carried forward to the next fiscal year. Organizations on the Recognized Non-Profit List (Section 1-108 of the Code of Public Local Laws) are eligible to apply. Administrative costs may not exceed 15% of the total amount requested. Grant reports are no longer required at time of application, but organizations funded in FY26 must submit a complete grant report and supporting expenditure documents by June 30, 2026.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Tuesday, January 6, 2026, by 3:00pm for FY 2027 funding cycle
structured_extraction.contact_name: Maria Kramer (Director, Office of Grant Management) / Carsten Ahrens (Senior Grant Manager)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Recognized non-profit charitable organizations operating in Washington County that are listed on the Board of County Commissioners Recognized Non-Profit List (Section 1-108 of the Code of Public Local Laws). structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services that improve the community and quality of life for Washington County citizens. Funding may be used for operating expenses, capital expenses, or projects. Applications must target at least one of the six prioritized service areas: Families and Children, Domestic Violence, Arts & Cultural, Seniors, Recreation, or Other. All funds must be expended within one year.

requirements_list: Organization must be included on the Board of County Commissioners Recognized Non-Profit List (Section 1-108 of the Code of Public Local Laws)
Organization must be a charitable non-profit organization with IRS 501(c)(3) designation with 'Valid' status
Organization must be incorporated as a business entity with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) and be 'In Good Standing' at the time of application submission
Organization must have an office in and provide services within Washington County
Organization must provide services that improve community and quality of life
Organization must not have unpaid liens, judgments, or past due obligations to Washington County Treasurer or any other government entity
Application must be submitted during the published application window and by the established deadline
Administrative costs may not exceed 15% of total amount requested

Organization must submit completed application forms signed by authorized representative, budget narrative worksheets (using the FY27 budget spreadsheet), and all required documentation by the deadline
Organization must be compliant with all previous County funding obligations and grant reporting requirements
Organization must submit most recent certified audit or detailed financial statement
Application must not be requesting funds for an endowment or to benefit an individual
Organization must target at least one of the six prioritized service areas: Families and Children, Domestic Violence, Arts & Cultural, Seniors, Recreation, or Other
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Check if your organization is on the Recognized Non-Profit List (Section 1-108). 2. Review the Application Guidelines and Requirements for FY 2027 and all supporting materials available on the OGM website starting December 1, 2025. 3. Complete all required application sections: Overview, Statement of Need (1 page max), Past Performance (1 page max), Organizational Capacity and Staffing Plan (2 pages max), Program Plan (4 pages max), Collaborations/Partnerships/Coordination of Services (1 page max), and Budget Spreadsheet using the FY27 Excel template. 4. Gather required attachments: IRS 501(c)(3) determination letter, SDAT proof of good standing, most recent audit or financial statement, IRS Form 990, letters of support, and W-9 form (if applicable). 5. Prepare six hard paper copies (unsecured with staples, clips, or rubber bands) and one electronic PDF copy. 6. Submit both paper and electronic copies by January 6, 2026, at 3:00 PM. Paper copies to: Washington County Office of Grant Management, 100 W. Washington Street, Room 1601, Hagerstown, MD 21740, Attn: Julie Mackereth, Senior Office Associate. Electronic copy to: cahrens@washco-md.net (cc: jmackereth@washco-md.net). 7. Applications are accepted as submitted and will not be checked by OGM staff for accuracy or completeness. 8. Applications are reviewed and scored using a rubric with criteria: Application Submission (10 points), Statement of Need (20 points), Past Performance (5 points), Organizational Capacity and Staffing (10 points), Program Plan (30 points), Collaborations/Partnerships/Coordination (10 points), and Budget/Narrative (15 points). 9. Review considerations include total funding available, geographic distribution, service duplication, and previous performance. 10. Applicants will be notified of funding decisions when the County budget is approved (May-June 2026).

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides qualifying businesses with State income tax credits and local real property tax credits in return for job creation and capital investments made in designated Enterprise Zones. Approximately 5,500 acres in Washington County are within three state-designated Enterprise Zones, including the City of Hagerstown/Washington County Enterprise Zone (approximately 4,000 acres) and the Town of Hancock Enterprise Zone (1,500 acres). The State of Maryland approves each zone for a 10-year period.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two primary tax incentive programs: (1) State Income Tax Credits for job creation based on new jobs created after Enterprise Zone designation - maximum $1,000 per non-disadvantaged employee (one-time); $3,000 first year, $2,000 second year, and $1,000 third year for economically disadvantaged employees certified by Maryland Department of Labor; (2) Local Real Property Tax Credits - 80% of property taxes on increased assessment for years 1-5, declining to 70%, 60%, 50%, 40%, and 30% for years 6-10 respectively; (3) Exemption from Commercial Building Excise Tax on new construction within Enterprise Zones.
structured_extraction.program_audience: New and existing for-profit businesses located or relocating to designated Enterprise Zones in Washington County, Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credits for new jobs created and capital investments (construction, building additions, renovations) in designated Enterprise Zones. Income tax credits apply to wages paid for newly created positions. Real property tax credits apply to the increased property assessment resulting from capital improvements. Commercial building excise tax exemption applies to new construction projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Hagerstown/Washington County Enterprise Zone (approximately 4,000 acres, including Hopewell Valley Industrial Park, Washington County Business Park, CSX Valley Park, City of Hagerstown Business Park, and Central Business District in downtown Hagerstown); Town of Hancock Enterprise Zone (1,500 acres, stretching from Pennsylvania border to Potomac River, including commercial and industrial development areas and Main Street commercial frontage)
requirements_list: Businesses must have been located within Zone boundaries on designation date, relocated to Zone after designation, or started construction/expansion after designation
For income tax credits: Minimum job creation requirements - 1 new job in Central Business District or Hancock Zone; 5 new jobs outside Central Business District
For real property tax credits: Minimum capital investment - $5,000 in Central Business District or Hancock Zone; $50,000 outside Central Business District

Business types eligible: Manufacturing, warehousing, research and development, corporate/regional headquarters offices, service industries; retail/mercantile only eligible in Hancock Zone or Central Business District
New employees must work at least 35 hours per week for at least 6 consecutive months
New employees must earn at least 150% of federal minimum wage
New employees must spend at least 50% of working time in Enterprise Zone or on activities directly related to Zone business
Employee cannot be replacement hire for non-disadvantaged credit
For property tax credit: Application must be submitted before project completion and issuance of User/Occupancy Permits
For income tax credit: Application submitted after hiring new employees
Property must be certified to Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation by December 31st of year construction is completed
Excess income tax credits carry forward 5 years from date qualified employee was hired
Designation dates: Hagerstown-Washington County Enterprise Zone (December 15, 1982), Hancock Enterprise Zone (December 15, 1995)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Determine property location in a Zone by contacting Washington County Department of Business Development. 2) Verify minimum eligibility criteria for jobs or capital investment. 3) Submit Application for Maryland State Enterprise Zone Certification form to Washington County Department of Business Development. For property tax credits: submit before project completion. For income tax credits: submit after hiring new employees. 4) For income tax credits only: Submit 'New Jobs Created' form listing newly created positions (not replacements) with full-time employment (35+ hours/week) employed at least 6 months in the Zone or related activities. 5) Local Job Service Office (Maryland Department of Labor) reviews employee list and determines individual eligibility as 'disadvantaged' or 'non-disadvantaged.' 6) Washington County Department of Business Development sends approval letter or denial explanation. 7) For property tax credits: Credits automatically appear on Washington County and Town of Hancock tax bills in July; City of Hagerstown issues credit voucher. 8) For income tax credits: Claim credits using Maryland Tax Form 500Z with copy of approval letter from DBD. 9) After initial approval, company does not need to reapply for additional job credits; contact Job Service to identify 'disadvantaged' employees and claim credits.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Gaming Commission distributes funds from The Washington County Gaming Fund to eligible organizations. In 1995, the Maryland General Assembly passed legislation enabling tip jar gaming in Washington County. Monies collected from tip jars are deposited into a dedicated Gaming Fund account to be allocated to local charities. By statute, 50% of the Gaming Funds are allocated to the Washington County Volunteer Fire & Rescue Association, with the remaining allocated to local charitable organizations making application annually to the Gaming Commission. The Commission has the sole authority to review applications and distribute funds in accordance with State Statute and County Regulations.

Any funds not spent within the performance period must be returned to the fund.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are released each April. Completed applications must be submitted electronically via email to jmackereth@washco-md.net and copied to slapole@washco-md.net no later than 3:00 p.m. on the deadline date (typically May 6). Required documentation includes: signed Request for Funding application, most recent annual financial statement, Gaming Fund Grant Report (if applicable), W-9 form, Washington County vendor forms, and supporting documentation. Applications are reviewed by the seven-member Gaming Commission. A Public Funding Hearing is held (typically in June), where applicants may appear to answer questions and clarify issues. Appearance is encouraged but not required. Organizations may schedule hearing times with the Office of Grant Management. Funding awards are announced during the Board of County Commissioners meeting in August, with award letters sent out and funds disbursed several weeks after announcement.

structured_extraction.program_description: Tax credit program for owners of historic properties in Washington County who undertake qualified rehabilitation and preservation work on their historic structures. The program provides stackable tax credits at the local level (25% County credit), with the possibility of combining with State (20%) and Federal (20%) credits, plus an additional 5% credit for eligible exterior work on new construction attached to historic structures.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Washington County offers a 25% county property tax credit for qualified rehabilitation, restoration, or preservation work on historic structures that minimizes destruction of historic fabric and maintains sympathetic design. An additional 5% credit is available for eligible exterior work on new construction attached to existing historic structures. Any unused credit carries over for up to 5 years or until fully expended. Credits are stackable with State (20%) and Federal (20%) tax credits, potentially providing up to 70% in combined tax credits.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential or commercial property owners with property documented on the Maryland Inventory of Historic Properties located in qualifying geographic areas in Washington County, Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Qualified rehabilitation, restoration, or preservation work on historic structures including roof repair/replacement, chimney repair/replacement, window restoration, new storm doors/windows, masonry re-pointing, structural repairs, architectural/engineering/consulting fees, and tool/equipment rental
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Structures must be located within the Antietam Overlay (AO1 or AO2) district, or be a contributing structure to a surveyed and adopted Historic Rural Village (Antietam, Cavetown, Fairplay, Highfield, Leitersburg, Pen Mar, Ringgold, Rohrersville, Sandy Hook, or Tilghmanton). Properties with Historic Preservation (HP) Overlay zoning qualify. Contributing structures located within Towns listed on the National Register of Historic Places with appropriate zoning and design guidelines also qualify. Structures must be on the Maryland Inventory of Historic Properties.
requirements_list: Property must be documented on the Maryland Inventory of Historic Properties
Property must be located in a qualifying geographic area (Antietam Overlay AO1/AO2, Historic Rural Village, HP Overlay zone, or eligible municipality)
Rehabilitation work must minimize destruction of historic fabric and maintain thoughtful and sympathetic design
Work must be consistent with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation and Washington County Design Guidelines for Historic Structures
Application must be submitted BEFORE work begins
Owner must maintain itemized expense records with invoices/receipts and proof of payment
Completed projects may be inspected by the Historic District Commission
For properties under Maryland Historical Trust Easement, copy of easement document must be included
Property owner must comply with all Federal, State, and local laws and permitting requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application process consists of three parts: Part I (Evaluation of Significance) - Determine if the structure qualifies for the tax credit by verifying location in a qualifying area and documenting historic characteristics (unless property has HP Overlay); Part II (Description of Rehabilitation) - Describe proposed work and obtain approval from the Historic District Commission BEFORE work begins; Part III (Request for Certification of Completed Work) - Submit completed project documentation after work is finished. Applicants must submit all parts with required supporting documentation (photos, significance justification, architectural plans, itemized expenses with receipts). Applications may be submitted to the Washington County Historic District Commission via mail (747 Northern Avenue, Hagerstown, MD 21742) or email (askplanning@washco-md.net). Equivalent applications (such as State or Federal credit applications) may be accepted. The Historic District Commission reviews each application for compliance with ordinance and applicable standards. Upon approval, the credit amount is forwarded to the Treasurer's Office for property bill updates.

Grant applications requesting $25,000 or less are reviewed and approved by the Office of Grant Management (OGM) with the concurrence of the County Administrator. Grant applications requesting more than $25,000 are reviewed by the OGM and County Administrator, with final approval made by the Board of County Commissioners. Grants are paid to the applicant, not to vendors. Any changes exceeding 10% of approved line items must have OGM approval. Unused funds must be returned to the County within 30 days of project completion.

The application can be accessed from the County's website under the Office of Grant Management, submitted by email, or printed and mailed in. Upon receipt, the Office of Grant Management (OGM) will: (1) Determine if the applicant is qualified to receive funding; (2) Determine if the event or project is qualified to receive funding; (3) Determine if the request meets the funding goals of the County Commissioners and the purpose of Hotel Rental Tax Funding; (4) For requests of $25,000 and below, approve or deny the request with the concurrence of the County Administrator; (5) For requests exceeding $25,000, process the application and forward to the County Administrator for review, and upon favorable review the County Commissioners will hear the request and may take action; (6) Notify the applicant in writing of approval or denial. All organizations receiving grant funding must complete a Hotel Rental Tax Grant Report and submit it with supporting documentation (budget itemizations and/or receipts) within 60 days of project completion. Applications must be saved to your computer before completion to avoid data loss.

The program has protected 1,507 acres with over $6.1 million invested in Washington County.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides protections for farmers against nuisance complaints in Washington County. Adopted by the Board of County Commissioners in October 2003. The ordinance preserves, protects, enhances and encourages Agricultural Operations and the development and improvement of Agricultural Land for the production of food and other agricultural products. It clarifies and limits the circumstances under which Agricultural Operations may be deemed to constitute a nuisance, trespass or other interference with the reasonable use and enjoyment of land, including but not limited to smoke, odors, flies, dust, noise, chemicals, or vibration.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The ordinance provides legal protections for farmers against nuisance complaints in Washington County, enabling agricultural operations to continue without interference from neighboring property owners. Agricultural Operations conducted on Agricultural Land in accordance with Generally Accepted Agricultural Management Practices are protected from private actions alleging interference with use or enjoyment of property. The ordinance establishes the Washington County Agricultural Reconciliation Board (WCARB) to arbitrate and mediate disputes and determine whether Agricultural Operations are conducted consistently with Generally Accepted Agricultural Management Practices. The WCARB is composed of five members appointed by the Board of County Commissioners: one representative from the Washington County Farm Bureau, one from Maryland Cooperative Extension Agricultural Science faculty, and three citizens at large (including one attorney). Disputes must be submitted to the WCARB within 30 days of the occurrence. The WCARB has 45 days to hold a hearing and 20 days to render a written decision. Decisions are binding on the parties but may be appealed to Circuit Court within 30 days for trial de novo.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers and agricultural operators in Washington County; property owners adjacent to or near Agricultural Operations
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The ordinance does not provide financial assistance. It provides legal protections for agricultural operations conducted in accordance with Generally Accepted Agricultural Management Practices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland
requirements_list: Agricultural Operation must be conducted on Agricultural Land (land in an Agricultural zoning district, carried on tax rolls as agricultural, or used as an Agricultural Operation continuously for at least one year)
Agricultural Operation must be conducted in accordance with Generally Accepted Agricultural Management Practices
Private action alleging nuisance cannot be maintained unless plaintiff has sought and obtained a final decision from the Agricultural Reconciliation Board
Disputes must be submitted to WCARB within 30 days of the date of occurrence or date party became aware of the occurrence
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For disputes: Parties should submit the controversy to the Washington County Agricultural Reconciliation Board (WCARB) in writing through the Washington County Planning Department within 30 days of the date of the occurrence giving rise to the controversy. The WCARB will conduct informal proceedings and hold a hearing within 45 days of receiving the written request. The WCARB will render a written decision within 20 days of the hearing. Decisions are binding but may be appealed to Circuit Court for Washington County within 30 days for trial de novo. For nuisance complaints affecting public health: Contact the Washington County Health Department.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides gap financing to small businesses seeking to locate or expand in Garrett, Allegany, and Washington counties. The program partners with banks and other lenders to fund the part of a project that a primary lender cannot cover, with the main goal of creating or retaining jobs in the region.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A pool of money granted by federal and state entities for making loans to create and save jobs. The program provides loans from $10,000 to $400,000 as gap financing, meaning a bank or other private lender must fund at least 50% of the project. Interest rates connect to the prime interest rate. Loan terms are up to 5 years for working capital and up to 15 years for fixed assets like real estate.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program is for businesses, including corporations, partnerships, and sole proprietorships. The business must be in Allegany, Garrett, or Washington County. It is for businesses that cannot get all their needed funding from traditional lenders.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: You can use funds for business acquisition and expansion. You can also use them for land and building costs, buying machinery and equipment, start-up costs, and working capital.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Garrett, Allegany, and Washington counties in Maryland's Appalachian region
requirements_list: A business plan is required.
A private lender must fund at least 50% of the total project cost.
Applicant must provide a denial letter from the primary lender for 100% of the project, along with their approval to finance a majority of the project.
One job must be created or retained for every $30,000 borrowed within the first 36 months of the loan.
A minimum equity injection of 10% is generally required for start-up businesses.
Personal guaranties of the debt are required from all owners with 20% or greater interest.
Applicants must provide a completed personal financial statement and 3 years of both business and personal tax returns.
A $250 non-refundable application fee is required.
Approved borrowers are assessed a 1.5% loan origination fee at closing.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, create a business plan and determine your funding needs. Second, apply for a loan from a private bank to determine how much they will finance. Third, complete the program's application form and submit it with the required documents and application fee.

structured_extraction.program_name: Job Creation and Capital Investment Real Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides up to a fifteen-year tax credit on the County portion of real estate taxes for qualified businesses that either expand or locate and meet specific investment and job creation thresholds. The program was enacted by the Washington County Board of County Commissioners to attract and retain businesses that provide well-paying jobs and make capital investments in the community. The program is part of Washington County's broader strategy to support business growth, job creation, and infrastructure investment.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County Department of Business Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Real property tax credits on the County portion of real estate taxes for the increased assessed property value offered through three tiers: TIER ONE provides 3 years of credits (55%, 40%, 25%) for 1,500 sq. ft. expansion and 5 new full-time employees within 12 months; TIER TWO provides 6 years of credits (55%, 55%, 40%, 40%, 25%, 25%) for 2,500 sq. ft. expansion and 25 new full-time employees within 24 months; TIER THREE provides 15 years of credits (75% for first five years, then reduced by 5% annually until reaching 25%) for $20M investment, 200 new full-time employees within 24 months with 80% paid at 200% of Maryland State minimum wage. Credits apply to the County portion of real estate taxes for newly constructed, renovated, expanded, or previously unoccupied properties that are owned or leased. Lessors must reduce tenant tax liability by the credit amount. Businesses in Enterprise Zones are not eligible and must apply under the Enterprise Zone Program.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annual Employment and Certification Report due by February 1
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses expanding operations or relocating to Washington County that can meet investment and job creation requirements
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Real property tax credits for qualified business expansion, renovation, construction, or relocation in Washington County
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland. Businesses in Enterprise Zones are not eligible for this program and must apply under the Enterprise Zone Program.
requirements_list: Apply before occupying space or hiring employees
Submit letter of intent and official application before completing construction
Eligible properties must be newly constructed, renovated, expanded, or previously unoccupied and can be owned or leased
TIER ONE: Minimum 1,500 sq. ft. expansion and 5 new full-time employees within 12 months
TIER TWO: Minimum 2,500 sq. ft. expansion and 25 new full-time employees within 24 months
TIER THREE: Minimum $20M capital investment, 200 new full-time employees within 24 months, with 80% of new employees paid at 200% of Maryland State minimum wage
Businesses must continue to meet all applicable program requirements for each year they receive the tax credit

Submit Annual Employment and Certification Report by February 1 each year including employee names, Social Security numbers, home city/state, employment dates, annual salary, hours worked, and benefits information
Notify DBED upon construction completion with square footage documentation
Failure to meet requirements results in forfeiture of credit for that year and repayment obligation
Failure to apply before hiring or occupying new premises may result in ineligibility
Businesses cannot receive another tax credit or exemption for the same property in the same taxable year under any other state or county law
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit letter of intent and completed application before occupying space or hiring employees, including company information, Federal Employer Identification Number, NAICS code, contact details, property information, land owner information, project details (square footage, description, location), and capital expenditure information. 2. Submit official application and employee certification report before completing construction. 3. Upon construction completion, notify Washington County DBED and provide square footage documentation. 4. Create required full-time employees within the specified timeframe (12 months for TIER 1, 24 months for TIERs 2 and 3). 5. Receive certification from Washington County Department of Business and Economic Development (DBED). 6. Submit Annual Employment and Certification Report by February 1 each year, which includes employee details (first initial and last name, last four digits of Social Security Number or unique ID, home city and state, start and end dates of employment), salary information, hours worked, and benefits information. 7. If business fails to meet requirements in any taxable year, the credit is forfeited and becomes due and repayable to the County. Businesses are strongly encouraged to engage with DBED early in their planning process.
